MAR.short: Morocco's 2018 law on the right of access to information is in force and its commission is at work; its decisions are not known.
MAR.summary:
Law in force. Morocco's law is Law no. 31-13 on the right of access to information, promulgated on 22 February 2018 and published on 3 May 2018, in force one year after publication. The Ministry of Justice says requests and complaints are filed and handled under it.

Law put to work and applied. The law's oversight body is set up. The Commission on the Right of Access to Information, led by its president, signed a partnership agreement with the Minister of Justice on 31 March 2026, and it runs the national portal through which requests are made. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

MDG.short: Madagascar's access to public information bill has been before the National Assembly since 2026 and was left off its August session; no law exists.
MDG.summary:
Law in force. Madagascar has a bill and no law. A decree of the Prime Minister presented bill no. 017/2025 on access to information of a public nature, in 88 articles, after the Council of Ministers deliberated it on 3 December 2025. Deputies debated it in committee from 8 May 2026, and it was left off the agenda of the extraordinary session opened on 25 August 2026.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the draft, bill no. 017/2025. A bill makes no rules and sets up no oversight body until it is passed, promulgated and in force. Once it is, what would put it to work is a decree or regulation made under it, or an information commission or commissioner appointed, and what would show it applied is a decision or penalty on a request for information, or published figures of requests.

Not held. No source held says an access to information law is in force.

MLI.short: Mali has no single access to information law; a 2026 study finds the right spread across several laws, one of 1998.
MLI.summary:
Law in force. Mali has no single access to information law. A study published in April 2026 finds the legal framework for the right spread across several laws, among them Law no. 98-012 on relations between the administration and its users, and calls for a specific law. The existing laws are counted here for the part that gives the right; the study names no draft of a single law.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the law itself, the laws the 2026 study describes. What would put it to work is a decree, regulation or order made under it, an information commission or commissioner appointed, or an existing body such as an ombudsman taking up its oversight. What would show it applied is a decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the body that oversees it. Neither is recorded for Mali.

Not held. No source held names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's Right to Information Law of 2014 is in force; rules made under it and an oversight body are not known.
MOZ.summary:
Law in force. Mozambique's law is Law no. 34/2014 of 31 December 2014, the Right to Information Law, passed by the Assembly of the Republic to set how the right to information is exercised. It applies to the bodies of the State and to the public administration.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the law itself, Law no. 34/2014. What would put it to work is a decree, regulation or order made under it, an information commission or commissioner appointed, or an existing body such as an ombudsman taking up its oversight. What would show it applied is a decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the body that oversees it. Neither is recorded for Mozambique.

Not held. No source held names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up.

MRT.short: Mauritania's government bill on access to public information has been under discussion since April 2026; it has not reached parliament.
MRT.summary:
Law in force. Mauritania has a bill and no law. Reporters Without Borders reported on 23 June 2026 that a bill drafted by the government on access to and use of public information had been under discussion since April 2026 and had yet to go through parliament. No law is in force.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the draft, the government bill under discussion since April 2026. A bill makes no rules and sets up no oversight body until it is passed, promulgated and in force. Once it is, what would put it to work is a decree or regulation made under it, or an information commission or commissioner appointed, and what would show it applied is a decision or penalty on a request for information, or published figures of requests.

Not held. No source held says an access to information law is in force.

MUS.short: Mauritius had no access to information law as of February 2026, only promises of one; no bill is known.
MUS.summary:
Law in force. A Defi Media blog of 14 February 2026 says successive Mauritian political parties have promised Freedom of Information and failed to deliver. It says Senior Counsel Rama Valayden urges the government to introduce it, and names no law or bill; his 2022 draft is a constitutional amendment to section 12, put forward by Senior Counsel Valayden himself. The blog is headed with his call for action on Freedom of Information and the proposed constitutional change.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the same February 2026 blog, which describes a promise not yet delivered by any of the successive political parties, and the 2022 draft it mentions amends section 12 of the constitution. Nothing held shows a rule made, an oversight body set up or a request decided under an access law.

Not held. Nothing held shows an access to information bill or draft law before the government or parliament.

MWI.short: Malawi's Access to Information Act has run since 2020; its oversight body reported over 36,000 requests handled in the year to March 2025.
MWI.summary:
Law in force. Malawi's law is the Access to Information Act, 2016, assented to on 10 February 2017 and published in the Gazette on 16 February 2017. It became operational on 30 September 2020, and it gives a right to information held by public bodies and by the private bodies it names.

Law put to work and applied. The Malawi Human Rights Commission, which the Act makes its oversight body, presented a report on carrying the Act out on 10 October 2025. The report says that from April 2024 to March 2025 information holders handled over 36,000 requests and rejected 11. The Commission has also used the Act on a private company: it issued a notice to Mota-Engil to assess whether the company could comply, a step that reached the High Court on 6 March 2026.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2022 Access to Information Act has regulations of December 2024 for choosing its commissioner; whether the Act has started is not known.
NAM.summary:
Law in force. Namibia's law is the Access to Information Act, 2022 (Act No. 8 of 2022), published in the Government Gazette on 28 December 2022. It gives a right of access to information held by public and private bodies and starts on a date the Minister sets; that date is not recorded.

Law put to work and applied. Regulations made under the Act were gazetted on 9 December 2024, setting the terms of the selection committee and the process for appointing the Information Commissioner. Regulations made in the last three years are counted as the law applied. The appointment of a commissioner, a decision on a request and published figures of requests are not recorded, so what is held shows the Act being prepared for use and not yet used.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

NER.short: Niger's 2011 ordinance on access to public information is in force and was cited by a minister in 2025; rules under it are not known.
NER.summary:
Law in force. Niger's law is Ordinance no. 2011-22 of 23 February 2011 on the charter of access to public information and administrative documents, an ordinance with the force of law that gives any person a right to ask public bodies for information. The Minister of Communication cited it on 22 October 2025 as standing.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the law itself, Ordinance no. 2011-22. What would put it to work is a decree, regulation or order made under it, an information commission or commissioner appointed, or an existing body such as an ombudsman taking up its oversight. What would show it applied is a decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the body that oversees it. Neither is recorded for Niger.

Not held. No source held names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up.

NGA.short: Nigeria's 2011 Freedom of Information Act is in force and the Federal High Court ordered disclosure under it in 2025 and 2026.
NGA.summary:
Law in force. Nigeria's law is the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, assented to on 28 May 2011, which gives any person a right to request information held by public institutions. The Federal High Court treats it as taking precedence over the Petroleum Industry Act where the two conflict.

Law put to work and applied. The courts enforce the Act. On 13 October 2025 the Federal High Court in Abuja held the national oil company a public institution under the Act and ordered it to supply information requested on a $3 billion loan. On 24 February 2026 the Federal High Court in Lagos ruled that the Nigeria Shippers Council had breached the Act over a journalist's request of 2020, and ordered disclosure or reasons. The Act has no information commission; rules made under it are not recorded.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2013 law on access to information is in force; rules made under it and an oversight body are not known.
RWA.summary:
Law in force. Rwanda's law is Law no. 04/2013 of 8 February 2013 relating to access to information, published on 11 March 2013. It is the country's access to information law and has stood since 2013, with no repeal or replacement recorded.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the law itself, Law no. 04/2013. What would put it to work is a decree, regulation or order made under it, an information commission or commissioner appointed, or an existing body such as an ombudsman taking up its oversight. What would show it applied is a decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the body that oversees it. Neither is recorded for Rwanda.

Not held. No source held names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up.

SDN.short: Sudan's Right to Access Information Law of 2015 is on the books; nothing since 2016 says how it stands or is used.
SDN.summary:
Law in force. Sudan's law is the Right to Access Information Law of 2015, ratified by the National Assembly on 27 January 2015 and signed by the President on 22 February 2015, in effect from signing. The National Information Center listed it in 2016 among the laws governing the sector.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the law itself, the Right to Access Information Law of 2015. What would put it to work is a decree, regulation or order made under it, an information commission or commissioner appointed, or an existing body such as an ombudsman taking up its oversight. What would show it applied is a decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the body that oversees it. Neither is recorded for Sudan.

Not held. No source held names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up.

SEN.short: Senegal's access to information law was promulgated in September 2025 and its commission created; decisions on requests are not known.
SEN.summary:
Law in force. Senegal's law is Law no. 2025-15 on access to information, adopted by the National Assembly on 26 August 2025, promulgated on 4 September 2025 and published on 25 September 2025. It is the first law to set how the right of access is exercised.

Law put to work and applied. The law's oversight body has been created. The Open Government Partnership's review of May 2026 reports that Senegal created the Commission nationale d'accès à l'information under the law, and that the law carries sanctions for bodies that do not comply. The commission's members being named is not recorded. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's 2013 Right to Access Information Act is in force with a working commission; a bill to replace it went to Cabinet in 2026.
SLE.summary:
Law in force. Sierra Leone's law is the Right to Access Information Act, 2013, signed by the President on 31 October 2013. A replacement is being written: a Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill was validated on 7 November 2025, and Cabinet approved repealing the 2013 Act and enacting the new one, announced on 21 April 2026.

Law put to work and applied. The Act's oversight body is long set up. The Right to Access Information Commission presented its sixth annual report to the Minister of Information and Civic Education on 17 November 2025, and it was already at work in January 2017. The figures in the report are not held. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

SOM.short: Somalia's cabinet approved an access to information bill in 2024; in September 2025 it still awaited the Lower House.
SOM.summary:
Law in force. Somalia has a bill and no law. The Council of Ministers approved the Official Information Bill in March 2024 and sent it to the House of the People. A Ministry of Information official said on 28 September 2025 that the Cabinet had passed the access to information law and that it awaited presentation to the Lower House.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the draft, the bill awaiting the Lower House. A bill makes no rules and sets up no oversight body until it is passed, promulgated and in force. Once it is, what would put it to work is a decree or regulation made under it, or an information commission or commissioner appointed, and what would show it applied is a decision or penalty on a request for information, or published figures of requests.

Not held. No source held says an access to information law is in force.

SSD.short: South Sudan has an Access to Information Commission with a budget line; the law is not named in what is held, nor any decision.
SSD.summary:
Law in force. South Sudan's access to information law is not itself named in what is recorded; its commission is. The Minister of Information's paper of 6 September 2023 lists the Information Commission among six bodies under the ministry, and a commission set up shows a law in force behind it.

Law put to work and applied. The oversight body exists and is funded through the budget. The budget performance report for 2024/25 lists the Access for Information Commission among the agencies with an allocation. On 4 September 2025 the Ministry of Information said it had estimated a budget for the Commission's operations and described it as facing operating challenges. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

STP.short: Sao Tome and Principe had a draft access law before the National Assembly in 2018, still not adopted in 2021; later status is not known.
STP.summary:
Law in force. Civil society organisations (CIP-STP, FONG-STP, PDHEG and Wêbeto) submitted a draft Lei de Acesso aos Documentos e Informações Administrativas to the President of the National Assembly in 2018. It was written by a national consultant under the Pro PALOP project, and the 2018 submission is reported by STP Digital. In November 2021 those organisations were still calling for the draft to be adopted during the Quinzena da Cidadania, and STP Digital reported on 1 December 2021 that it was not yet adopted.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the same STP Digital report, which concerns a draft only: the calls made during the Quinzena da Cidadania, 15 to 30 November 2021. Nothing held shows a rule made, an oversight body set up or a request decided under an access law.

Not held. Nothing held says the draft was adopted since 2021, or that any access law is in force or applied.

SWZ.short: Nothing held says whether Eswatini has an access to information law or a draft of one, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not held. Nothing held names an access to information law or a draft of one, or says there is none.

SYC.short: Seychelles' 2018 Access to Information Act is in force with a commission that says its orders are ignored; no dated decision is known.
SYC.summary:
Law in force. Seychelles' law is the Access to Information Act, enacted on 20 July 2018. The Information Commission was created under it, and the Commission proposed amendments to the Act in a paper of November 2025.

Law put to work and applied. The Act's oversight body is set up. The Information Commission was created under the Act and was later named the data protection authority as well. Its paper of November 2025 says it has issued orders and decisions under the Act since 2019 and that information holders have ignored them, the Act giving no clear way to enforce them. No decision is dated, and no figures of requests are recorded. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

TCD.short: Chad had no freedom of information law in January 2023; nothing newer is held, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: Not held. No law or draft is on record, and no source dated in the last three years says the country has none.

TGO.short: Togo's 2016 law on access to public information is in force with an implementing decree of 2017; nothing done under it since is known.
TGO.summary:
Law in force. Togo's law is Law no. 2016-006 of 30 March 2016 on freedom of access to public information and documentation, adopted by the National Assembly on 10 March 2016. It guarantees citizens a right of access to information held by public bodies and has stood since 2016, with no repeal or replacement recorded.

Law put to work and applied. Rules have been made under the law. Decree no. 2017-104/PR of 10 August 2017 applies it, naming the public bodies it covers and the officials responsible. The decree is older than three years and nothing later is recorded. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 2016 access to information law is in force, but its oversight body lacked a president in late 2025 and could not meet validly.
TUN.summary:
Law in force. Tunisia's law is Organic Law no. 22 of 2016 on the right of access to information, promulgated on 24 March 2016. It gives every person a right to ask public bodies for information and took effect one year after publication.

Law put to work and applied. The law's oversight body is set up and stalled. The government told a deputy, as reported on 30 November 2025, that the access to information body, nine members elected by Parliament for six years, has been working without its president and deputy, which has blocked legally valid meetings. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 2016 Access to Information Act has been in force since July 2017; rules made under it are not known.
TZA.summary:
Law in force. Tanzania's law is the Access to Information Act, 2016, assented to on 23 September 2016, gazetted on 30 September 2016 and commenced on 1 July 2017. It gives every person a right of access to information held by public bodies.

Law put to work and applied. The nearest held fact is the law itself, the Access to Information Act of 2016. What would put it to work is a decree, regulation or order made under it, an information commission or commissioner appointed, or an existing body such as an ombudsman taking up its oversight. What would show it applied is a decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the body that oversees it. Neither is recorded for Tanzania.

Not held. No source held names rules made under the law or says its oversight body is set up.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2005 Access to Information Act is in force, and courts ruled on requests and on the Act itself in 2025 and 2026.
UGA.summary:
Law in force. Uganda's law is the Access to Information Act, 2005, assented to on 7 July 2005, which gives every citizen a right of access to the records of public bodies. The Constitutional Court ruled on it on 4 December 2025, holding its exemption for court records before a case ends unconstitutional.

Law put to work and applied. The courts decide requests under the Act. On 7 August 2026 the High Court allowed the national examinations board's appeal against a magistrate's order, made on a complaint under the Act, that had compelled release of a candidate's examination script. The judgment applies the Act's section 4 right of access. The Act has no information commission; rules made under it are not recorded.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 2000 access to information law is enforced by the Information Regulator, which ordered a mining company to disclose records in May 2026.
ZAF.summary:
Law in force. South Africa's law is the Promotion of Access to Information Act, 2000, the law under which the Information Regulator acts on complaints about refused requests. It was amended on 17 April 2025, and a parliamentary committee approved the publication of amended court rules under it in September 2026.

Law put to work and applied. The Information Regulator, established on 1 December 2016, monitors and enforces the Act alongside the data protection law. On 22 May 2026 it issued an enforcement notice under the Act directing the mining company Sibanye-Stillwater to give a complainant access to compliance reports, after a complaint lodged in September 2023. The Regulator briefed the press on its enforcement of the Act on 31 August 2026.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

ZMB.short: Zambia's 2023 Access to Information Act came into force in June 2025, with regulations and oversight guidelines issued the same year.
ZMB.summary:
Law in force. Zambia's law is the Access to Information Act, 2023 (Act No. 24 of 2023), assented to on 22 December 2023. It came into force on 25 June 2025, when the minister signed a commencement order.

Law put to work and applied. Rules followed within months. The Minister of Information and Media made the Access to Information (General) Regulations, 2025, setting request forms, fees and procedures, signed on 20 August 2025. The Human Rights Commission, which the Act names as its oversight body, issued guidelines under it on 5 December 2025. Court rules under the Act were still being finalised in July 2026. Rules made in the last three years are counted as the law applied; a decision on a request is not recorded.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's 2020 Freedom of Information Act is in force with regulations of 2021; nothing done under it since is known.
ZWE.summary:
Law in force. Zimbabwe's law is the Freedom of Information Act, 2020, published and commenced on 1 July 2020. It gives a right to ask public bodies for information and repealed the Access to Information and Protection of Privacy Act.

Law put to work and applied. Rules have been made under the Act. A joint submission to the United Nations of July 2026 says the Act was put to work through the Freedom of Information (General) Regulations, 2021, and recommends that the Act be fully carried out. The regulations are older than three years. A decision, order or penalty on a request for information, or figures of requests published by the oversight body, dated in the last three years, is not recorded.

Not held. No source held dates a decision, order or penalty on a request, published figures of requests, or a rule made under the law, in the last three years.

AGO.short: A draft AI law was out for public consultation in 2026; no rule on AI is in force.
AGO.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Angola has a draft law and no rule in force. The ministry for telecommunications and information technology lists a proposed law on artificial intelligence on its public consultation portal, which in August 2026 recorded 18 contributions from companies, 18 from specialists and five from the public. A review published in December 2025 describes the draft as a comprehensive framework for developing, supplying and using AI, built on levels of risk and reaching providers outside the country.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The draft under consultation would apply to AI across sectors and not to one sector or one use. It has not been sent to the Council of Ministers or the National Assembly in any source dated to September 2026.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

BDI.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BDI.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

BEN.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BEN.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

BFA.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

BWA.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

CAF.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

CIV.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CIV.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

CMR.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CMR.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

COD.short: No hard law on AI and no draft were named in 2024; soft law prevailed. Whether a draft exists since is not known.
COD.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. A law-faculty dean writing on droitnumerique.cd published an article on 23 August 2024 about AI policy and automated decision-making in the DR Congo. The dean says the DRC has not yet developed its hard law on AI and that soft law still largely prevails. The article names no draft law. In the dean's account, soft law and not hard law is what governs AI in the DR Congo.

General AI law and the law applied. No general AI law is described in the same 23 August 2024 article on droitnumerique.cd. The dean places the country's rules on AI in soft law, which still largely prevails, and names neither a hard law on AI nor a draft of one. The article is the dean's account of how the DR Congo governs AI and automated decision-making, and it describes soft law as the instrument in use.

Not held. Whether a draft law exists is not known; the one source is a 2024 opinion piece.

COG.short: A bill adopted in April 2026 sets an ethical framework for AI in research; whether it is in force is not known.
COG.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. On 8 April 2026 the Congolese National Assembly adopted a bill on the orientation and development of scientific research. The bill introduces an ethical framework for AI and institutes a national committee to oversee responsible AI use. The report of the adoption, published by the Congolese news agency ACI, does not say the bill is in force. The bill is a law on scientific research, and AI is one of the matters it regulates.

General AI law and the law applied. The only measure held is the research bill, adopted by the National Assembly on 8 April 2026. Its AI provisions, the ethical framework and the national committee on responsible AI use, sit within a bill on scientific research. They cover AI within scientific research and not across sectors. No other law, decree or regulation on AI is held for the Republic of the Congo.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

COM.short: A media code in force since February 2026 requires AI-generated content to be labelled; there is no law on AI itself.
COM.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. The Code of Information and Communication, adopted by Law 25-021/AU of 26 December 2025 and promulgated by decree on 2 February 2026, requires any content generated or heavily modified by AI to be labelled as such, under its article 231. The media regulator, the Conseil national de la presse et de l'audiovisuel, can impose penalties of up to 1,000,000 Comorian francs.

General AI law and the law applied. The rule in force covers one use, AI-generated content in the media, and sits in a code that governs the press and broadcasting. The Comoros has no law on AI itself applying across sectors, and no bill or draft of one appears in any source dated to September 2026. No penalty imposed under article 231 is on record either.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

CPV.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CPV.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

DJI.short: A national newspaper said in August 2026 that no law in Djibouti addresses AI; no draft is named.
DJI.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Djibouti has no law on AI. La Nation, reporting the country's AI readiness assessment in August 2026, said that no law specifically addresses artificial intelligence to date. It describes the Digital Code as a framework for data protection only. The article names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and no ministry asked to write one.

General AI law and the law applied. With no law that addresses AI in August 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The article reports the readiness assessment carried out with UNESCO's support, and sets the missing law beside it as part of where the country stands on AI. The Digital Code it names is the nearest rule the country has, and it covers personal data and not AI.

Not held.

DZA.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
DZA.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

EGY.short: A 2024 financial regulator decree on robo-advisors is in force; a general AI law is still a draft in 2026.
EGY.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. FRA Board Decree No. 57 of 2024 regulates robo-advisors for investment and is AI-specific. It requires client suitability assessments and gives clients a right to discontinue automated transactions. A 2026 Legal 500 guide by a law firm also says the Government is preparing a draft AI law with the House of Representatives' Communications and IT Committee, and elsewhere calls it the draft currently before Parliament.

General AI law and the law applied. The same 2026 Legal 500 guide states that no binding AI-specific statute is in force in Egypt. The one binding AI-specific measure it names is the 2024 decree of the Financial Regulatory Authority board on robo-advisors for investment, which reaches that sector and no other. The decree dates from 2024 and the draft law from the guide's 2026 imprint.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

ERI.short: A review of June 2026 says Eritrea has no AI law and no AI-specific legislation; no draft is named.
ERI.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Eritrea has no law on AI. A legal-status page last reviewed on 8 June 2026 states that Eritrea has no dedicated AI law and no AI-specific legislation, and that AI is not governed by any specific national framework. It names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation, and no ministry or body asked to prepare one.

General AI law and the law applied. With no AI-specific legislation in June 2026, there is no general AI law in force and nothing to apply. The same page says no national framework of any kind governs AI in the country, so no regulator holds a duty to oversee it. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI is recorded either.

Not held.

ETH.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ETH.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

GAB.short: An ordinance of April 2026 governs AI-generated content and bans deepfakes; there is no law on AI itself.
GAB.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Gabon has a binding rule on one use of AI. A report of August 2026 cites an ordinance of April 2026 governing AI-generated content, which among other things prohibits deepfakes. The report gives no number for the ordinance and quotes none of its articles. It sets the ordinance beside a national technical committee on AI and a national AI agenda for 2026 to 2036.

General AI law and the law applied. The ordinance of April 2026 covers content generated by AI and not AI across sectors. Gabon has no law on AI itself in any source dated to September 2026, and no bill or draft of one is named. No prosecution, order or penalty under the ordinance is on record, and the body that enforces it is not named.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

GHA.short: A draft information technology bill of 2026 would regulate AI among other technologies; no rule on AI is in force.
GHA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Ghana has a draft and no rule in force. A report of 26 May 2026 says the proposed National Information Technology Authority bill, written to replace the 2008 law on the authority, includes regulation of emerging technologies such as AI and blockchain. It is one of 15 digital bills the government put out together, and the report records a consultant's objection to the speed of the consultation.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The draft bill treats AI as one of several emerging technologies an information technology regulator would oversee, and is not a law on AI itself. No source dated to September 2026 says it has gone to cabinet or to parliament, and none names a separate AI bill.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

GIN.short: A ministry official said in October 2025 that Guinea has no AI law or framework; whether a draft is under way is not known.
GIN.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. On 14 October 2025 the secretary-general of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy said Guinea lacks a legislative and regulatory framework on AI at the opening of a workshop to diagnose the country's position on AI. The official added that Guinea has not yet adopted a specific AI law.

General AI law and the law applied. The same official, speaking on 14 October 2025 at the opening of the diagnostic workshop, said Guinea has not adopted an AI-specific law, unlike other countries of the sub-region. The statement covers the whole legislative and regulatory framework on AI, and no law on AI of any scope is named. The statement is the ministry official's own account of the legal position on AI.

Not held. Whether any draft is under way is not known.

GMB.short: An assessment of June 2026 says The Gambia has no legislation on AI and none proposed.
GMB.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. The Gambia has no law on AI. An assessment by the Oxford Institute of Technology and Justice states that as at June 2026 there is no dedicated legislation regulating the use of AI in The Gambia and no proposed legislation on AI. It is the one source held that says in terms that no draft exists as well as no law.

General AI law and the law applied. With no legislation on AI in force or proposed in June 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The assessment looks at AI in the justice system, where it describes an automated system for recording and transcribing court proceedings, in use without any rule written for AI. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI is recorded.

Not held.

GNB.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

GNQ.short: A ministry was revising a preliminary draft of an AI law in 2025; no rule on AI is in force.
GNQ.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Equatorial Guinea has a draft and no rule in force. In August 2025 the ministry responsible for transport, telecommunications and AI systems was writing a preliminary draft of an AI law, and a working session went through the observations and amendments made to its first version. The report is dated 27 August 2025 and gives no date for the session.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The preliminary draft is for a law on AI itself and not for one sector or one use. No source dated to September 2026 says it has been approved by the Council of Ministers or sent to parliament, and nothing on its content beyond the drafting sessions is recorded.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

KEN.short: An AI bill has been before the Senate since February 2026; no rule on AI is in force.
KEN.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Kenya has a bill before parliament and no rule in force. The Artificial Intelligence Bill was introduced in the Senate on 19 February 2026. A memorandum sent to the Senate in May 2026 describes the bill as creating an AI Commissioner's office, an advisory committee and a classification of high-risk systems, with transparency duties and standards for the public sector. It was still a bill in September 2026.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force: a university centre wrote in September 2026 that Kenya has no AI laws and that most regulation touching AI falls under the Data Protection Act. The Senate bill would apply across sectors. An earlier Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Society Bill of 2023, which proposed licensing, was not passed.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

LBR.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LBR.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

LBY.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LBY.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

LSO.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
LSO.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

MAR.short: The electoral law revised for the 2026 elections makes AI-made falsehoods a crime; a general AI bill of 2025 has not passed.
MAR.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Morocco has a binding rule on one use of AI. An interview published in July 2026 says the revised electoral law for the 2026 legislative elections makes it a crime to use AI and digital means to alter the truth or to harm the private lives of individuals and candidates. The government's draft organic law 53.25, laid before the House of Representatives in October 2025, set two to five years' imprisonment and a fine of 50,000 to 100,000 dirhams.

General AI law and the law applied. The rule covers elections and not AI across sectors. A private member's bill on regulating the use of AI, of 17 articles, was received by the bureau of the House of Representatives in January 2025; no source dated to September 2026 says it has been debated or passed.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

MDG.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MDG.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

MLI.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MLI.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

MOZ.short: A law on AI in education was almost ready for cabinet in September 2026; no rule on AI is in force.
MOZ.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Mozambique has a draft for one sector and no rule in force. The education and culture minister said on 16 September 2026 that a law to regulate the use of AI in education is almost ready and will go to the Council of Ministers for approval before the end of 2026. It would cover every institution from primary school to higher education.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. A month earlier the chairman of the national institute for information and communication technologies said that Mozambique does not yet have specific legislation governing AI and called for a dedicated legal framework. The education law would cover one sector, and no draft of a law on AI itself is named.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

MRT.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MRT.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

MUS.short: Regulations in force since March 2026 govern AI in higher education; there is no law on AI itself.
MUS.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Mauritius has a binding rule on AI in one sector. The Higher Education (Use of Artificial Intelligence) Regulations 2026, Government Notice 39 of 2026, were made by the minister under the Higher Education Act 2017 and came into operation on 31 March 2026. They oblige higher education institutions to adopt policies on AI and require the use of AI tools to be disclosed.

General AI law and the law applied. The regulations apply to higher education only. Mauritius has no law on AI itself applying across sectors in any source dated to September 2026, and no bill or draft of one is named. Its AI strategy and its guidelines on the development and use of AI are not binding. No decision or penalty under the regulations is on record.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

MWI.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
MWI.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

NAM.short: The minister said in August 2026 that no AI legislation has been introduced; a strategy comes first.
NAM.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Namibia has no law on AI. The minister for information and communication technology said at a meeting on 3 August 2026 that the government has put a national AI strategy before legislation, so no AI legislation has yet been introduced; a second report of the meeting says the same. A year earlier, at the launch of the country's AI readiness assessment, the absence of a formal regulatory framework for AI was named as a standing problem.

General AI law and the law applied. With no AI legislation introduced by August 2026, there is no general AI law to apply and no draft of one is named. The readiness assessment recommended a national framework for governing AI, and the strategy the minister described is the step the government has chosen to take first.

Not held.

NER.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
NER.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

NGA.short: A 2025 data protection directive sets duties for anyone deploying AI; several AI bills are before parliament and none has passed.
NGA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Nigeria has a binding rule that names AI, inside its data protection rules. The data protection commission's General Application and Implementation Directive of 2025 requires an organisation deploying AI to document its parameters, assess unequal outcomes and test the system, under article 43, and to stop using AI systems that pose undue risks to human rights, under article 44.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI itself is in force. Four AI bills passed second reading in the House of Representatives on 3 December 2024, and a proposed Artificial Intelligence Bill with a licensing regime and an AI council was under debate in November 2025. In January 2026 the government was preparing to regulate AI through the National Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill, with yearly impact assessments for high-risk systems.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

RWA.short: A review of September 2026 says Rwanda has no AI act and relies on its 2023 AI policy; no draft is named.
RWA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Rwanda has no law on AI. A university centre wrote in September 2026 that there is no AI Act in Rwanda, and that the country's framework for AI rests on the National AI Policy of April 2023, with the laws on personal data and privacy as supplementary support. It names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI.

General AI law and the law applied. With no AI Act in September 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The policy of 2023 that carries the field is a statement of the government's aims and binds no one; the data protection and privacy laws beside it apply to AI only as they apply to any processing of personal data. No rule for one sector that names AI is recorded.

Not held.

SDN.short: The Council of Ministers discussed a draft data and AI law in August 2026; no rule on AI is in force.
SDN.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Sudan has a draft and no rule in force. On 6 August 2026 the Council of Ministers discussed a draft Data and Artificial Intelligence Law put forward by the ministry for digital transformation, and directed that it be studied further before going for approval to the interim parliament, a joint sitting of the Sovereignty Council and the Council of Ministers.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. Five days later the undersecretary of the justice ministry said the ministry was preparing, with the digital transformation ministry, three draft laws for 2026, one of them the law regulating data and AI. The draft joins AI to data in one law across sectors; nothing on its content is recorded.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

SEN.short: A July 2024 diagnostic found no AI-specific legal text in Senegal; whether a draft has appeared since is not known.
SEN.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. An IPAR diagnostic published in July 2024 covers the policy, legal and ethical framework on AI in four West African countries, Senegal among them. It says there is as yet no legal text specific to AI at continental, regional or national level.

General AI law and the law applied. The same July 2024 IPAR diagnostic adds that, of the four West African countries it covers, only Benin has a framework suited to regulating AI. It names no such framework for Senegal, and it finds no legal text specific to AI at national level. The diagnostic names no law, decree or regulation on AI in force in Senegal, and none for the West African region or for the continent as a whole.

Not held. Whether any draft is under way, or the position since July 2024, is not known.

SLE.short: The justice minister said in September 2026 that no specific AI legislation has been enacted; no draft is named.
SLE.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Sierra Leone has no law on AI. The attorney-general and justice minister told a UNESCO meeting in Riyadh on 16 September 2026 that the country has established a position on AI but has not yet enacted specific AI legislation. The report of his remarks names no bill, draft decree or draft regulation on AI, and no date by which one is to be written.

General AI law and the law applied. With no specific AI legislation enacted by September 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The minister set out a national position on AI to UNESCO without naming a law to carry it, and the report gives no account of what that position requires of anyone. No rule for one sector or one use that names AI is recorded.

Not held.

SOM.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SOM.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

SSD.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SSD.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

STP.short: UNESCO's 2026 profile and the minister both say the country has no AI-specific laws or regulations; no draft is named.
STP.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Sao Tome and Principe has no law on AI. UNESCO's country profile, published in January 2026, states that the country has no AI-specific laws or regulations governing the development, use or deployment of AI. The minister of education wrote the same in the preface to the country's AI readiness assessment of 2025. Neither names a bill or a draft.

General AI law and the law applied. With no law or regulation specific to AI in January 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The profile and the readiness assessment both treat the data protection law and its authority as the nearest rules the country has, and neither records a rule for one sector or one use that names AI.

Not held.

SWZ.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

SYC.short: A private member's draft bill covering AI was presented to Assembly members in 2024; no rule on AI is known to be in force.
SYC.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Seychelles has a draft and no rule in force. A private member's draft Pro-Human Technology Bill, covering AI in employment and education among other technologies, was presented to National Assembly members at a seminar on 6 March 2024. The Speaker told the seminar the bill was still far from reaching the Assembly, and it is expected to go to an Assembly working group.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The only draft held, the Pro-Human Technology Bill, is a private member's bill that covers AI together with other technologies, among them its use in employment and education. It was presented to Assembly members in March 2024, has not reached the Assembly, and is expected to go to an Assembly working group.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

TCD.short: In April 2026 a minister said Chad's digital texts cannot regulate AI and set up a committee; no draft law is known.
TCD.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Chad has no binding rule on AI and no draft. On 27 April 2026 the telecoms minister said that existing digital texts no longer allow AI to be regulated. He installed a 34-member committee and gave it 45 days to propose updated texts for the digital legal framework.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The article of 27 April 2026 describes the current legal vacuum on AI and names no draft text. The telecoms minister installed a committee of 34 members and set it 45 days to propose updated texts, after saying that the existing digital texts no longer allow AI to be regulated. No draft text on AI is named in the article.

Not held. What the committee proposed after its 45 days is not known.

TGO.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
TGO.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

TUN.short: A draft data protection law including AI use was before a committee in February 2026; no rule on AI is known in force.
TUN.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Tunisia has a draft and no rule in force. Organic law proposal 095/2025 on personal data protection runs to 132 articles in 6 chapters and includes regulation of AI use. It was heard before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 17 February 2026, as a proposal in the Assembly and not yet as a law passed by it. The text reached committee as a data protection reform, with the regulation of AI use as one of its provisions.

General AI law and the law applied. No law on AI is in force. The proposal under review, the Proposition de loi organique 095/2025, is a data protection law that includes AI use among its subjects, and not a law on AI itself. Its 132 articles in 6 chapters were heard before the Assembly's Rights and Freedoms Committee on 17 February 2026, and the chapters on personal data sit alongside the provisions that regulate AI use.

Not held. No source held says a law, decree or regulation that sets a rule for AI is in force.

TZA.short: Regulations of January 2025 prohibit fabricated AI-generated content online; there is no law on AI itself.
TZA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Tanzania has a binding rule on one use of AI. Government Notice 57 of 28 January 2025, made under the Electronic and Postal Communications Act, amends the Online Content Regulations of 2020 to add unethical, fabricated and AI-generated video, audio and still pictures to the content prohibited online. It obliges internet service providers and the owners of social media platforms to filter and remove such content.

General AI law and the law applied. The rule covers online content and not AI across sectors. A university centre wrote in September 2026 that Tanzania lacks a dedicated AI law and that the laws used for AI are mostly data protection laws. No bill or draft of a law on AI itself is named, and no order or penalty under the 2025 amendment is on record.

Not held. No source held says a law on AI itself, applying across sectors, is in force.

UGA.short: A review of September 2026 says Uganda has no AI laws in place; a 2025 government assessment found the same.
UGA.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Uganda has no law on AI. A university centre wrote in September 2026 that Uganda has no AI laws in place and uses data protection laws in place of a dedicated framework. An assessment by the ministry responsible for information and communication technology with the International Telecommunication Union, dated 2025, lists the lack of an AI policy and of a legal and regulatory framework among its main findings.

General AI law and the law applied. With no AI laws in place in September 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. The 2025 assessment recommends that Uganda develop a policy and a legal framework for AI. Neither source names a bill or a draft, or a rule for one sector that names AI.

Not held.

ZAF.short: Two sources of August 2026 say South Africa has no law or regulations on AI; national rules are expected in 2027.
ZAF.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. South Africa has no law on AI. The chief executive of a technology company wrote in August 2026 that South Africa currently has no law governing artificial intelligence and that national rules are expected in 2027; the same piece ran a week earlier in a second outlet. A research centre wrote the same month that the country has no national AI policy or regulations in place.

General AI law and the law applied. With no law governing AI in August 2026, there is no general AI law to apply. Rules expected in 2027 are an intention; no bill or draft regulation on AI is named in either piece. The research centre's paper says so in a study of automated decisions in social grants, where existing law is the only test.

Not held.

ZMB.short: Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ZMB.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a law or binding rule on AI, or a draft of one, or says there is none.

ZWE.short: An analyst wrote in July 2026 that Zimbabwe has no AI law and no draft; whether one has been introduced since is not known.
ZWE.summary:
Binding rule on AI in force. Zimbabwe has no AI-specific rule in force. On 27 July 2026 Tashinga Magaya of African Law Matters wrote that the National AI Strategy is not a law, that the proposed regulator has no enabling Act, and that the Cyber and Data Protection Act is the law that applies to AI today. She urged that a draft AI Act be introduced within twelve to eighteen months.

General AI law and the law applied. As at 27 July 2026, no AI act exists in Zimbabwe. The National Digital Regulatory Committee named in the strategy has no enabling legislation, and a draft AI Act is still to be introduced to Parliament. The strategy is the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2026-2030, and the Cyber and Data Protection Act is the law that applies to AI today.

Not held. Whether a draft AI Act has been introduced since July 2026 is not known.

AGO.short: Angola's national AI strategy was drafted and awaiting formal approval in 2026; when it will be approved is not known.
AGO.summary:
Strategy adopted. Angola has a National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in draft. UNESCO's readiness assessment of Angola, published in July 2026, lists the strategy's formal approval as a next step, so a text exists and the government has not yet approved it. No source held gives the date drafting began or names the body that wrote it.

Body named and action funded. The same assessment lists setting up an interinstitutional coordination mechanism for AI as a next step, so no such body was in place in July 2026. Because the strategy is not yet adopted, there is nothing for a body to carry out or for money to follow. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up for it, or public money set aside for it. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held says a national AI strategy is adopted and still running.

BDI.short: Burundi's national AI strategy for 2025 to 2030 was validated at a workshop in April 2026; whether the government has approved it is not known.
BDI.summary:
Strategy adopted. Burundi has a national AI strategy for 2025 to 2030 in draft. It was validated in Bujumbura in April 2026 with UNDP support, and was designed by the Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy. The validation session opened on 21 April 2026. No source held says the government has approved or launched it.

Body named and action funded. A UNDP workshop in November 2025 assessed the country's AI landscape and fed the strategy, which the government then said it would draw up. Because the strategy is not yet adopted, there is nothing for a body to carry out or for money to follow. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up for it, or public money set aside for it. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held says a national AI strategy is adopted and still running.

BEN.short: Benin adopted a national AI and big data strategy in 2023, running to 2027; whether a body carries it out is not known.
BEN.summary:
Strategy adopted. Benin adopted a national strategy for AI and big data covering 2023 to 2027. A comparative study of four West African countries says Benin was the first of the four to adopt a national AI strategy, in 2023. In July 2026 a ministry representative described a university's own AI strategy as in line with the national one, which was then still running.

Body named and action funded. The national strategy runs to 2027. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up or named to carry out the strategy. No source held names public money allocated to it, or an action in it started with its funding named, in the last three years. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held names a body set up or named to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's draft national AI roadmap for 2026 to 2030 went to a validation workshop in June 2026; its adoption is not known.
BFA.summary:
Strategy adopted. Burkina Faso has a national AI roadmap for 2026 to 2030 in draft. The Ministry of Digital Transition held a validation workshop on the draft on 17 June 2026, and had begun drafting a national AI action plan through a consultation workshop in 2025. A comparative study presented in August 2026 says the country does not yet have a dedicated national AI strategy.

Body named and action funded. The roadmap is expected to guide the country's AI work once it is adopted. Because the strategy is not yet adopted, there is nothing for a body to carry out or for money to follow. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up for it, or public money set aside for it. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held says a national AI strategy is adopted and still running.

BWA.short: Botswana's government said in 2025 that it was finalising a national AI policy; whether it has since been adopted is not known.
BWA.summary:
Strategy adopted. Botswana has a National Artificial Intelligence Policy in draft. At the Botswana Tech Summit on 13 August 2025 the Assistant Minister of Communications and Innovation said the government was working on finalising the policy, after an AI readiness exercise with UNESCO. No source held dated since then says whether the policy has been finished, approved or launched.

Body named and action funded. The policy was still being finalised in August 2025. Because the strategy is not yet adopted, there is nothing for a body to carry out or for money to follow. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up for it, or public money set aside for it. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held says a national AI strategy is adopted and still running.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic was drafting a national AI strategy for 2024 to 2028 in 2024; whether it has been adopted is not known.
CAF.summary:
Strategy adopted. The Central African Republic has a national AI strategy for 2024 to 2028 in draft. On 21 November 2024 the minister of posts, telecommunications and digital economy said the country was in the full drafting phase of the strategy. No source held dated since then says whether the draft has been finished, approved or launched.

Body named and action funded. The strategy was in its drafting phase in November 2024. Because the strategy is not yet adopted, there is nothing for a body to carry out or for money to follow. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up for it, or public money set aside for it. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held says a national AI strategy is adopted and still running.

CIV.short: Cote d'Ivoire has adopted a national AI strategy to 2030; in 2026 a budgeted roadmap was still awaited and no body is known.
CIV.summary:
Strategy adopted. Cote d'Ivoire has an adopted national AI strategy. The strategy was handed to the Prime Minister on 13 March 2025 for adoption by the government, and a comparative study presented in August 2026 says the country has adopted its AI strategy to 2030. In September 2026 the strategy was being turned into projects, with a three-year roadmap to follow.

Body named and action funded. On 11 September 2026 the minister said the government would speed up the strategy's implementation, with a budgeted roadmap expected within three weeks. In March 2025 the money needed to carry out the strategy had not been disclosed, and a national committee for AI and data governance was listed as a first action. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up or named to carry out the strategy. No source held names public money allocated to it, or an action in it started with its funding named, in the last three years. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held names a body set up or named to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

CMR.short: Cameroon launched its first national AI strategy in July 2025, with targets to 2040; whether a body carries it out is not known.
CMR.summary:
Strategy adopted. Cameroon launched its National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in July 2025. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications unveiled it at national consultations on 7 and 8 July 2025, and the government officially launched it there as its first national AI strategy. It sets targets to 2040, among them 60,000 AI professionals and 12,000 direct AI jobs.

Body named and action funded. An international policy observatory, updated in April 2026, lists the strategy as run by the Minister of Posts and Telecommunications. No source held names a council, office, agency or ministry unit set up or named to carry out the strategy. No source held names public money allocated to it, or an action in it started with its funding named, in the last three years. No implementation plan or budget for it is held.

Not held. No source held names a body set up or named to carry out the strategy: a council, office, agency, committee or ministry unit.

COD.short: The Democratic Republic of the Congo validated its national AI strategy in August 2026; its adoption by the Council of Ministers is not known.
COD.summary:
Strategy adopted. The Democratic Republic of the Congo has a national AI strategy validated and awaiting adoption. Public bodies, partners and experts validated it at a ceremony in Kinshasa on 4 August 2026, ending a process led by the Ministry of Digital Economy.
