DJI.short: Djibouti's 2025 Digital Code creates a data protection authority; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
DJI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Digital Code's data-protection regime creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP), independent with administrative and financial autonomy, as reviewed on 5 November 2025. That review does not say the commission has been constituted or its members appointed, so the law is the only step the sources show. The National Assembly voted the Code on 30 June 2025, and Jones Day reports that the regime establishes the CNDP.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is from the same 2025 Jones Day report, which frames the competent authorities as still to be put into operation. Nothing in the sources held shows the commission at work in practice. They record no ruling by the commission against an organisation and no figures it has published.

Not held. No source held says the authority's head or members have been appointed, and none records a ruling or published figures.

DZA.short: Algeria has a working authority with a named president in 2026; it has issued decisions but no ruling against an organisation or figures are known.
DZA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law 18-07 is enforced by the national data protection authority (ANPDP), and Samir Bourehil is named as its president in July 2026, attending a study day alongside the Justice and Interior ministers. The authority adopted a deliberation at its sitting of 15 July 2026, signed by its president with twelve members named at the foot. It also issues authorisations and receives declarations of processing as of December 2025. An earlier US commercial guide from September 2024 already named it as the enforcer of Law 18-07.

Rulings and published figures. The authority issued a decision in early 2026 on employee and candidate drug test results, and its July 2026 deliberation sets rules on publishing images on digital platforms. No ruling against a named organisation is held, and no published figures.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held, and no figures it has published.

EGY.short: Egypt has a data protection authority in 2026, still led by an acting chief; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
EGY.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection Center (PDPC) is confirmed as the supervisory authority for implementation, monitoring and enforcement under the executive regulations of November 2025. A 7 August 2026 report shows it acting under Law 151 of 2020, under an acting chief executive, Susan El-Okbawy, who is described as affiliated to the ICT ministry. In October 2026 it launched its electronic portal for accreditation, licence and permit applications.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is the licensing and breach-handling role the acting chief executive described in August 2026, with a compliance deadline of November 2026 for organisations covered by the law. The sources describe a body that is licensing and preparing for enforcement. No ruling against an organisation is held, and no figures published by the centre.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held, and no figures it has published.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection authority and has issued no rulings or figures, as of 2026.
ERI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law Lab Africa states that no supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. Levellers states, in a page reviewed on 8 June 2026, that Eritrea has no data protection statute and has not appointed a data protection authority. The Horn of Africa Initiative matrix update of June 2025 says Eritrea remains without regulatory oversight for data protection, while Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia have established authorities.

Rulings and published figures. Law Lab Africa found no enforcement decisions for Eritrea and none published, in its verification pass of 1 August 2026. Levellers states there is no data protection authority to register with or appeal to, so none issues rulings. A Data Protection Africa fact sheet, last updated 24 May 2022, records no authority report and no public report.

Not held. Nothing is held on any plan to set up an authority or pass a data protection law.

ETH.short: Ethiopia has an authority, the Communications Authority, in 2025. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
ETH.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator, in an overview of July 2024. By November 2025 Shega described the Authority, whose mandate was extended from telecom regulation to data protection, as enforcing the law. Its Director General, Balcha Reba, said data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission and that staffing and technical capacity are being expanded.

Rulings and published figures. The Shega article of 15 November 2025 describes enforcement as on a slow path, one year after the law. It names the permission requirement for processors and collectors as the Authority's current step. The overview of the proclamation says only that the Authority is designated as regulator, and names no decision, fine or order against an organisation.

Not held. No ruling against a named organisation in the last three years is held. No published count of decisions or complaints is held.

GAB.short: Gabon has an authority and fined a bank 90 million FCFA in 2024. No published figures are known.
GAB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 7 of Loi n°025/2023 creates the APDPVP as an independent administrative authority, with powers to authorise processing, receive complaints and fine from CFA 1 million to 100 million. Its 25 April 2024 plenary sat with a named president, vice-president and six other commissioners, appointed by Council of Ministers decision of 12 July 2023. Its president was still speaking as head of the authority on 4 September 2026.

Rulings and published figures. By deliberation n°073 of 25 April 2024, on a complaint of 27 November 2023, the APDPVP plenary fined Citibank Gabon S.A. 90,000,000 FCFA. It found the bank had diverted employee data from its declared purpose and processed ethnic-origin data, and it added a two-month formal notice.

Not held. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled, for a period ending in the last two years, is held.

GHA.short: Ghana has a working data protection authority, and in 2026 it reported rises in activity, but no ruling against an organisation is known.
GHA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Commission describes itself as an independent statutory body established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843). In August 2025 the Minister for Communication swore in its new governing board, chaired by Teki Akuetteh. Its 2026 budget estimate is GHS 9,720,400, all from internally generated funds, with 39 staff. The Commission's own page names its Executive Director, Dr Arnold Kavaarpuo, and a board member at a vehicle commissioning on 20 February 2026, and a GNA report says it operates only from its head office.

Rulings and published figures. On 7 September 2026 the Communications Minister said the Commission's regulatory activity rose 51.5 per cent and newly registered data controllers 98.4 per cent in the first half of 2026. In October 2026 it was running registration and spot checks under Act 843. In January 2026 it said it would intensify compliance checks and regulatory actions.

Not held. No ruling by the Commission against a named organisation in the last three years is held, and no regular published enforcement figures.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2016 law provides for a data protection authority, but none is known to be in place, to have ruled, or to publish figures.
GIN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law defines an Autorité de Protection and gives it functions covering declarations, authorisations, transfer approval and investigation. It names no constituted body or members. In June 2024 the National Transition Council's commissions debated a bill to establish the authority, with members' designation and mandates still contested and plenary adoption pending. The CNT page gives the authority's name as Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is the 2016 law, which gives the authority power to investigate and to approve transfers, issue guidelines and receive processing declarations, though declarations go to the authority 'designated by regulation'. No ruling or published figure from the authority is held.

Not held. No source held says the authority's head or members have been appointed, and no ruling or figure is held.

GMB.short: The Gambia's 2025 law created a data protection commission, which was acting by 2026, but no ruling or published figure is known.
GMB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025 establishes an independent oversight Commission, as a review of 26 December 2025 states, and a report of October 2025 says its compliance and enforcement mechanisms remain to be established. In August 2026 a notice has the Information Commission of The Gambia developing a communication strategy on the Act, alongside the Access to Information Act, 2021, which suggests the Commission is acting for the Act.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that the Act lets the Commission assess cross-border transfers and impose conditions, a power described in February 2026, and the same source does not say the Commission is constituted. No ruling or published figure from the Commission is held, and no count of complaints or registrations.

Not held. No ruling by the Commission against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection authority as of 2026, so it has made no ruling against an organisation and publishes no figures.
GNB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, a speaker said on 22 September 2026, with these matters handled by several institutions sector by sector. The Data Protection Africa factsheet, published 25 May 2022, states that the country has no data protection law and that its authority is not appointed.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held for Guinea-Bissau, in 2026 or any earlier year. The nearest held fact is the factsheet of 25 May 2022, which states that the data protection authority is not appointed, so there is no body in place to rule on a complaint, to fine an organisation or to publish a count of its work.

Not held. Nothing is held on any plan or draft to create an authority, or on any ruling or figures.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's 2016 law creates an authority, but by 2022 it was not appointed; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
GNQ.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Articles 15 and 29 of Law No. 1/2016, dated 22 July 2016, name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, with a Secretaría Técnica and a Registro General under it. They state that it is to be created by a decree that will fix its structure. Data Protection Africa, in a factsheet published 23 May 2022, states that the authority is not yet appointed or operational.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held. The nearest held fact is the factsheet of 23 May 2022, which states that the authority created by the 2016 law is not yet operational, so it had no decisions or figures to publish.

Not held. No source says whether the head or members of the authority have been appointed since 2022, and none reports a ruling or figures.

KEN.short: Kenya has had an authority since 2020 and it has fined businesses; its only published count is a running total, not a yearly figure.
KEN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, and Immaculate Kassait has been the inaugural commissioner since 2020, TechTrends KE reports; on 30 September 2026 the Public Service Commission had shortlisted 13 of 152 applicants to succeed her. Its March 2025 bulletin shows offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru. The Standard reports that the office launched an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system on 14 July 2026.

Rulings and published figures. As at September 2024 the office had fined at least nine businesses a total of KES 26,275,000, Cadmus Cyber Solutions states, including Oppo Kenya in 2022 (KES 5m) and SBM Bank in 2024 (KES 450,000). The office's own bulletin gives cumulative counts to March 2025: 7,128 complaints received, 97 percent resolved, 215 determinations, penalties on 10 entities and 103 compensations.

Not held. No count of decisions, fines or complaints settled is held for a period ending in the last two years, and the 215 determinations carry no period.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2026 Act gives the work to an existing commissioner; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
LBR.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024, printed on 23 March 2026, gives data protection functions to the Independent Information Commissioner in sections 8 and 10 (the printed Act). That body was created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010. Before the Act, in February 2025, a minister told the Africa-China Reporting Project that Liberia had no national data protection authority, and in June 2025 the Liberian Observer reported that the country still lacked a dedicated data protection law.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held. The nearest held fact is that the printed Act of 23 March 2026 does not say the Commissioner has begun acting under it.

Not held. Nothing held says the Commissioner or its members have been appointed under the Act, or that any ruling or figures have been published.

LBY.short: Nothing is held on whether Libya has a data protection authority, has ruled against an organisation or publishes figures.
LBY.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a data protection authority for Libya or says there is none.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2012 law creates a commission, unappointed in 2025; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
LSO.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Act (Act 5 of 2012) establishes a Data Protection Commission, but the law firm Z. Mayet and Associates states that the Commission and its Commissioner had not been appointed as at 31 October 2025, so the regulator did not exist in practice. Cenfri said the same of the Commission in an article published on 23 March 2026: the Data Protection Commission under the Act has remained unappointed, with no date given for that statement.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held. The nearest held fact is the position stated by Z. Mayet and Associates in October 2025, that neither the Commission nor its Commissioner had been appointed, so the regulator did not exist in practice.

Not held. Nothing held says the Commission or its Commissioner has since been appointed, or that any ruling or figures have been published.

MAR.short: Morocco has an authority, the CNDP, active in 2026; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
MAR.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Morocco's CNDP, the national commission for the control of personal data protection, works under Law 09-08. It was installed in 2010, and its president says it began fifteen years ago. In August 2026 it informed parties and citizens of the data rules for the 23 September 2026 elections and opened a 3020 public line. It keeps the national register of processing operations for 2010 to 31 December 2022, and signed a cooperation memorandum with Portugal's authority on 8 February 2026.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is procedural: on 28 November 2025 the CNDP validated five new deliberations, D-939 to D-943 of 2025, showing it acting as the supervisory body, and the Official Gazette published its members under Law 09-08 in 2012. Its president says its alert system is being strengthened, up to sanctions.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

MDG.short: Madagascar's authority, the CMIL, was sworn in during 2025; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known for 2026.
MDG.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Law 2014-038 provides for the CMIL: article 28 institutes an independent authority of nine members with regulatory and sanctioning powers. It had still not been created in February 2025. Seven members were sworn in at the Cour suprême on 4 August 2025, and the bureau was elected on 14 August 2025. Midi Madagasikara reports the Council of Ministers validated the decree naming its members, and a government announcement of 27 March 2026 says the CMIL is now effectively in place.

Rulings and published figures. The CMIL's own annual report, published January 2026, says no processing declaration has been registered, citizen complaints went untreated for ten years, and it still lacks premises and staff, with 104 posts targeted in the 2026 Finance Law and none yet recruited.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

MLI.short: Mali has an authority, the APDP, which fined a clinic and published figures for 2025.
MLI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Mali's APDP is an independent administrative authority of 15 members under Article 20 of Law 2013-015. It held its second ordinary session on 3 August 2026 with all commissioners present, and runs regional offices at Kayes, Sikasso, Segou and Mopti. It opened a Ségou antenna on 4 December 2025. On 18 November 2025 its president signed the operational roadmap of the AES coordination framework with Burkina Faso and Niger.

Rulings and published figures. For 2025 the APDP annual report, as summarised by Sahel Tribune, gives about 1,000 formal notices, fines totalling 22 million FCFA and 51 complaints, 28 of them handled. It fined a Bamako clinic 5 million FCFA for obstructing a verification mission linked to an undeclared video-surveillance system. In June 2025 it also fined a company 5 million FCFA for refusing a verification mission.

Not held. No gap is recorded on whether the authority exists, has ruled or publishes figures.

MOZ.short: Mozambique has no data protection authority yet; none has ruled against an organisation or published figures, as of 2025.
MOZ.summary:
Named in law and appointed. A UNECA inception report of June 2025 states that Mozambique has no data regulatory authority, though INTIC, INCM, INAGE and CEDSIF oversee parts of data governance. The World Bank restructuring paper says the Data Protection Office was not yet established as of October 2025. A September 2025 review says the draft law would give the role to the existing Regulatory Authority for ICT, alongside a National Council chaired by the Prime Minister.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling and no published figure is held, and no body exists to issue them. The nearest held fact is that the Data Protection Office, which the World Bank paper says is not yet established, had its project funding cut from US$18m to US$11m. The same inception report names a Data Protection Bill.

Not held. Whether an authority has been established since October 2025, and any ruling or figure it has published.

MRT.short: Mauritania has a data protection authority, in session in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
MRT.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 64 of Law 2017-020 creates an independent Authority for Personal Data Protection attached to the Prime Minister, with its composition and the appointment of members left to a decree. Decree 2022-13 of 18 February 2022 is cited for its composition and operation. The authority is in session: it held monthly meetings on 29 April 2026 and 30 June 2026, and its president was sworn in for a second term on 7 October 2026.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures are held. The nearest held fact is that the authority adopted deliberation 005/2025 on 30 July 2025, and met on 14 July 2025 to adopt deliberation 004/2025, both general rules rather than findings against an organisation.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

MUS.short: Mauritius has a data protection authority and published 2024 figures on complaints and breaches; no ruling against an organisation is known.
MUS.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Office has operated since 16 February 2009 and enforces the Data Protection Act 2017. Its 2024 annual report is signed by Data Protection Commissioner Drudeisha Madhub. In June 2026 regulations on data protection officers gave the Office roles in receiving notifications, certifying officers and approving training institutions.

Rulings and published figures. The Office publishes annual figures. For January to December 2024 it reports 179 new complaints, 158 of them on CCTV, and 39 complaints closed. It also reports 105 personal data breaches notified, 112 cross-border transfers authorised and 12 rejected under section 36, 10 impact assessments received and four compliance inspections. The figures are the Office's own and cover the 2024 calendar year. No ruling against a named organisation is held.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

MWI.short: Malawi's regulator MACRA has acted as its data protection authority since 2024; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
MWI.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 4 of the Data Protection Act, 2024 designates the Malawi Communications Regulatory Authority (MACRA) as the Data Protection Authority, and the Act came into force on 3 June 2024. In November 2025 the World Bank said MACRA had appointed an acting Data Protection Commissioner and recruited staff from its own budget. In July 2026 Daniel Chiwoni was named as its Head of Data Protection, and a World Bank-funded consultancy is developing the authority's institutional structure and policies.

Rulings and published figures. In October 2025 the authority issued guidelines on personal data breach notification and a guideline and checklist on compliance. In July 2026 it consulted stakeholders on proposed registration fees, and in September 2026 GIZ was supporting its work on audits and investigations.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held, and no published figures are held.

NAM.short: No law names a data protection authority in Namibia; only draft bills of 2020 and 2022 do, and no rulings or figures are known.
NAM.summary: Not held. No law held names an authority, and no source dated in the last three years says the country has none. An authority is named only in draft bills of 2020 and 2022.

NER.short: Niger's authority was running in 2025, but a June 2026 report says it was abolished; no rulings or figures are known.
NER.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 6 of Law 2022-59, as amended by Law 2023-31, creates the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel (HAPDP), attached to the Presidency, with ten members named by decree. Its president took office on 18 September 2024, and on 18 November 2025 the HAPDP signed the AES data-protection roadmap with Burkina Faso and Mali. A report of 13 June 2026 says a decree abolished the HAPDP and split its powers between the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior.

Rulings and published figures. The HAPDP president said in July 2025 that the plenary deliberates on authorisations and sanctions, and a Le Sahel profile of September 2024 gives it powers of inspection and administrative and financial sanction under articles 92-106.

Not held. No source says the authority's head or members have been appointed since the report of its abolition. The decree is not held, and nothing says the two ministries are doing the job.

NGA.short: Nigeria has a data protection commission that fined Multichoice 766 million naira in 2025; no yearly count of its rulings is known.
NGA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2023 Data Protection Act created a formal Data Protection Commission. It is headed by National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji, who said in September 2026 that it generated over N12 billion in revenue over three years. It keeps a registration list of Data Processors of Major Importance and issued a Notice of Investigation on 1 April 2026.

Rulings and published figures. The Commission issued a Final Order against Meta finding violations of the data rights of over 60 million Nigerians and imposing a $32.8 million fine. The fine was later set aside when the Federal High Court in Abuja adopted a settlement between the Commission and Meta. That court-approved settlement dates from 2025, and under it Meta funds a two-year programme.

Not held. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled is held for a period ending in the last two years.

RWA.short: Rwanda's cyber security authority is its named data protection supervisor in 2026; no ruling against an organisation is known.
RWA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The National Cyber Security Authority acts as the supervisory authority for personal data protection and privacy under the Data Protection Act, as an article of 26 January 2026 states. It was published as Rwanda observed Data Privacy Week, held on 26 to 30 January 2026. The Act itself is recorded as introduced on 15 October 2021, and the same article is the source for both facts.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that the authority was the named supervisor under the Act in January 2026. No ruling against a named organisation, no fine and no count of complaints or decisions is held for the authority in the last three years, so there is nothing further to state here.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

SDN.short: A 2022 factsheet says Sudan has no data protection authority; nothing more recent is known, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not held. No law held names an authority. A factsheet last updated on 24 May 2022 says Sudan has no data protection authority appointed, and no source from the last three years says whether that still holds.

SEN.short: Senegal has an authority, created in 2008. It has ruled against organisations, in 2024 and 2026, and publishes quarterly figures.
SEN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP) is an independent administrative authority set up by law no. 2008-12 of 25 January 2008. It was acting in the April to June 2026 quarter, holding two plenary sessions and issuing decisions, and in September 2026 its permanent secretary described joint interoperability work with the DAF. Its president has signed a partnership convention with Benin's authority.

Rulings and published figures. In April 2024 the CDP's plenary session served a formal notice on SOLID SA, operator of the Kay Voter platform, and in March 2026 it ordered a company to uninstall a meeting-room camera. It publishes quarterly figures, including 317 files handled in January to March 2026 and 195 files handled in April to June 2026.

Not held. Nothing further is held on the four questions.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone has no authority yet; one is named only in a 2025 bill. No rulings or figures are known.
SLE.summary: Not held. No law held names an authority, and no source from the last three years says the country has none. An authority is named only in a bill of 2025.

SOM.short: Somalia has an authority, inaugurated in 2024. No ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
SOM.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 6 of the Data Protection Act establishes the Data Protection Authority as an independent agency, and it was inaugurated on 24 February 2024. The law provides for a General Manager and a Board of up to nine members to be appointed within two years. By June 2026 it was accepting registration applications from controllers and processors.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that it issued its Registration Guidelines, version 1.0 of January 2026, issued under Law No. 005 of 2023, setting fees, a 30-day approval timeline and mandatory registration. Its own service page lists the registration forms it issues under Article 10 of the Act. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

SSD.short: South Sudan has no data protection authority as of 2026, so it has made no rulings and published no figures.
SSD.summary:
Named in law and appointed. South Sudan has no data protection authority in place. A 2022 factsheet stated that none had been appointed and that no law established one. In February 2026, Digital Rights Frontlines said the country still lacks a fully operational, independent authority and that the government intends to introduce a Data Protection Bill. Radio Tamazuj reported in late 2025 that a draft bill, once passed, would establish a Data Protection Commission to protect the personal data of South Sudanese online users.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held, because no authority exists to issue them. The nearest held fact is the February 2026 statement that the country lacks an operational, independent authority, which the 2022 factsheet had said in the same terms four years earlier.

Not held. Whether the draft bill has been passed, and when a commission would be appointed, is not held.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe has had a data protection agency since at least 2022; no ruling against an organisation or published figures are known.
STP.summary:
Named in law and appointed. São Tomé and Príncipe has a National Personal Data Protection Agency, the ANPDP, which the 2022 ALT Advisory factsheet says Law 03/2016 establishes and which has an appointed head. In 2026 Téla Nón described it as the body that by law authorises and supervises all data processing, and Macau's data protection office signed a cooperation memorandum with it, signed for the agency by its president, on 1 June 2026. It was a founding member of the Lusophone Data Protection Network, and its president attended the network's first meeting in August 2025.

Rulings and published figures. The 2022 factsheet calls the agency operational and relatively active in authorisations, resolutions and opinions. A 2024 International Bar Association chapter says the agency imposes fines and ancillary measures under the law, but it names no sanction, decision or count. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures are held.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a data protection authority and issued enforcement notices to three organisations in 2024 and 2025; no counts of decisions are known.
SWZ.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Act 2022 designates the Eswatini Communications Commission as the Eswatini Data Protection Authority, as an authority notice states, with powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions. It is acting: in July 2026 it began validation workshops on draft health-data guidelines under an acting chief executive, and in September 2026 it was running an outreach campaign with information desks in major towns.

Rulings and published figures. The authority's own enforcement page lists enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act, issued in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and to Liberty Life Swaziland Limited, and in March 2025 to the Royal Science Technology Park. The registration regime for organisations was in place by February 2026.

Not held. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled, for a period ending in the last two years, is held.

SYC.short: Seychelles has an authority, active since 2023; no ruling against an organisation and no figures for its rulings are known.
SYC.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 5 of the Data Protection Act, 2023 names the Information Commission as the authority, with powers to investigate, audit, issue enforcement notices and impose fines up to SCR200,000. The Commission says it took on the mandate at the end of December 2023. Its 2025 annual report shows a Chief Information Commissioner, two Information Commissioners and a chief executive in post.

Rulings and published figures. The Commission reports each year on the Act: its 2024 annual report notes recruitment and staffing challenges for the new Act, and the National Assembly lists the 2025 report as published on 13 April 2026. It is advertising a Senior Data Protection Analyst post. No ruling against a named organisation is held.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held. What the annual reports record about enforcement is not known.

TCD.short: Chad's data protection directorate had its director and deputy appointed by decree in June 2026; no rulings or figures are known.
TCD.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Decree 2011/PR/2026 of 1 June 2026 appointed a director, replacing a predecessor, and a deputy director of the Direction du contrôle et de la protection des données personnelles, a directorate of the Agence Nationale de Sécurité Informatique et de Certification Electronique (ANSICE). The directorate carries the control and protection of personal data in its title, and its two senior posts were filled by presidential decree in mid-2026.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling, fine or order against a named organisation, and no published count of decisions or complaints, is held. The nearest held fact is the same June 2026 decree filling the senior posts of the personal data directorate, which concerns who leads the body and not what it has decided.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

TGO.short: Togo has an authority, active since 2024; no ruling against an organisation is known, and no figures it publishes are known.
TGO.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Article 55 of the 2019 data protection law creates a national authority, the IPDCP, whose president the President of the Republic appoints by decree. It became operational in 2024 under Colonel Bédiani Belei, who says it holds powers of control, injunction and sanction, and launched its activities on 28 March 2025 in Lomé.

Rulings and published figures. Its recent work is training and cooperation. It trained its first 32 data protection correspondents in June 2026, ran a first certification session on 30 September 2026 in Atakpamé, and signed a cooperation agreement with Mali's authority on 23 September 2026. It also signed a cooperation accord with the broadcast regulator on 10 December 2025. No ruling against a named organisation is held.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held. No figures the authority publishes are known.

TUN.short: Tunisia has an authority, appointed in 2021, but a 2026 report says it is at a standstill; no ruling or figures are known.
TUN.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The 2004 organic law names and defines a national authority for personal data protection, the Instance, and gives it powers over declarations, authorisations and transfers. Government decree 2021-230 of 16 April 2021 appointed twelve named members for three years, and decree 2020-312 of 15 May 2020 puts the citizen-ID register under its control and lets any person lodge an objection with it. A bill tabled in July 2025 provides for a new personal data protection authority and passes the 2004 authority's property, files and data to it.

Rulings and published figures. No ruling against an organisation and no published figures are held. In October 2026 the Forum Chawki Gaddes said the authority's activities are at a standstill and called for its reactivation.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held. No renewal of the members appointed in April 2021 for three years is held.

TZA.short: Tanzania has an authority that is working in 2026 and ruled against organisations in 2025; no published figures are known.
TZA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 6 of the Personal Data Protection Act establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as a body corporate, with a seven-member Board and a Director General. It is acting: Director General Dr Emmanuel Mkilia announced on-site inspections in Dodoma on 28 August 2026, and the Commission ran the eighth phase of its data protection officer training on 7-8 October 2026 for more than 300 participants. It certifies data protection officers under a programme launched with the Open University of Tanzania on 14 July 2026.

Rulings and published figures. On 19 August 2025 the Commission ruled in Complaint No. PDPC/CMP/002/2025 against an Instagram business-page respondent, awarding the complainant TZS 20 million, fining the respondent TZS 5 million and ordering deletion of a newborn's photos within 14 days. It also ruled in Abdul Said Naumanga v. Mi Casa Company Limited, awarding TZS 20,000,000 and ordering deletion of the complainant's personal data.

Not held. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled is held for a period ending in the last two years.

UGA.short: Uganda has an authority that is working in 2026 and ruled against Google in 2025 and WhatsApp in 2026; no published figures are known.
UGA.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Personal Data Protection Office, established under the Data Protection and Privacy Act, is headed by director Baker Birikujja, who addressed an ISACA Kampala breakfast on 18 August 2026. It briefed government IT officers on data protection on 13 August 2026. It keeps a register of data collectors, controllers and processors, and a report describes it as an independent office under NITA-U.

Rulings and published figures. On 18 July 2025 the Office found Google LLC in breach of the registration and cross-border transfer duties and ordered it to register and document its transfer compliance within 30 days. On 20 February 2026 it partly upheld the AdLegal International complaint and issued five corrective orders to WhatsApp LLC, with no fine. By letter of 17 July 2026 it confirmed that WhatsApp had carried out the measures on time.

Not held. No count of the authority's decisions, fines or complaints settled is held for a period ending in the last two years.

ZAF.short: South Africa has an authority that has fined and ruled against organisations since 2023, and it published complaint figures for 2024/25.
ZAF.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to monitor and enforce POPIA and PAIA. Its annual report for the year to 31 March 2025 describes an independent body under section 39 of POPIA that held 4 ordinary and 40 special meetings. National Treasury appropriated R135.7m for it for 2025/26. On 11 September 2026 Parliament's Justice Committee invited comment on candidates for vacant positions on it.

Rulings and published figures. The first fine, R5 million on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development, came in July 2023. It issued WhatsApp LLC an enforcement notice on 10 September 2024. On 20 May 2026 it published an enforcement notice against Central Johannesburg TVET College. A R500,000 fine on Blouberg Local Municipality was reduced to R250,000 by the Polokwane High Court in April 2026. It reports 1,355 POPIA complaints in 2024/25, 745 of them resolved.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

ZMB.short: Zambia has an authority, in post in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
ZMB.summary:
Named in law and appointed. The Data Protection Commission of Zambia is treated as an existing body in a World Bank tender dated 10 August 2026, which describes it as conducting investigations, issuing determinations and enforcing the law. Its first Data Protection Commissioner was appointed in June 2023. The Commissioner, Likando Luywa, spoke on oversight and registration of data controllers in June 2026. A Commissioner and a Deputy Commissioner took part in a September 2025 review of a draft health data statutory instrument.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner had issued regulations and guidelines and opened online registration for controllers and processors, with a 30 April 2025 deadline. No ruling against a named organisation and no published figures are held beyond that.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe has an authority, acting in 2026; no ruling against an organisation and no published figures are known.
ZWE.summary:
Named in law and appointed. Section 5 of the Cyber and Data Protection Act designates the existing Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (POTRAZ) as the Data Protection Authority, and section 6(2) says it is not subject to the direction or control of any person. It is acting: POTRAZ states it is the designated authority and has trained data protection officers. The 2024 licensing regulations have it issue licences within 14 days and keep a register of controllers.

Rulings and published figures. The nearest held fact is that POTRAZ issued Regulatory Notice 2 of 2026 on compliance inspections, which start on 1 September 2026. In June 2025 it was handing over data controller licences and planning inspections triggered by complaints and unlicensed processing. Its Business Times interview lists powers to audit, investigate, warn, direct and initiate prosecutions.

Not held. No ruling of the authority against a named organisation in the last three years is held.

AGO.short: Angola's 2011 data protection law is in force and its agency fined named companies in 2025 and 2026; a count of decisions is not known.
AGO.summary:
Authority. Lei n.º 22/11 creates the Agência de Protecção de Dados (APD) as a public-law body of seven members. Its organic statute was approved on 10 October 2016, and three board members were appointed on 6 September 2019. Its board took a sanction decision on 10 August 2026.

Standing. Lei n.º 22/11, the Lei da Protecção de Dados Pessoais, was published on 17 June 2011 and entered into force that day. On 25 June 2026 the Assembleia Nacional rejected a UNITA bill to amend it.

Regulations. Decreto Presidencial n.º 60/21 of 10 March 2021 sets the fees the APD charges for registering files and authorising processing. Decreto Presidencial n.º 214/16 approves the APD's organic statute.

Application. The APD fined Lizíria, Lda., owner of Hotel Diamante, the kwanza equivalent of USD 115,000 on 10 August 2026 for breaching articles 30 and 31 of the law. Valor Económico reported on 26 June 2026 fines of about USD 505,000 on Crescer Tech and USD 112,000 on Fast Digital Center, and fines of USD 100,000 on TAAG and USD 75,000 on Banco de Desenvolvimento de Angola, disclosed in September 2025.

Last twelve months. The law is under revision: an APD administrator said on 17 June 2026 that the public consultation was complete and the bill would go to the Assembleia Nacional in the next legislative year. On 21 April 2026 terms of reference were issued for drafting a new organic law for the APD.

Not held. No count of the APD's decisions for a stated period ending by 30 September 2026. The companies it sanctioned in June and July 2024 are not named.

BDI.short: Burundi promulgated its first personal data protection law in March 2026; no decision under it is recorded, and its commencement date is not known.
BDI.summary:
Authority. The law establishes an independent administrative authority to oversee the protection of personal data. The bill the National Assembly adopted in January 2026 makes that authority responsible for enforcement.

Standing. The National Assembly unanimously adopted a bill on personal data protection on 15 January 2026. It governs the collection and processing of personal data in the public and private sectors. The head of state promulgated the law on 10 March 2026.

Regulations. The law as the National Assembly approved it on 15 January 2026 is structured in eight chapters.

Application. The law sets up a dedicated body to implement and monitor data protection regimes.

Last twelve months. Burundi validated a National Data Governance Strategy on 7 November 2025. It adopted its first personal data protection law on 15 January 2026 and promulgated it on 10 March 2026.

Not held. The date the law takes effect, any regulation made under it and any decision taken under it. No appointment to the authority the law names is reported.

BEN.short: Benin's data protection law is in its 2018 digital code and was applied in 2025; how many regulations are in force is not known.
BEN.summary:
Authority. The Autorité de Protection des Données Personnelles (APDP) is constituted: seventeen of its officers were sworn in before the Court of First Instance of Cotonou on 14 September 2026. It succeeds the CNIL, whose members were installed in October 2010.

Standing. The data protection rules are Book V of the Code du numérique, Law no. 2017-20, promulgated on 20 April 2018. It replaced Law no. 2009-09 of 22 May 2009 and was amended by Law no. 2020-35 of 6 January 2021. In September 2026 La Nation treated the Code as the framework governing personal data processing.

Regulations. Decree 2022-107 of 16 February 2022, taken under the Code, authorises the interior ministry's national video-protection data processing. Decree 2020-187 of 11 March 2020, also taken under it, authorises the national police to collect traveller identity and fingerprint data at borders.

Application. For 2025, La Nation's account of the APDP's annual report gives 907 files examined, 793 validated, 64 inspection missions and 20 complaints treated. The authority counted 347 decisions from 2016 to 15 December 2020, among them a 2020 injunction to a controller to guarantee a complainant's right of deletion.

Last twelve months. The swearing-in of seventeen APDP officers on 14 September 2026 was done under Article 468(2) of the Code. The APDP's president spoke at a regulators' forum in Johannesburg on 1 to 3 September 2026.

Not held. How many regulations are in force under the Code, and the date the Code commenced, are not stated. The 2025 figures are held through a newspaper's account, not the APDP's report itself, and no ratification of the Malabo Convention is stated.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso has a 2021 data protection law; its commission warns and inspects, but whether any sanction has been imposed is not known.
BFA.summary:
Authority. The Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) was created by a 2004 law and has worked since December 2007. The 2021 law makes it the supervisory authority, with nine members appointed by decree. It held its sixth plenary session of the year on 26 June 2025. A bill adopted on 3 August 2026 merges the CSC and the CIL into a new regulator, ARCOD, whose first college is still to be formed.

Standing. Law n°001-2021/AN was adopted on 30 March 2021, repeals the 2004 law and gives one year from entry into force for all processing to comply. On 1 July 2025 the CIL president recalled that it makes data protection compulsory. The legislature adopted a new data protection bill on 3 August 2026.

Regulations. The 2021 law itself sets the declaration duties and the fines.

Application. By communiqué of 24 December 2024 the CIL warned that repeatedly posting people's images on social media without consent violates the law. On 26 June 2025 it validated its public report for 2024, covering compliance controls and the handling of complaints and authorisation requests. On 1 July 2025 the Prime Minister launched its awareness sessions for ministries and public institutions.

Last twelve months. The bill voted on 3 August 2026 indexes fines to turnover and bans the transfer of sensitive data abroad, and requires prior consent for commercial prospecting. The law organising ARCOD as the single authority for communications regulation and personal data protection was adopted the same day.

Not held. No regulation under the 2021 law, no named sanction and no published count of decisions or complaints. Whether the bill voted on 3 August 2026 has been promulgated is not known.

BWA.short: Botswana's Data Protection Act 2024, in force since January 2025, was applied in July 2026; whether regulations exist under it is not known.
BWA.summary:
Authority. The Information and Data Protection Commission was established in 2022, and in July 2025 its commissioner had employed three contract officers while the deputy commissioner and two director posts were unfilled. Kepaletswe Somolekae was the newly appointed commissioner in February 2026.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2024 (Act No. 18 of 2024) came into operation on 14 January 2025. It was published on 29 October 2024 and repeals the Data Protection Act No. 32 of 2018. It applies to all organisations processing personal data, public entities included.

Regulations. Statutory Instrument No. 4 of 2025, made by the Minister for State President on 13 January 2025, sets the Act's commencement date.

Application. In a public notice dated 17 July 2026 the Commission issued a Determination and an Enforcement Notice against DPSM for contraventions of the Act. It ordered the ePayslip portal suspended, and a data protection impact assessment and a revised privacy notice submitted within one month. DPSM suspended the portal on 22 July 2026.

Last twelve months. In February 2026 the new commissioner vowed firmer enforcement against non-bank financial institutions. The July 2026 notice left an administrative fine possible if DPSM did not comply.

Not held. No regulation made under the Act is held. No published count of decisions for a stated period is held.

CAF.short: A personal data protection law was adopted in 2024; no decision under it is recorded, and its commencement date is not known.
CAF.summary:
Authority. Loi n° 24.001 provides for a personal data protection agency and gives the ministry in charge of the digital economy twelve months from promulgation to set it up, with the agency's missions vested in that ministry meanwhile. Data Protection Africa stated on 28 January 2026 that the authority had not yet been appointed.

Standing. Loi n° 24.001 on the protection of personal data was adopted in mid-January 2024 and promulgated; its text gives no commencement date and no compliance period. Data Protection Africa stated on 28 January 2026 that the country has a data protection law in place.

Regulations. The law's text names no composition, seat or financing for the agency.

Application. Until the agency is set up, its missions rest with the ministry in charge of the digital economy.

Last twelve months. On 28 January 2026 Data Protection Africa recorded the authority as not yet appointed.

Not held. No regulation, decision, sanction or count of decisions under the law is held. The date the law came into force and any appointment to the agency are not held.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire has a 2013 personal data protection law, with compliance checks made in 2022; whether any controller has been sanctioned is not known.
CIV.summary:
Authority. Decree no. 2015-79 names ARTCI as the body that receives declarations, rules on authorisation requests within one month and imposes withdrawals and fines under the law. ARTCI was handling compliance and authorisation requests in July 2026.

Standing. Law no. 2013-450 of 19 June 2013 on personal data protection is the general law, and the 2015 decree made under it sets filing fees, prior authorisations and fines of up to FCFA 500 million on repeat breach. On 18 May 2026 the digital minister cited the 2013 law as the country's existing framework.

Regulations. Decree no. 2015-79 of 4 February 2015, signed by the President, sets the filing, authorisation, withdrawal and fine-recovery procedures under the law.

Application. The minister listed compliance control operations carried out in 2022 and national awareness campaigns launched from 2015. In July 2026 ARTCI was handling about 100 paper compliance and authorisation files each month.

Last twelve months. On 2 July 2026 ARTCI launched Certinum, an online platform for compliance and processing-authorisation requests, with the Treasury and ONECI the first two bodies to use it. The minister said a national register of data protection correspondents was created in 2026.

Not held. No named decision or sanction on a controller, and no published count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled for a stated year. The 2022 control operations carry no count and no sanction.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 data protection law came into force in June 2026; no decision under it is recorded, and its authority's appointment is not known.
CMR.summary:
Authority. The law defines the Autorité as an independent public body in charge of data protection and gives it supervision, notification and enforcement functions.

Standing. Cameroon's general law is Loi n° 2024/017 of 23 December 2024 on the protection of personal data. The Minister of Posts and Telecommunications told the National Assembly in April 2025 that the country had adopted it. The Ministry of Finance's budget directorate states that the deadline for its entry into force was reached on 23 June 2026 and that the law is now in force.

Regulations. The law itself sets the principles, the obligations of controllers and the rights of data subjects, as the minister described it to the Assembly.

Application. The law has been in force since 23 June 2026, and enforcement under it is a function of the Autorité.

Last twelve months. The law entered into force on 23 June 2026, which the budget directorate reported on 6 July 2026.

Not held. No regulation, decree or order made under Loi n° 2024/017 is held, and no decision, sanction or judgment applying it. No source states that the head or members of the Autorité have been appointed.

COD.short: The 2023 Digital Code, in force, covers personal data; a data protection officers' network launched in 2026; any decision under it is not known.
COD.summary:
Authority. Article 262 of the Digital Code creates an independent Autorité de protection des données with legal personality and its own budget. A ministerial order of 17 August 2024 provisionally transferred its missions to the telecommunications regulator, ARPTIC. In March 2026 the Minister of Digital Economy described the authority's creation as forthcoming.

Standing. Ordonnance-loi n° 23/010 of 13 March 2023, the Digital Code, sets the rules on the protection of personal data in its Book III. It entered into force in 2023.

Regulations. The Code provides that a Prime Minister's decree will fix the authority's organisation and functioning. On 6 August 2024 the think tank Law & Technologies called on the government to draft and sign it.

Application. On 12 March 2026 the Ministry of Digital Economy launched a national network of data protection officers in Kinshasa, to standardise personal data practice and support compliance in the public and private sectors, backed by RUDI International and Droit-Numérique.cd.

Last twelve months. The network launched in March 2026 was reported as part of plans to establish a dedicated Data Protection Authority. On 20 April 2026 the co-author of a book on personal data protection said the Code's Book III replaces the embryonic provisions of the 2020 telecommunications law.

Not held. No decision, sanction or count of decisions under the Digital Code is held, and no regulation made under it. No source shows the authority constituted, or ARPTIC acting in its place.

COG.short: Congo has a 2019 personal data protection law with a commission inaugurated in January 2026; whether decisions have been made under it is not known.
COG.summary:
Authority. The National Personal Data Protection Commission was inaugurated after its members were appointed under Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025, as reported on 22 January 2026.

Standing. Congo's general law is Law No. 29-2019 of 10 October 2019 on personal data protection. It was in force in January 2026, when the Commission it provides for was inaugurated.

Regulations. Decree No. 2025-538 of 31 December 2025 completes the institutional framework the law established, by appointing the Commission's members.

Application. The Commission elected its President, Vice President and Rapporteur at its inaugural meeting, reported in January 2026.

Last twelve months. The Commission's members were appointed by decree of 31 December 2025 and the Commission was inaugurated with its leadership elected, reported on 22 January 2026.

Not held. Whether any regulation made under Law No. 29-2019 is in force, and any decision, sanction or count of complaints under the law. The date the law commenced.

COM.short: Comoros enacted a personal data protection law in 2021; no decision under it is on record, and whether it is in force is not known.
COM.summary:
Authority. The law institutes a supervisory body, which its Article 19 names the Commission nationale de l'informatique et des libertés, with nine members. As of mid-2024 the authority had not been formally constituted or made operational.

Standing. The Assembly of the Union adopted Loi n°14-029/AU on the protection of personal data, in 68 articles, in plenary session on 26 June 2014. The Union of Comoros enacted its Protection of Personal Data Law on 29 June 2021, as a comprehensive framework.

Regulations. Under Article 24 of the law, the nine members of the commission are named by decree.

Application. The authority that the law gives the task of supervision was not operational as of mid-2024.

Last twelve months. The latest dated position is that of mid-2024, when the authority had not been formally constituted.

Not held. Whether the law has commenced, and from what date, is not held, nor is any regulation made under it or any decision applying it. Nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held, including whether the authority has been constituted since mid-2024.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's 2001 data protection law, last amended in 2021, is in force and cases reach its authority; whether any was decided is not known.
CPV.summary:
Authority. The Comissão Nacional de Protecção de Dados (CNPD) began work in 2015–2016 and completed a decade in 2025, under its president, Faustino Varela. The National Assembly's own budget gave it CVE 36,313,115 for 2025, with no revenue of its own.

Standing. Law 133/V/2001 is the general data protection regime, applying within the country and to the processing of data of people located in it. The CNPD's president dates the base law to 2001 and says the commission has worked from it since 2015–2016.

Regulations. The law was amended in 2013 and again in 2021: the first amendment led to the CNPD being set up, and the second added the obligation to appoint a data protection officer.

Application. The CNPD's president said in February 2025 that cases involving artificial intelligence and big data have reached the commission, among them two of images manipulated with generative AI and a first image-manipulation case in 2021. Cases that may be criminal are sent to the Ministério Público.

Last twelve months. In March 2025 the CNPD held an international conference on personal data protection for its tenth anniversary, opened by the Prime Minister.

Not held. Whether any regulation has been made under the law, and any dated decision, sanction or published count of decisions under it. Nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026.

DJI.short: Djibouti enacted a data protection law in June 2025; no decision under it is recorded, and its start date is not known.
DJI.summary:
Authority. The Digital Code's data-protection regime creates the National Commission for the Protection of Personal Data (CNDP), independent and with administrative and financial autonomy. Jones Day reported at the National Assembly's vote that the competent authorities were still to be operationalised.

Standing. The National Assembly passed Djibouti's first Digital Code on 30 June 2025, with a data-protection regime embedded in it, to be promulgated by the President and published in the Journal Officiel. TechHive Advisory states that the regime was enacted in June 2025.

Regulations. The data-protection regime runs to 156 articles and sits within the Digital Code.

Application. The Code's embedded data-protection regime establishes the CNDP, as reported at the Assembly's vote on 30 June 2025.

Last twelve months. TechHive Advisory, writing on 5 November 2025, described the regime as enacted in June 2025 and the commission as created by it.

Not held. The date the Code was promulgated or came into force, and whether the CNDP has been constituted or its members appointed. No regulation under the law, no decision under it and no event in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 is held.

DZA.short: Algeria's 2018 data protection law has been in force since 2023 and its authority issues rules; whether any controller has been sanctioned is not known.
DZA.summary:
Authority. The Autorité nationale de protection des données à caractère personnel (ANPDP) adopted a deliberation by a majority of its members on 15 July 2026, signed by its president. Samir Bourehil was its president in July 2026. It issues authorisations and receives declarations of processing.

Standing. Law n° 18-07 of 10 June 2018 came into force on 10 August 2023, the US International Trade Administration states. Law 25-11, promulgated in July 2025, amended it, adding duties to appoint a data protection delegate, keep a processing register and log automated operations. The law was in force in July 2026.

Regulations. Délibération n° 04 of 15 July 2026, in eleven articles, sets conditions for processing and publishing images and recordings of natural persons. In the months before it the ANPDP published rules on workplace video surveillance and on appointing data protection delegates. A compliance package of guidelines and four templates was released in 2025.

Application. The authority decided in January or February 2026 that a positive or negative test result alone is standard health data, so employers need no prior authorisation. It runs an online complaint service for data subjects, and by December 2025 it had held its first study day and a series of training meetings with national bodies.

Last twelve months. Délibération n° 04 treats publication on foreign-run platforms as a transfer abroad. A study day at the national police college in July 2026 announced a unified guide for administrative, security and judicial procedures.

Not held. No decision or sanction on a named controller is held. No count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled is published for a stated period.

EGY.short: Egypt's personal data protection law dates from 2020; its authority has issued guidance, but whether any decision has been made under it is not known.
EGY.summary:
Authority. The supervisory authority is the Personal Data Protection Center, which the executive regulations confirm as responsible for implementation, monitoring and enforcement. In November 2025 it was run by an acting chief executive, Soussan El-Okbawy, who chaired a session at Cairo ICT on 16 November.

Standing. Egypt's general law is the Personal Data Protection Law, Law No. 151 of 2020, which the Cairo Review treated in June 2025 as the country's operating data protection law. Access Partnership said in February 2026 that enforcement is expected from 1 November 2026, the end of a one-year grace period.

Regulations. The executive regulations were still pending in February 2025. They were issued by ministerial decree on 1 November 2025 as Executive Regulations No. 816/2025.

Application. In January and February 2026 the Personal Data Protection Center published guidelines on consent, lawful bases, direct marketing, data protection officers, records of processing, licences and permits and privacy notices, with templates for notifying a breach.

Last twelve months. The executive regulations were issued on 1 November 2025, and the Center's guidelines followed in January and February 2026.

Not held. No sanction, order or decision on a named controller under the law, and no published count of cases settled. The date the law came into force is not held either.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no data protection law as of 2026 and no supervisory authority; whether a bill is being drafted is not known.
ERI.summary:
Authority. No supervisory authority has been established in Eritrea, as of 1 August 2026. The Horn of Africa Initiative's update of June 2025 recorded the country as without regulatory oversight for data protection, while Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia had supervisory authorities.

Standing. Eritrea has no comprehensive data protection law in force, as of 1 August 2026. The Horn of Africa Initiative's update of June 2025 placed it at a nascent stage, without data protection legislation, and a UNECA country profile published in 2022 said it lacked a comprehensive legal framework for data protection.

Regulations. No comprehensive data protection law is in force, as of 1 August 2026.

Application. No enforcement decisions are published and none could be found, as of 1 August 2026.

Last twelve months. The position was unchanged at 1 August 2026: no law, no regulator and no enforcement.

Not held. No bill or draft of a data protection law is on record, and whether one is in preparation is not held. Nothing is held on regulations.

ETH.short: A personal data protection proclamation was published in 2024 and its regulator approved about 10 data transfers by 2025; decisions against controllers are not known.
ETH.summary:
Authority. The proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator. In November 2025 the Authority, whose mandate was extended from telecom regulation to data protection, was enforcing the law and expanding its staffing and technical capacity, its Director General Balcha Reba said.

Standing. Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024, the country's first comprehensive personal data protection law, was approved on 4 April 2024 and published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024. It took effect on publication.

Regulations. In November 2025 four directives were expected to be approved in the coming months, and delays in issuing them had slowed implementation.

Application. The Director General said in November 2025 that the Authority had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and approved them as a temporary measure, and that data processors and collectors now need its permission.

Last twelve months. At a workshop co-hosted with Huawei in November 2025, Authority officials previewed a digital portal for registering data controllers and processors.

Not held. No sanction or order on a named controller is held, and no published count of decisions for a stated period. No directive under the proclamation is held as approved.

GAB.short: Gabon has a 2011 data protection law, last amended in 2023, and its authority fined a bank in 2024; whether regulations exist is not known.
GAB.summary:
Authority. The Autorité pour la Protection des Données Personnelles et de la Vie Privée (APDPVP) is created by article 7 of Loi n°025/2023 as an independent administrative authority. Its commissioners were appointed by a Council of Ministers decision of 12 July 2023 and its bureau was elected on 6 September 2023. Its president gave an interview as head of the authority in September 2026.

Standing. Gabon's data protection law is Loi n°001/2011, amended by ordinance in 2020 and again by Loi n°025/2023 of 12 July 2023, published in the Journal Officiel on 15 July 2023 with no grace period for compliance. The authority applied it as law in force in April 2024.

Regulations. Loi n°025/2023 was promulgated by Décret n°166/PR.

Application. On 25 April 2024 the authority's plenary fined Citibank Gabon S.A. 90,000,000 FCFA for diverting employee data from its declared purpose and processing data on ethnic origin, with a formal notice of two months. The decision answered a complaint of 27 November 2023.

Last twelve months. On 20 January 2026 the authority supervised the destruction of the personal data of unsuccessful 2022 bidders held by the public procurement directorate. It accompanied a data centre project for several months before commissioning, reported in June 2026. Its president said in September 2026 that it had logged about 715 declarations of conformity, issued about 50 reasoned opinions and received about 30 complaints from individuals.

Not held. Whether any regulations have been issued under Loi n°025/2023. The authority's counts carry no year or period, and nothing dated in the twelve months to 30 September 2026 shows the law being strengthened or weakened.

GHA.short: Ghana has the Data Protection Act of 2012, applied by a court against a company in 2024; whether regulations exist under it is not known.
GHA.summary:
Authority. The Data Protection Commission is established under the Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) and enforces it. The Minister for Communication swore in a new Governing Board, chaired by Teki Akuetteh, reported on 1 August 2025. In August 2026 the Commission operated only from its head office.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2012 (Act 843) is in force: a circuit court treated its sections 17 to 30 and 43 as binding on a data processor on 18 September 2024, and in February 2026 the Minister for Communication called on all institutions that process personal data to comply with it.

Regulations. Amendments to the Act are in process and a draft Data Protection Act, 2025 has been published, according to a roundup by Digital Policy Alert and Tech Hive Advisory of 11 January 2026.

Application. On 18 September 2024 Circuit Court 2, Adentan, Accra found Bolt Holdings OU in breach of sections 20, 21, 28 and 30 of the Act over a driver profile registered with the plaintiff's stolen identity, and awarded GHC1,900,000 in compensation and GHC20,000 in costs. The Commission reported that in 2025 it conducted compliance audits across several sectors and expanded registrations of data controllers.

Last twelve months. In January 2026 the Commission announced that 2026 would be a year of enforcement. The Minister reported that in January to June 2026 its regulatory activity rose 51.5 per cent and newly registered data controllers rose 98.4 per cent.

Not held. No regulation made under the Act is held, and no source says there is none. No published count of decisions, sanctions or complaints settled in a stated year is held.

GIN.short: Guinea has a 2016 cybersecurity and personal data protection law with no decision under it on record; its commencement date is not known.
GIN.summary:
Authority. The 2016 law defines an Autorité de Protection and names no constituted body or appointed members. On 20 June 2024 the CNT's commissions debated a bill to establish the Autorité de Protection des Données à caractère Personnel, with the designation of members and their mandates contested and plenary adoption pending.

Standing. Loi L/2016/037/AN on cybersecurity and personal data protection was adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by President Alpha Condé in 2016, and covers personal data processing by individuals, companies and public institutions. Part Two of the text is a full personal data protection regime.

Regulations. Article 5 of the law sends processing declarations to the competent authority "designated by regulation".

Application. The law gives the Autorité de Protection the functions of receiving declarations, granting authorisations, approving transfers, investigating and issuing guidelines.

Last twelve months. On 19 November 2025 Minister Rose Pola Pricemou said Guinea is strengthening its regulatory framework with a new data-protection law.

Not held. The date the 2016 law came into force, any regulation made under it, any decision applying it and the constitution of its authority. The stage and timetable of the new law announced in November 2025.

GMB.short: The Gambia enacted its first general data protection law in 2025; no decision under it is on record and its commencement date is not known.
GMB.summary:
Authority. The Act establishes an independent oversight Commission. A notice published on 17 August 2026 has the Information Commission of The Gambia preparing a communication strategy to raise awareness of the Access to Information Act, 2021 and the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act, 2025.

Standing. The National Assembly passed the Personal Data Protection and Privacy Bill 2025 in its Third Ordinary Session, and President Barrow assented to the Act on 7 November 2025. It is the country's first comprehensive data protection law and has no grace period before it becomes enforceable.

Regulations. In February 2026 regulations and guidance under the Act, on research purposes, the income base for fines and transfers, were still to be issued.

Application. Paradigm Initiative called in January 2026 for the relevant authorities to implement and enforce the law.

Last twelve months. Parliament's passage of the bill was reported on 6 October 2025, when it awaited presidential assent, and assent followed on 7 November 2025.

Not held. The date the Act commenced is not stated, and no source says the Commission's members have been appointed. No decision, sanction or count of complaints under the Act is on record.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau has no data protection law; a bill was awaiting discussion in parliament in 2025, and whether it has advanced since is not known.
GNB.summary:
Authority. Guinea-Bissau has no dedicated national data protection authority, a professor at the Bissau Faculty of Law said on 22 September 2026.

Standing. The country does not yet have specific data protection legislation, the same speaker said. The government's national report to the Universal Periodic Review, published on 18 February 2025, lists a personal data protection bill among several awaiting discussion in the National People's Assembly.

Regulations. The bill leaves the organisation of the body it would create to a decree.

Application. Data protection matters are handled by several institutions, sector by sector.

Last twelve months. At an ECOWAS Court conference in Dakar on 22 September 2026, the professor said the bill provides for what it calls a "Data Protection Agency", and that its membership puts its independence at risk.

Not held. No law is enacted, and where the bill stands is not known: nothing shows it has moved since it was reported as awaiting discussion in 2025. Nothing is held on regulations or on any decision.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea has had a personal data protection law since 2016; whether it has been applied, or its supervisory body created, is not known.
GNQ.summary:
Authority. Articles 15 and 29 of the law name the Órgano Rector de Protección de Datos Personales as the supervisory body, with a Secretaría Técnica and a Registro General under it. The law states that the body is to be created by a decree that will fix its structure.

Standing. Ley Núm. 1/2016, de Protección de Datos Personales, was sanctioned and promulgated by the President on 22 July 2016. It sets rules for the processing of personal data in the public and private sectors, and enters into force twenty days after its publication in the Boletín Oficial del Estado.

Regulations. The law leaves the structure of the Órgano Rector to a decree.

Application. The law places the power to sanction with the Minister of Telecommunications and New Technologies.

Last twelve months. The law in force is the one dated 22 July 2016.

Not held. Whether the decree creating the Órgano Rector was issued, whether any regulation was made under the law, and whether any decision or sanction has been taken under it. Nothing dated after 22 July 2016 is held.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2019 Data Protection Act is in force and its commissioner has fined businesses; the number of decisions in any one year is not known.
KEN.summary:
Authority. The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner was established under the Data Protection Act, 2019, and its first commissioner has been in office since 2020. In March 2025 it had offices in Nairobi, Kisumu, Mombasa, Eldoret, Machakos, Nyeri and Nakuru.

Standing. The Data Protection Act, 2019 is in force. The ICT Cabinet Secretary told the Senate in May 2026 that the Act is being enforced, and the office has issued fines under it since 2022.

Regulations. The Data Protection (Registration of Data Controllers and Data Processors) Regulations, 2021 are in force under the Act. They set 24-month registration certificates and make processing on an expired certificate an offence.

Application. As at September 2024 the office had fined at least nine businesses a total of KES 26,275,000. Its bulletin states that by March 2025 it had issued 215 determinations and imposed penalties on 10 entities.

Last twelve months. In August 2026 the office published a draft guidance note on transfers of personal data to offshore AI providers. On 28 August 2026 it gave holders of expired registration certificates until 11 September 2026 to renew or face enforcement.

Not held. No count of decisions or sanctions for a single stated year: the figures to March 2025 are cumulative. The date the Act commenced is not given.

LBR.short: Liberia approved a data protection act in March 2026; it has no recorded decision, and whether the Commissioner has begun acting is not known.
LBR.summary:
Authority. The Act confers data protection functions on the Independent Information Commissioner, the oversight body created by the Freedom of Information Act of 2010.

Standing. The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act of 2024 was approved on 9 March 2026 and printed on 23 March 2026. It takes effect on publication into handbills, and existing businesses have one year from the effective date to comply. President Boakai's promulgation of the law was announced on 19 August 2026.

Regulations. The Act requires implementing rules within 24 months of its taking effect.

Application. The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection said on 13 September 2026 that it is aware of its responsibilities under the Act, and that it took part in validating the legal framework.
