ZAF.summary:
Rule in force. South Africa's Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA) prohibits transfers of personal information outside the country unless the recipient is under adequate legal protection, the data subject consents, or a contract or the data subject's interest requires the transfer. The Act took effect in July 2020, with a grace period to 30 June 2021, so the rule has applied in full since mid-2021. It is a single statutory rule covering every responsible party that sends personal information out of South Africa, and the conditions for a lawful transfer are set out in the Act itself.

Means of complying published and rule applied. An article published on 17 January 2024 states that POPIA does not name the countries with adequate protection and creates no mechanism for the regulator to recognise such countries. On that account the party sending the data has to judge adequacy for itself, case by case, since the Act supplies no approved list to rely on.

Not held. No source held says the Information Regulator has published a list of countries, model contract terms, a permission procedure or guidance on sending data abroad.

ZMB.short: Zambia's Data Protection Act, passed in 2021, sets conditions for sending personal data abroad; whether it has come into effect is not known.
ZMB.summary:
Rule in force. Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, enacted on 24 March 2021, sets the conditions for sending personal data outside the Republic in Part X, sections 70 and 71. The Act says it commences on a date the Minister appoints by statutory instrument, and the published text gives no date.

Means of complying published and rule applied. The Act sets out three routes. The first is the data subject's consent together with standard contracts or intragroup schemes approved by the Commissioner. The second is a transfer to a country the Minister has prescribed, on a test of an adequate level of protection. The third is a transfer the Commissioner approves where it is necessary, case by case.

Not held. No source held says a rule on sending personal data abroad is in force.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's data protection authority issued a transfer rule in 2024 and reported 24 authorisations by 2025; which organisations and destinations is not known.
ZWE.summary:
Rule in force. On 13 November 2024 POTRAZ, the designated data protection authority, issued guideline CDPG 5 of 2024 under sections 6(1)(a) and 28(3) of the Cyber and Data Protection Act. It took effect on publication and bars data controllers from sending personal data abroad unless they have notified the Authority and met stated conditions: an impact assessment, the data subject's consent, adequate protection in the destination country and a data-sharing agreement.

Means of complying published and rule applied. The same guideline sets out the notification, impact assessment, consent, adequacy and agreement steps, includes a letter requesting prior authorisation from the Authority, and gives a contact address for complaints and guidance. In a report published on 26 December 2025, POTRAZ said 24 cross-border transfers of personal data have been authorised.

Not held. The dates of the 24 authorisations, the organisations that received them and the countries data went to are not held. No list of approved destination countries or model contract terms is held.

AGO.short: Angola's identity law, amended in 2017 and 2021, gives each citizen a unique number on a chip card. No rules since 2023 are known.
AGO.summary:
Law in force. Angola's identity card rests on Lei n.º 4/09, the law on civil identification and the issue of the citizen's identity card. The National Assembly amended it in August 2017 and again in January 2021, each amendment in force on publication. On 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers reviewed a civil and criminal identification bill that would gather the rules on the identity card and criminal records into one law.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law as amended gives each identity card a number that acts in law as the unique citizen number, and the card carries an encrypted QR code. Since 2017 the card has also carried a microprocessor holding the holder's tax, social security, birth-record and voter numbers, so that it can be read by public and private institutions.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

BDI.short: Burundi's identity card runs on ministerial orders of 1978 and 1986; in 2026 the texts for a national identification file were still to be adopted.
BDI.summary:
Law in force. Burundi's identity card runs on two ministerial ordinances, of 1978 and 1986, with no law behind them. The government's procedures page for the card lists those ordinances as its main texts and names no identity law. The page is held as published in January 2026 and says further texts remain to be adopted before the national identification file is instituted.

Digital identity covered and rules made. With no law in force, none provides for a digital identity. The same page says the national identification file still awaits its instituting texts, and the card it describes rests on the two ordinances alone. Burundi therefore answers the first question only: an identity system run on orders, with the texts for its register still to be adopted.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

BEN.short: Benin's 2017 identification law, amended in 2025, sets up a biometric register and a personal number. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
BEN.summary:
Law in force. Benin's law no. 2017-08 of 19 June 2017 on the identification of natural persons is the law behind the national register and the personal identification number. In June 2025 the National Assembly adopted law no. 2025-12 amending its article 6, extending who the law covers, and the 2017 law stands as amended.

Digital identity covered and rules made. Article 6 as amended provides for a national biometric population register and a personal identification number for each person entered in it. The 2025 amendment adds special numbers for foreigners and for naturalised persons of African descent, so the register and the number now reach beyond citizens. The number is the one each person keeps for life in the register. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's assembly adopted a unique electronic identification bill in October 2024. Whether it has been promulgated is not known.
BFA.summary:
Law in force. Burkina Faso's transitional legislative assembly adopted the bill on unique electronic identification of the natural person on 11 October 2024. On 19 August 2025 the minister for digital transition said the law had been adopted the previous year. Neither source says the law has been promulgated.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The adopted text underpins a system giving each resident a random unique identifier, issued against biographic data, fingerprints and iris, and linked to the national identity card, the passport, the driving licence, the patient file and the bank account. Until a source says the law is promulgated, that provision is a bill's and not a law's. The identifier is to be issued once to each resident and kept for life, by the text as reported in October 2024.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

BWA.short: Botswana's 1986 National Registration Act, amended in 2025, is in force. Whether it provides for a digital identity is not known.
BWA.summary:
Law in force. Botswana's National Registration Act commenced on 31 December 1986 and has been amended up to 2017; it has the Registrar of National Registration keep a national register of citizens aged 16 or over and issue identity cards. The National Registration (Amendment) Act, 2025 followed: in July 2026 the minister told Parliament what it changes.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2025 amendment lets a passport or a driving licence serve as identification while a defaced, lost or expired identity card is being replaced. That is the newest change to the law on record. The Act itself provides for the national register and the card, and the minister described the amendment in March 2026 as now in effect. No other change to the Act since 2017 is on record.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

CAF.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for the Central African Republic, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
CAF.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's 2019 law on digital identification is the basis of its biometric identity card. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
CIV.summary:
Law in force. Côte d'Ivoire's biometric identity project is backed by the Law on Digital Identification, no. 2019-566, an enacted law of five articles. A 2025 study of ten African identity systems records the law with an executive decree and the 2013 data protection law alongside it, and treats the three together as the legal basis of the system.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The same study says the 2019 law establishes the legal basis for the biometric digital identity and that its second article describes the identity document as a secure card serving several applications. It is the one law in the country's framework that the study names as written for the digital identity itself, and it is short: five articles in all. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

CMR.short: Cameroon's 2024 civil registration law provides a unique personal identification number for every citizen. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
CMR.summary:
Law in force. Cameroon's Law 2024/016, the new civil registration law, is the law the national civil status office is implementing, as reported in October 2025. It is an ordinary law of 2024 and replaces the earlier civil registration regime. The report describes the office as working under it, with the registers being moved onto digital systems.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law authorises digital birth, marriage and death certificates and a unique personal identification number for every citizen. The number is the part of the law that makes it an identity law as well as a civil registration one: each citizen is to hold one number, issued from the civil register, and the certificates drawn from that register may be digital. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

COD.short: The DRC's population file rests on a 2022 decree; a bill on identifying persons was tabled in parliament in June 2026.
COD.summary:
Law in force. The Democratic Republic of the Congo's population file was created by the Prime Minister's decree no. 22/07 of 2 March 2022, with no identity law among its legal bases. On 12 June 2026 two deputies tabled a private member's bill on the general rules for identifying natural persons, which is to go to committee.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No law is in force. The 2022 decree gives the population file a national identification number and biometric data and puts the national identification office in charge of it, on the strength of a decree alone. The bill tabled in June 2026 describes the present arrangements as resting on decrees, which is what it sets out to change. The bill had not been debated by the end of September 2026.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

COG.short: Congo's identification number and identity card rest on decrees of 2004 and 2009, the latter amended in 2024; no identity law is known.
COG.summary:
Law in force. The Republic of the Congo's unique identification number was instituted by decree no. 2004-469 of 3 November 2004, and no law is named behind it. The national identity card rests on a 2009 decree, which decree no. 2024-2692 of 13 November 2024 amended. Both instruments are decrees.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No law is in force, so the rules that follow are made under decrees. An order of 12 March 2020 added the capture of iris and fingerprints to the identification number, and an order of 12 October 2022 made the number mandatory for eight economic transactions and five administrative formalities. The 2024 decree provides a card holding both thumbprints. No bill for an identity law is on record.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

COM.short: The Comoros's 2014 law institutes a biometric identity card. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
COM.summary:
Law in force. The Comoros has a law instituting its identity card: law no. 14-023/AU of 24 June 2014, promulgated by decree no. 14-137/PR. The decree is held from the Ministry of Justice's site, which lists it as the instrument that brought the law into force. The law is an act of the Assembly of the Union.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Ministry of Justice describes the 2014 law as instituting the Comorian digital, biometric identity card. That description, in the title under which the ministry publishes the promulgating decree, is what is held on the law's content: it is a law for a biometric card, and the ministry calls the card digital. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record. The card it institutes is the national identity card Comorians hold.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde's 2013 law and 2014 decree-law set up an electronic identity card; the last rules known under them date from 2017.
CPV.summary:
Law in force. Cabo Verde's national civil identification and authentication system was created by Lei n.º 43/VIII/2013 of 17 September 2013. The national identification card was then created by Decreto-Lei n.º 19/2014 of 17 March, which also governs its issue, replacement, use and cancellation. The card was launched on 23 January 2018.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The card is an electronic one whose chip holds a digital certificate and applications for identification, authentication and digital signature. Rules were made under the decree-law in 2017: Portaria n.º 21/2017 of 15 June regulates the capture of biometric data and Portaria n.º 35/2017 of 2 September sets how long the card is valid. Those rules all date from before September 2023, and none made under the law since then is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

DJI.short: Djibouti's 2019 identification law sets up a unique number and biometric register; the last rules known under it date from 2020.
DJI.summary:
Law in force. Djibouti's law no. 39/AN/19 on the identification of natural persons was published on 21 January 2019. It creates the national identification number and the national register of natural persons, which the population directorate runs. A decree of 13 July 2020 was made under its article 9.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law creates a unique national identification number and a central register of biographic and biometric data, the single reference for the identity card and travel documents. Decree no. 2020-150 sets the number's composition and requires administrations, hospitals, schools, utilities and traders to carry it on their documents. A second 2020 decree governs access to the register. Those rules all date from before September 2023, and none made under the law since then is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

DZA.short: Algeria's law of February 2026 sets rules for electronic identification tied to the biometric identity card. No rules made under it are known.
DZA.summary:
Law in force. Algeria's Council of Ministers approved a draft law on trust services and digital identification on 2 November 2025. It became law no. 26-02 of 17 February 2026, which fixes the general rules on trust services for electronic transactions and on electronic identification and is published by the ministry of post and telecommunications.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law sets the rules for electronic identification. Reports on its draft say it introduces a national digital identification framework built on the existing biometric identity card and updates the 2015 electronic signature law. The identity it provides for is therefore one that is checked electronically, tied to the card citizens already hold. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

EGY.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for Egypt, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

ERI.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for Eritrea, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's 2023 Digital Identification Proclamation sets up a biometric identity database. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
ETH.summary:
Law in force. Ethiopia's Digital Identification Proclamation, no. 1284/2023, was signed by the President on 18 April 2023 and came into force on its publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette. It is a proclamation of the federal parliament, written for the digital identity and for nothing else, and it is the law the identity system runs under.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The proclamation sets up a digital identification system that collects demographic and biometric data in a central database. The system it describes is digital from the start: a person is enrolled with biometric data and identified from the central database. The proclamation's second article sets out the terms the rest of the text relies on. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

GAB.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for Gabon, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GAB.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

GHA.short: Ghana's identity Acts of 2006 and 2008 are in force; 2026 regulations require biometric verification against the national register.
GHA.summary:
Law in force. Ghana's identity system rests on two Acts of Parliament that the National Identification Authority lists as its laws: the National Identification Authority Act, 2006 and the National Identity Register Act, 2008. The Authority is the statutory body the 2006 Act set up to create and maintain the national identity register.

Digital identity covered and rules made. Regulations made under the 2008 Act, gazetted on 27 March 2026 and in force from 9 June 2026, require organisations to verify identity through the Authority's biometric verification system, in real time against its database. An earlier notice under the same laws, of 15 February 2024, specifies the portable card readers that may be used. The 2026 regulations amend the register regulations of 2012.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2023 law on identifying persons is in force; in 2026 its applying decrees were still drafts. Whether it covers digital identity is not known.
GIN.summary:
Law in force. Guinea has a law on the identification of physical persons, numbered L/2023/0019. On 26 February 2026 the head of the identification office named it at a workshop where officials said the country now has two new laws, on identification and on civil status. The minister's declaration of 10 August 2026 lists their adoption and dissemination among the year's achievements.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The rules to apply the law are still drafts. A workshop at Kindia from 12 to 17 January 2026 reviewed and validated draft decrees and orders applying the identification law and the civil status law. A validated draft is not yet a rule, and what the law provides for the identity itself is not stated in these reports.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

GMB.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for The Gambia, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GMB.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

GNB.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for Guinea-Bissau, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

GNQ.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for Equatorial Guinea, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

KEN.short: Kenya's digital identity system rests on a 2018 executive order and 2020 regulations, added to a 1947 act; it has no law of its own.
KEN.summary:
Law in force. Kenya has no stand-alone digital identity law. Its digital identity system, the National Integrated Identity Management System, began under executive order no. 1 of 2018, in which the president directed a central master population database to be built. The government then wrote the system into the 1947 Registration of Persons Act by an omnibus amendment, and no Act of its own was passed for it. The High Court ruled in January 2020 that an appropriate and comprehensive regulatory framework should be enacted before the system was rolled out.

Digital identity covered and rules made. With no identity law of its own in force, none provides for a digital identity. The system is anchored on the Huduma Namba regulations of 2020, and civil society organisations objected that regulations cannot create a system of that weight. The inserted section 9A has the system keep a national population register and assign each person a unique number. Kenya therefore answers the first question only.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2011 National Identification Registry Act sets up a biometric identification system. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
LBR.summary:
Law in force. Liberia's National Identification Registry Act was approved by the President on 1 August 2011 and published on 8 August 2011. It repeals a 1983 decree that had established the earlier identification system and sets up the National Identification Registry as the body in charge. The Act took effect on publication.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act sets up a National Biometric Identification System and a biometric card for each person, enrolled with a fingerprint and a photograph. The Registry the Act creates is the body that runs that system. The Act is therefore a law for a biometric identity from its first day, and no later amendment to it is on record. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

LBY.short: Libya's 2014 national number law gives each citizen a unique number in a biometric database. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
LBY.summary:
Law in force. Libya's Law No. 8 of 2014 on the National Number was issued by the General National Congress on 24 March 2014 and took effect on issue. It sets up the national number and a national database, run with the Civil Registry Authority. It is an ordinary law and no amendment to it is on record.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law provides for a twelve-digit national number unique to each citizen and a national database completed with ten fingerprints, an iris print, a photograph and a signature. The number and the biometric database are both in the law's own articles, the second and the third, and the database is the reference the number is checked against. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2011 identity cards law, in force since 2013, sets up a biometric register and unique number. No rules since 2023 are known.
LSO.summary:
Law in force. Lesotho's National Identity Cards Act, 2011 was published in the Government Gazette on 21 March 2011 and commenced on 1 July 2013. It repealed the National Identity Cards Act, 2004. It is an Act of Parliament and has been the law for the identity register and the card since its commencement.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act establishes a National Identity Register that records fingerprints and an image for everyone aged sixteen and over. It assigns each entry a unique national identity number and provides for an identity card with a chip that holds the fingerprints. The register, the number and the chip card are all set out in the Act itself. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MAR.short: Morocco's 2020 law creates a population register against which identity is checked online. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
MAR.summary:
Law in force. Morocco's law no. 72-18, on the targeting of beneficiaries of social support programmes, was promulgated on 8 August 2020 and published in the Bulletin officiel on 7 January 2021. It creates the national population register and the national registers agency that runs it. It is a statute and no bill to replace it is on record.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law's second article defines authentication as checking declared data online and in real time against the national population register. An identity entered in the register is therefore one that can be checked electronically, which is what the law provides the register for. The register and the agency are the law's two creations. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MDG.short: Madagascar's parliament passed an identification law in July 2025 and the constitutional court cleared it. Whether it has been promulgated is not known.
MDG.summary:
Law in force. Madagascar's law no. 2025-019 on the identification of natural persons was adopted by the National Assembly on 3 July 2025 and the Senate on 4 July 2025. The President referred it for review before promulgation, and on 26 August 2025 the High Constitutional Court ruled that it conforms to the Constitution.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No source says the law has been promulgated, so it is counted as passed and not yet in force. The court's decision is the last step on record: a law adopted by both houses, referred on 28 July 2025 and cleared a month later. What the law provides for the identity itself is not stated in the decision. The law is numbered 2025-019 and carries the year of its adoption.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

MLI.short: Mali's 2006 law gives each person a unique identification number; the last rule known under it is a decree of November 2022.
MLI.summary:
Law in force. Mali's law no. 06-040 of 11 August 2006 institutes the national identification number and a national identification register. It was adopted by the National Assembly on 13 July 2006 and promulgated by the President. A decree of 3 November 2022 instituting the biometric national identity card cites it as its basis.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The law gives each person a unique number held in a national register, to be shown on the identity card, the passport and civil status records. A decree of 18 October 2006 fixes the fourteen-digit number and obliges public services to use it. The 2022 decree requires the number for any biometric identity card application. Those rules all date from before September 2023, and none made under the law since then is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MOZ.short: A civil identification and identity card bill passed first reading in March 2022; whether it became law is not known.
MOZ.summary:
Law in force. On 16 March 2022 the Assembly of the Republic approved in first reading, by consensus, the Council of Ministers' bill setting the legal regime for civil identification and the national citizen identity card, the Bilhete de Identidade. The bill is meant to replace colonial-era legislation.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The nearest held fact is the same bill, which covers civil identification and the citizen identity card. The existing biometric card, the Bilhete de Identidade, dates from Decree 11/2008 of 29 April. In May 2026 a tender was launched for a consultancy on a mobile digital identity and signature system, and a partner was being sought for a mobile digital ID and e-signature rollout. The Interior Ministry's national directorate of civil identification runs an electronic civil identity system, described in a March 2023 document.

Not held. No source says a national identity law is in force.

MRT.short: Mauritania's civil status code, amended in February 2025, provides for a national biometric population register. No rules made under it since are known.
MRT.summary:
Law in force. Mauritania's identity system rests on its Civil Status Code, law no. 2011-003 of 12 January 2011, which covers the national population register and secure identity documents. Law no. 2025-011 of 24 February 2025 replaced three of its articles after adoption by the National Assembly and promulgation by the President.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The code as amended provides for the national biometric population register in its new article 31. Its new article 15 provides for applications for secure identity documents, and for digital civil status acts, through information systems the administration adopts. The 2025 amendment is thus the text that writes the biometric register and digital acts into the code. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

MUS.short: Mauritius's 1985 identity card law is in force; 2024 regulations under it set a new card with a digital seal and fingerprints.
MUS.summary:
Law in force. Mauritius's identity card rests on the National Identity Card Act, No. 60 of 1985, which the identity card unit lists as the law behind the card system. The Act is an Act of Parliament, and regulations made under its section 10 came into operation on 19 February 2024, when the new card began to be issued.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The National Identity Card Regulations 2024 were made by the minister on 16 February 2024. They set the new identity card, its digital seal and an application made with fingerprints, and they revoke the regulations of 2013. Through them the 1985 Act now provides for a card that is biometric and can be checked electronically. The new card has been issued since 19 February 2024.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

MWI.short: Malawi's National Registration Act is in force and was under review in 2026. Whether it provides for a digital identity is not known.
MWI.summary:
Law in force. Malawi's National Registration Act is in force: on 23 July 2026 the Homeland Security Minister made amendment regulations under it, and the registration bureau runs the national identity card under the Act. In July 2026 a stakeholders' meeting was held to review the Act under the Digital Malawi Acceleration Project.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act is being reviewed and has not been replaced. The meeting reported in July 2026 brought stakeholders together as the bureau reviews the registration laws, and no bill has followed on record. The regulations of 23 July 2026 were made under the Act as it stands, and what the Act provides for the identity itself is not stated in either report. The Act's number and year are not given in either.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2024 Civil Registration and Identification Act provides a unique number and electronic identity documents. No rules made under it are known.
NAM.summary:
Law in force. Namibia's Civil Registration and Identification Act, No. 13 of 2024, is the statute for civil registration and legal identity. It sets up a civil register that includes an identity register under a Registrar-General. In July 2026 officials said the electronic identity card is legally recognised under the Act.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act assigns each person a unique identity number, authorises physical or electronic identity documents and governs how register data is authenticated and verified. In July 2026 an official of the Office of the Prime Minister said it allows institutions to accept either the physical card or its digital version, which the ministry said can be verified electronically. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

NER.short: Niger's cabinet adopted a draft ordinance in April 2026 adding a unique identifier and biometrics to its registers. Whether it was signed is not known.
NER.summary:
Law in force. Niger's Council of Ministers adopted a draft ordinance on the civil status regime on 22 April 2026. It amends law no. 2019-29 of 1 July 2019 to clarify the national civil status register and the national population register. It is a draft adopted by cabinet; no source says it has been signed.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No identity law is in force. The draft ordinance would add biometric parameters and a unique identifier to the registers the 2019 civil status law set up, which is what would make it the country's identity law. Until it is signed, the unique identifier and the biometric register are proposals, and the 2019 law stands as a civil status law. The 2019 law is numbered 2019-29.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

NGA.short: Nigeria's NIMC Act 2026, signed in June, makes the identity number foundational and provides for electronic verification. No rules made under it are known.
NGA.summary:
Law in force. Nigeria's National Identity Management Commission Act 2026 was signed into law on 26 June 2026, repealing the 2007 Act. The bill had passed second reading in the Senate in July 2024. A civil society speaker said on 29 July 2026 that the gazetted text was not yet available.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act reaffirms the national identification number as the foundational identity and makes the Commission responsible for verifying electronic identities. It makes the Commission the national repository for biometric data and, by one account, makes the number compulsory across fourteen sectors. The Commission described its work in September 2026 as in compliance with the Act. The Act was three months old at the end of September 2026, and no regulation made under it is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

RWA.short: Rwanda's single digital identity law, reported in 2026, ends old identity cards by June 2027. No rules made under it are known.
RWA.summary:
Law in force. Rwanda has a law governing registration into its single digital identity system. In March 2026 The New Times reported that the law sets a June 2027 deadline after which existing national identity cards are no longer valid, and that under it citizens cannot hold two government-issued identities. The law's number and date are not given.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The system the law governs is built on a unique single digital identification number, a derived token and a card with a QR code, with authentication that relies on biometric data. Enrolment under it takes fingerprints, a facial image and an iris scan, carried out by the national identification agency. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

SDN.short: Sudan's 2011 Civil Registry Act gives each citizen a unique national number in an electronic register. No rules made under it since 2023 are known.
SDN.summary:
Law in force. Sudan's Civil Registry Act 2011 was signed by the President, repealed the 2001 Act and came into force on signature. It sets up the civil registry, run by the Ministry of Interior, which issues the national number and the identity card. It is an act of the National Assembly, and no later amendment is on record.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act defines the national number as a unique number given to each citizen on registration, never to be repeated. It provides for civil registry records to be stored electronically on computer and for a central database. The number and the electronic register are both in the Act's own text, which gives only the year 2011. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2016 law institutes a biometric identity card; a bill to extend card validity was before parliament in September 2026.
SEN.summary:
Law in force. Senegal's identity card rests on a 2016 law instituting the ECOWAS biometric identity card. On 29 April 2026 the Council of Ministers adopted a bill to amend it and extend how long cards are valid, and on 29 September 2026 that bill, numbered 21/2026, was before the National Assembly.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2016 law is a law for a biometric identity card, which is how the reports of the amending bill name it. The bill concerns the card's period of validity; an Interior Ministry official said on 24 September 2026 that the amending text would extend the 2016 cards. It had not been passed by the end of September. The law in force is the one of 2016, unamended at that date.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone validated a draft civil registration and identification bill in November 2025; it had still to reach Cabinet and Parliament.
SLE.summary:
Law in force. Sierra Leone's National Civil Registration Authority held the final national validation of the draft National Civil Registration and Identification Bill and its regulations on 17 November 2025. The bill has still to go to Cabinet and then to Parliament. It is the draft that would replace the present registration law.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No source held says a national identity law is in force, so nothing is counted beyond the bill. The validation of November 2025 covered the draft regulations together with the bill, which means the rules are being written with the law and not after it. What the bill provides for the identity itself is not stated in the report. The validation was the last step before the bill leaves the Authority.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2023 identification law is in force; a 2024 regulation applies it and sets rules for banks and phone companies checking identity.
SOM.summary:
Law in force. Somalia's Public Identification and Registration Law, Law No. 009 of 20 March 2023, is in force. On 8 June 2024 the Prime Minister signed an implementing regulation made under it, following a Council of Ministers decision of 6 June 2024. The regulation took effect on signature.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The regulation defines the digital national identification system as the system the 2023 law established. It applies the law and sets rules for relying parties, among them banks and phone companies, which check identity against the system. The regulation of June 2024 is thus both the rule made under the law and the text that says the law's system is digital. The regulation is numbered 158 and was made a little over a year after the law.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

SSD.short: South Sudan's 2018 Civil Registry Act and 2024 regulations provide for a personal identification number; the World Bank calls them under-implemented.
SSD.summary:
Law in force. South Sudan's Civil Registry Act of 2018, with the Nationality Act of 2011, is the legal foundation of its identification system, a World Bank diagnostic of May 2026 says. The Bank says the Act and regulations made under it in 2024 have established the legal foundation for the country's identity system, and calls the framework under-implemented.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Civil Registration and National Identity Regulations, 2024, were made under sections 33 and 39 of the Act and regulate the issue of legal documents. The Bank says the Act and the regulations lay the foundation for an interoperable digital identity system based on a personal identification number. Both are in force on paper, by the Bank's account.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe had a new identity law in draft in September 2025. Whether it has been approved is not known.
STP.summary:
Law in force. São Tomé and Príncipe has a new identity law in draft. A World Bank mission of 8 to 12 September 2025 flagged as urgent its review, public consultation, finalisation and approval. The mission's note calls it the aggregated identification document law and treats it as drafted and not yet approved.

Digital identity covered and rules made. No source held says a national identity law is in force. The mission warned that without the law's approval the collection of data could be constrained, which is the reason it gave for urgency. No later report says the law has been consulted on, finalised or approved, and what it provides for the identity itself is not stated. The mission's note is dated September 2025.

Not held. No source held says a national identity law is in force.

SWZ.short: Nothing held names a national identity law or bill for Eswatini, or says there is none, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not held. Nothing held names a national identity law or bill, or says there is none.

SYC.short: Seychelles' identity cards law, amended in 2023, is in force. Whether it provides for a digital identity is not known.
SYC.summary:
Law in force. Seychelles' National Identity Cards Act, Cap. 294, is a statute in force. The Miscellaneous Amendments Act 2023, assented to on 8 November 2023, amended it. The amending Act is Act 22 of 2023 and changes several laws at once, the identity cards law among them.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2023 amendment adds a card for non-resident citizens and new rules on disclosing card information. The first is a new section 4A of the identity cards Act. Those are the changes to the law on record, and neither is described as setting up a biometric register or an identity that is checked electronically. The Act is the country's identity law and has no replacement bill on record. The 2023 Act is the newest amendment to it.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

TCD.short: A 2020 ordinance, ratified by law, sets up a biometric population register and unique national number; rules made since 2023 are not known.
TCD.summary:
Law in force. Chad's Ordinance 002/PR/2020 of 14 February 2020 on civil status, ratified by Law 006/PR/2020 of 29 May 2020, sets up the integrated population and secure titles system (SIGPTS), run by the national agency for secure titles, ANATS. The system issues a unique national identification number (NNI) through the national biometric population register.

Digital identity covered and rules made. Under article 8 of the ordinance the register holds the biographic and biometric data and the NNI of everyone on the territory, and article 2 obliges every resident or visitor to register. Article 10 makes the NNI unique, unintelligible and non-sequential. Because the register covers everyone on the territory, the number reaches citizens, foreign residents and visitors alike. These are the 2020 provisions as the UNHCR describes them in an April 2026 study of refugee inclusion in the system.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

TGO.short: Togo's 2020 biometric identification law, amended in 2022, sets up a unique number; the last rule known under it is a September 2022 decree.
TGO.summary:
Law in force. Togo's law no. 2020-009 of 10 September 2020 on the biometric identification of natural persons created the national identification agency. Law no. 2022-010 of 24 June 2022, adopted by the National Assembly and promulgated by the President, amended several of its articles.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The amended law defines a unique identification number issued after verification of demographic and biometric data, and a central database against which the number and the data are authenticated electronically. A decree of 9 September 2022 sets the rules for registering and updating the data and the conditions for using the number. Those rules all date from before September 2023, and none made under the law since then is on record. The agency the law created issues the number.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

TUN.short: Tunisia's organic law of March 2024 provides for a biometric identity card with an electronic certificate. No rules made under it are known.
TUN.summary:
Law in force. Tunisia's Organic Law No. 2024-22 of 11 March 2024 amends and completes the 1993 law on the national identity card; it was published in the official journal on 12 March 2024. Parliament had adopted it on 6 March 2024. A ministerial session on 22 April 2024 decided to start using the biometric card in the first half of 2025.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The organic law provides that the identity card carries an encrypted electronic chip holding the card number, a fingerprint and a photograph, and an electronic certificate that allows identity to be verified and documents signed electronically. It leaves the model of the card to a decree and the rules for the certificate to a joint ministerial order. No regulation or decree made under the law since September 2023 is on record.

Not held. No regulation or decree applying the law, and no rule made under it that others must check identity against the system, dated in the last three years, is held.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 1986 registration and identification law is in force. Whether it provides for a digital identity is not known.
TZA.summary:
Law in force. Tanzania's Registration and Identification of Persons Act, first passed in 1986, is recorded as still in force in the 2023 revised edition of the laws. It provides for the registration of persons and the issue of identity cards. In January 2026 the government said it would table an Infant Registration Bill in the session starting 27 January 2026.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 1986 Act is the law in force, and no source held says it provides for a biometric register or a unique number. The bill announced in January 2026 would let the identification authority register children from birth and give each a unique identification number. No report says it has been tabled or passed. The Act is numbered Cap. 36 in the revised laws.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

UGA.short: Uganda's 2015 Registration of Persons Act provides a unique number and biometric register; regulations were made under it in August 2024.
UGA.summary:
Law in force. Uganda's Registration of Persons Act, 2015 was assented to on 26 March 2015. It sets up the National Identification and Registration Authority, the national identification register and national identification cards. A Parliament release of 20 August 2026 describes the Authority as working under the Act.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The Act has the Authority assign a unique national identification number to every person registered and defines identity data to include fingerprints. Regulations made under it on 12 August 2024 set the card's validity at eleven years. In June 2026 the Authority said registered foreigners are given a unique identification number under the Act. The 2024 regulations amend the Registration of Persons Regulations, 2015, and are deemed in force from 20 November 2015.

Not held. Nothing on the four questions.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 1997 Identification Act is in force, with a replacement bill due in 2027 or 2028. Whether it covers digital identity is not known.
ZAF.summary:
Law in force. South Africa's Identification Act, 1997 is in force: the Minister of Home Affairs made the fourteenth amendment of the regulations under it on 23 June 2025, in operation from 1 July 2025. Its replacement, the National Identification and Registration Bill, is due in Parliament only in 2027 or 2028, a September 2026 report says.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 1997 Act is the law in force, and no source held says it provides for a digital identity. In May 2026 Home Affairs gazetted draft amended regulations under the Act for comment until 6 June 2026, which would regulate access to identity information. They were drafts at the end of September 2026. The Act of 1997 remains the law the population register and the identity document are kept under.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

ZMB.short: Zambia's National Registration Act is in force, with regulations of 2019. Whether it provides for a digital identity is not known.
ZMB.summary:
Law in force. Zambia's National Registration Act is in force. The National Registration Regulations, 2019 were made under its section 14; the Act provides for the national registration card, with a Chief Registrar and registrars. The regulations are Statutory Instrument No. 34 of 2019.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2019 regulations prescribe the registration procedure: an application, a photograph, the capture of ten rolled and ten plain fingerprints and a birth certificate, and the forms of the card with its number. They are the newest rules under the Act on record, and no source held says the Act provides for a register held digitally or an identity checked electronically. The Act is Cap. 126 of the laws of Zambia, and no amendment to it since 2019 is on record.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's 1976 National Registration Act is in force. Whether it provides for a digital identity is not known.
ZWE.summary:
Law in force. Zimbabwe's National Registration Act commenced on 24 September 1976. It sets up the Registrar-General of National Registration, a register of residents and identity documents, and its consolidated text is up to date to 31 December 2016. A statutory instrument gazetted on 30 January 2024 was made under its section 11.

Digital identity covered and rules made. The 2024 instrument amends the registration fees, which is not a rule on how identity is held or checked. The Act itself provides for the registration of residents and a register kept by the Registrar-General. No source held says the Act, or an amendment to it, provides for a biometric register or an identity checked electronically. The Act is Chapter 10:17 of the laws of Zimbabwe.

Not held. No source held says the law in force provides for a biometric register, an identity number unique to each person, or an identity that can be checked electronically.

AGO.short: No national digital strategy is on record for Angola, only a public administration digitalisation agenda and a World Bank programme, so no stage is set.
AGO.summary: Not held. No national digital strategy is held for Angola. The public administration agenda, the World Bank programme and the draft law on artificial intelligence are other kinds of instrument.

BDI.short: The World Bank stated in 2020 that Burundi has no national digital strategy, and whether one is now in preparation is not known.
BDI.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank's 2020 assessment recommends that the government adopt a national digital strategy as a pillar of its development plan, stating that the country lacks an overarching and cohesive one.

Standing. The World Bank's Burundi Digital Economy Assessment, published in 2020, states that Burundi lacks an overarching and cohesive digital strategy.

Text. The same 2020 assessment states there is no overarching digital economy strategy beyond the ICT policy PNDTIC 2010-2025.

Period. The nearest instrument is the ICT policy PNDTIC, which runs from 2010 to 2025.

Delivery plan. The 2020 assessment states that PNDTIC 2010-2025 lacks an actionable operational plan.

Reporting. The 2020 assessment names PNDTIC 2010-2025 as the only overarching instrument it finds.

Last twelve months. The latest statement held is the World Bank's 2020 assessment, which recommends adopting a new overarching strategic vision.

Not held. Both statements date from 2020 and nothing newer repeats them. No national digital strategy is on record as adopted, launched or in preparation.

BEN.short: Benin has a digital strategy to 2031 in preparation since February 2026, but whether it will be adopted or published is not known.
BEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Digital and Digitalisation ran the 5-6 February 2026 seminar that drafted the vision for the Stratégie numérique du Bénin 2031, with Deloitte.

Standing. The strategy is in preparation: on 24 March 2026 ASIN's director general said the agency was supporting the digital ministry in drawing it up, after consultations began at a Cotonou workshop on 5-6 February 2026. It follows a 2021-2026 digital strategy, described by a GSMA study published in January 2025.

Text. The February 2026 seminar was to end in a strategic reference document.

Period. The strategy runs to 2031, drawn up under the Ministries of Economy and Finance and Digital Affairs, where its predecessor covers 2021-2026.

Delivery plan. The seminar was to set the vision and priority initiatives for the next five years, with Deloitte giving technical support.

Reporting. The consultations launched in February 2026 cover internet coverage, e-services, artificial intelligence, digital skills and financing.

Last twelve months. The 5-6 February 2026 seminar brought public sector, private operators and technical partners together to define the vision and priority initiatives.

Not held. No adopting act, public text, period, plan or reporting is held for the 2031 strategy. The 2021-2026 strategy is only announced, with no adopting act or public text.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso adopted a digital economy strategy in 2018, running to 2027, but whether its text is published is not known.
BFA.summary:
Governance and finance. The health ministry's plan lists SN@DEN 2018-2027 with objectives covering its governance, digital trust and broadband.

Standing. The ministry's diagnostic report lists SN@DEN 2018-2027 as adopted on 6 June 2018, and the government presented a twelve-project roadmap to 2030 on 25 August 2025.

Text. The health ministry's plan lists SN@DEN among national strategies, with objectives for public administration, economic sectors and human capital.

Period. SN@DEN is listed with a period of 2018-2027, and a long-term digital strategy toward 2030 was described as current in March 2026.

Delivery plan. A Schéma directeur d'aménagement numérique was produced within the 2017-2020 action plan of SN@DEN, according to an article of 17 September 2021.

Reporting. The same 2021 article is the nearest held row, naming the Schéma directeur as the product of the 2017-2020 action plan.

Last twelve months. The health ministry's plan, dated January 2025, still lists SN@DEN with a period of 2018-2027.

Not held. No published text of SN@DEN is held. The 2030 roadmap is described only as announced or presented, with no adopting act, and no public text of it is held.

BWA.short: Botswana's cabinet adopted its digital transformation strategy in February 2020, running to 2026, but whether its text is published is not known.
BWA.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Communications as lead of the SmartBots Digital Transformation Strategy, and the first phase of one of its projects cost government P234 million in 2023.

Standing. The government online coordinator said the strategy was adopted by cabinet in February 2020, and in September 2026 the President said it would be formally launched in November 2026.

Text. A January 2026 data-centre briefing says the strategy was established to enhance connectivity, build a knowledge workforce and digitalise services.

Period. The ITU repository gives the strategy's time frame as 2021-2026.

Delivery plan. The President said in September 2026 that the strategy and action plan would be formally launched in November 2026.

Reporting. A EUR 4.85 million project running August 2024 to August 2027 supports a monitoring and evaluation framework and a progress dashboard for the strategy.

Last twelve months. On 23 September 2026 the President told the UN Economic Commission for Africa that the strategy and action plan would be formally launched in November 2026.

Not held. No published text of the strategy is held, and no delivery plan or progress report is held. The 2021-2026 period comes from a third-party repository.

CAF.short: The Central African Republic had a national digital plan in drafting in 2021, for 2020 to 2025, and whether it was adopted is not known.
CAF.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank assessment says technical assistance for the Digital CAR strategy is financed under the Central African Backbone project, co-funded by the European Union and the African Development Bank.

Standing. A workshop on 10-11 November 2021, opened by the chief of staff of the Ministry of Digital Economy, Posts and Telecommunications, presented the studies for the Plan National Stratégique Centrafrique Digitale 2025.

Text. The November 2021 workshop presented the studies for the plan, which is the nearest held row to a text.

Period. The workshop document gives the plan's period as 2020-2025.

Delivery plan. The World Bank assessment of 2020 lists the strategy as in preparation, with technical assistance commissioned by the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications.

Reporting. The 2020 assessment says a feasibility study on the digital strategy was launched in 2020 under the Central African Backbone project.

Last twelve months. The latest held row is the November 2021 workshop presenting the plan's studies.

Not held. Nothing after November 2021 is held on the plan, and no adoption or public text is held. Its stated period, 2020-2025, has ended.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire has a published digital strategy for 2021-2025, now past its period, and a 2025 successor whose adoption is not known.
CIV.summary:
Governance and finance. The published text has the Commission Nationale de Développement de la Société de l'Information steer the Stratégie nationale de développement du numérique 2021-2025, with a monitoring committee led by the digital ministry. Paradigm Initiative ties national allocations of about USD 91 million for 2024 and USD 101 million for 2025 to its cycle.

Standing. Fraternité Matin reports it adopted in January 2022. Its successor, the Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2025-2035, was validated at a workshop on 19-22 August 2025.

Text. The ministry published the strategy's own text, version 1.4 of 26 January 2022, on its site.

Period. The strategy covers 2021-2025, with 2025 targets for its 36 strategic indicators. The successor is named for 2025-2035.

Delivery plan. The action plan for seven pillars lists projects with start date, priority and budget in million FCFA, such as 95,000 million FCFA to connect public administrations to the national broadband network.

Reporting. We Are Tech Africa credited the strategy on 15 July 2025 with over 5,207 km of fibre, several online service portals and an operational National Cybersecurity Agency.

Last twelve months. A workshop on 3 September 2026 opened work toward 700 digital public services and a paper-free state by 2030.

Not held. No adopting act is on record for the strategy or for its successor. Whether the successor's text is public is not known.

CMR.short: Cameroon has a published digital plan adopted in 2016 whose period has ended, and an update in preparation, so progress is not known.
CMR.summary:
Governance and finance. The Plan stratégique Cameroun numérique 2020 assigns delivery to the postal and telecommunications ministry with the other ministries, ANTIC, ART and CAMTEL. Its financing column draws on the public investment budget, the telecommunications special fund and the State budget, alongside external financing.

Standing. The plan, dated May 2016, calls itself the adopted strategic plan and names no adopting act. A workshop on 3 July 2025 discussed the diagnostic for updating it, with the next step to follow government approval.

Text. The plan's full text, 72 pages, is published on the ministry's site.

Period. The plan began in 2016 and, on both its own text and the ITU repository, ended by 2025.

Delivery plan. The priority action plan lists projects per axis with indicators, 2020 targets and an amount in FCFA each, such as 125,000,000,000 for a broadband backbone extension.

Reporting. The plan assigns monitoring and evaluation to the PPBS committees of each administration and their monitoring-evaluation cells.

Last twelve months. The ITU repository lists Digital Cameroon 2020 as the country's strategy in its 2025 edition.

Not held. The update of the plan has no text or period yet. No report against the plan is held.

COD.short: DR Congo validated a national digital plan in 2019, now past its period, and a 2026 successor whose adoption is not known.
COD.summary:
Governance and finance. Paradigm Initiative lists the Presidency, the posts and telecommunications ministry and the regulator ARPTC as lead institutions of the Plan National du Numérique Horizon 2025, and reports public digital budget allocations of USD 103.7 million in 2025. The plan leaves its own budget to the Government and the ADN.

Standing. The national validation workshop of 3-5 September 2019 validated the plan, and no cabinet act is named. Its successor, the Politique sectorielle de l'économie numérique 2026-2030, was validated on 4 August 2026 and is due before the Council of Ministers.

Text. The full text, dated September 2019, is on the Presidency's site.

Period. The plan carries the strategy to the horizon 2025, with target years from 2020 to 2025.

Delivery plan. Its timetable gives 68 priority projects with indicators, baselines and targets dated 2020 to 2025.

Reporting. Agence Ecofin reported on 11 October 2025 that the ministry estimates the plan is about 60% complete.

Last twelve months. The Government's action programme for 2024-2028 sets putting the plan's remaining projects into action, and the successor was technically validated on 21-22 July 2026.

Not held. No adopting act is on record for the plan or for its successor. The successor has no action plan, steering body or monitoring yet, and the plan's progress is a ministry estimate.

COG.short: Congo adopted Vision Congo Digital 2025 by decree in 2019; its successor is awaiting approval, and its action plan and monitoring are not known.
COG.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy is mandated to implement Vision Congo Digital 2025, coordinated by an inter-ministerial committee, according to the World Bank appraisal of 11 May 2022.

Standing. Décret n° 2019-150 of 17 June 2019 approves the strategy. A successor, Stratégie numérique 2030, was reported complete on 13 October 2025 and awaits review and final approval by decree.

Text. The decree was published in the Journal officiel of 4 July 2019.

Period. The ITU repository gives the time frame as 2021 to 2025, while the successor is named Vision Congo digital 2030.

Delivery plan. A December 2020 World Bank diagnostic says the action plan was still being drawn up with consultants.

Reporting. The May 2022 appraisal lists monitoring and evaluation mechanisms among the requirements for implementing the strategy.

Last twelve months. A digital identity workshop in July 2025 was described as a milestone in implementing Congo Digital 2025.

Not held. No public text of Vision Congo Digital 2025, no monitoring and no domestic budget line for it are shown. Its successor is validated at ministry level but not adopted by decree, with World Bank finance only.

COM.short: Comoros adopted a public, costed digital strategy to 2028 in 2018; results against its targets are not known.
COM.summary:
Governance and finance. ANADEN, the national digital development agency created in 2019, has the implementation of Comores Numérique 2028 as its first mission, and the strategy itself designs a national digital council and an observatory.

Standing. The digital health strategy says the Government drew up Comores Numérique 2028 and adopted it in 2018.

Text. The text is public on ANADEN's site.

Period. Its roadmap runs from 2018 to 2028.

Delivery plan. The strategy costs its six axes at 52,995,160,485 KMF, planned costings of 2018, and a 2025 report gives a target of 5% of GDP for the digital sector by 2028.

Reporting. The strategy designs a national digital observatory to measure sector performance.

Last twelve months. On 25 August 2026 the minister said ANADEN is to contribute to implementing the strategy across the economy.

Not held. No published report on results against the strategy's targets, no domestic budget line for it and no adopting act are shown.

CPV.short: Cabo Verde approved a digital economy strategy to 2030 in 2024; its public text, plan and reporting are not known.
CPV.summary:
Governance and finance. On 25 November 2025 the Estratégia para a Economia Digital de Cabo Verde was presented to the Conselho Consultivo da Economia Digital, chaired by the Vice-Prime Minister.

Standing. Resolução 72/2026 lists it as approved in September 2024. The Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation, as that resolution only establishes its bases.

Text. The same resolution lists the strategy with a focus on competitiveness, innovation and the digital economy.

Period. It covers 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. NOSi's March 2020 action plan names three hubs for the strategy: connectivity, capacity-building and service provision.

Reporting. The same NOSi plan says implementation is under way with African Development Bank and World Bank support.

Last twelve months. The strategy was presented to the digital economy council on 25 November 2025, and the 2035 agenda's consultation followed on 6 August 2026.

Not held. No public text of the strategy and no plan, reporting, body or finance for it are shown. The Agenda Digital de Cabo Verde 2035 is in preparation and not adopted, and the 2019 to 2021 Agenda has ended.

DJI.short: Djibouti's cabinet heard a digital economy roadmap in March 2023; whether it was adopted is not known.
DJI.summary:
Governance and finance. The minister delegate for the digital economy presented the roadmap to the Council of Ministers in March 2023.

Standing. The government spokesperson's record of that session notes a communication on the "Djibouti Smart Nation: Feuille de Route pour l'Economie Numérique" and records no adoption. The Council of Ministers of 7 October 2025 listed drawing up a national digital strategy among the main challenges left.

Text. The nearest held statement is the March 2023 record's account of the roadmap.

Period. The nearest held statement is the communication of March 2023 on the roadmap.

Delivery plan. The roadmap is built on four pillars, smart administration, digital economy, smart trades and smart civil society, with structuring projects identified.

Reporting. The Council of Ministers record of 7 October 2025 follows the ministry's digital-maturity diagnostic of the administration.

Last twelve months. On 7 October 2025 the Council of Ministers listed a national digital strategy and sectoral roadmaps as still to be drawn up.

Not held. No adoption of the Smart Nation roadmap is on record, and no text, period, delivery plan or report is held for it. In October 2025 the Council of Ministers still listed a national digital strategy as to be drawn up.

DZA.short: Algeria adopted its national digital transformation strategy for 2025 to 2030 in May 2025, but costs and results against its targets are not known.
DZA.summary:
Governance and finance. The High Commission for Digitalisation, created by presidential decree 23-314 of 6 September 2023, designs the strategy and follows its implementation, and on 4 May 2026 it signed a project with UNDP, supported by the Government of Japan to support its implementation.

Standing. El Chaab says the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2025-2030 was adopted, approved and published in May 2025, and on 12 May 2025 the High Commissioner called it the approved strategy.

Text. The text is published on the High Commission's site, in an August 2024 version with twenty-five strategic objectives.

Period. The ITU repository gives its time frame as 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The minister said on 4 May 2026 that the implementation plan for 2025-2026 is under way, with an executive plan for 2027-2030 in preparation.

Reporting. The High Commission published a review of April 2024 to September 2026 listing its projects, and said on 2 September 2026 that the second national data centre at Blida implements its first axis.

Last twelve months. The National Digital Services Centre was inaugurated on 5 July 2026, and the Council of Ministers of 12 July 2026 gave administrations one month to connect to the National Data Center.

Not held. No adopting act is named; approval is stated by the press and the High Commissioner only. No cost for the plan, no domestic budget line and no results against the strategy's own targets are held.

EGY.short: Egypt's Digital Egypt strategy, running from 2016, is listed as adopted in 2025, but its text, plan and recent progress are not known.
EGY.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Communications and Information Technology as lead of the Digital Egypt Strategy.

Standing. The ITU repository's 2025 listing records the Digital Egypt Strategy as adopted, and on 13 March 2024 the Prime Minister named approval of a National strategy for building a fully digital state among the Supreme Council for Digital Society's objectives.

Text. The ITU repository's 2025 listing names the Digital Egypt Strategy as the country's strategy.

Period. The same repository gives its time frame as 2016 onward.

Delivery plan. At Cairo ICT'24 on 17 November 2024 the ICT minister briefed the Prime Minister on its four pillars: digital services, jobs in the digital economy, digital creativity and infrastructure.

Reporting. At the same briefing of 17 November 2024 the minister gave implementation figures, including 8 million registered on the Digital Egypt platform and 23 of a targeted 32 creativity centres built.

Last twelve months. The latest held figures are those of the 17 November 2024 briefing, when 8 million were registered on the Digital Egypt platform.

Not held. Adoption rests on a general listing with no adopting act, body or date, and no public text is held. No delivery plan, domestic budget line or reporting after November 2024 is held, and no approval of the fully digital state strategy is recorded.

ERI.short: Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, according to a June 2026 legal-status page; whether any is in preparation is not known.
ERI.summary:
Governance and finance. Levellers, in a legal-status page reviewed on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy.

Standing. The same Levellers page states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy, alongside no published national AI strategy.

Text. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Period. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Delivery plan. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Reporting. The nearest held row is Levellers' statement of 8 June 2026 that no national digital transformation strategy exists.

Last twelve months. Levellers, reviewing on 8 June 2026, states that Eritrea has no national digital transformation strategy.

Not held. The only statement of absence is a third-party legal-status page, not an Eritrean government source. No instrument in preparation is on record.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 in November 2025, but its public text and period are not known.
ETH.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Transformation Council, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Temesgen Tiruneh, met on 30 July 2026 and was said to provide strategic leadership for the Digital Ethiopia Strategy. Public ICT and digital allocations rose from about USD 250 million in 2020 to USD 500 million in 2024, which Paradigm Initiative attributes to the predecessor, Digital Ethiopia 2025.

Standing. The Council of Ministers approved Digital Ethiopia 2030 on 29 November 2025 and the Prime Minister launched it on 20 December 2025, as the successor to Digital Ethiopia 2025.

Text. The Ethiopian News Agency describes Digital Ethiopia 2030 as a comprehensive national blueprint building on the Homegrown Economic Reform Agenda.

Period. Digital Ethiopia 2025 covered 2020 to 2025, and the Prime Minister said on 20 December 2025 that it had been completed as the country moved to Digital Ethiopia 2030.

Delivery plan. CIO Africa, on 27 January 2026, lists the targets for 2030: 100 percent 5G coverage in 100 cities, 128 million mobile subscribers, a Fayda digital ID for every adult and digital payments up sevenfold.

Reporting. On 30 July 2026 the Council reviewed progress on the Digital Ethiopia Strategy, Fayda and the 5 Million Coders initiative.

Last twelve months. Digital Ethiopia 2030 was launched on 20 December 2025, with enablers named as electricity, cybersecurity, a sovereign government cloud, broadband rollout and scaling Fayda ID and interoperable payments.

Not held. No public text is held for Digital Ethiopia 2030, and no period is stated for it. No domestic finance line is tied to the 2030 strategy, and reporting is activity only, with no published results.

GAB.short: Gabon's minister presented a national digitalisation strategy in April 2026 after the 2020-2025 plan ended; whether it has been adopted is not known.
GAB.summary:
Governance and finance. The digital economy minister announced a permanent consultation framework with state IT directors on 3 April 2026. The earlier plan, Gabon Digital 2025, had ANINF as its lead and was financed by the African Development Bank, as reported in November 2020.

Standing. On 3 April 2026 the minister presented the main orientations of the national digitalisation strategy to state IT directors, with no adoption stated.

Text. The report of that meeting gives the strategy's orientations and no text.

Period. The International Telecommunication Union's repository gives the time frame of the earlier Gabon Digital strategy as 2020 to 2025.

Delivery plan. The strategy is built on five axes, regulatory framework, infrastructure, public services, local skills and data governance, and its sector master plans are still to be drawn up.

Reporting. The nearest held statement is the minister's presentation of 3 April 2026.

Last twelve months. The minister presented the five-axis strategy on 3 April 2026 and announced progressive sector master plans.

Not held. No adoption, text or period is held for the national digitalisation strategy presented in April 2026. No governing body, finance or report is held for it.
