GHA.short: Ghana's Digital Economy Policy and Strategy was adopted in 2024 with a 2028 target; whether any progress report exists is not known.
GHA.summary:
Governance and finance. The 2024 text of the Ghana Digital Economy Policy and Strategy names government budgetary support, development partner support and public-private partnerships as its funding sources, with no allocation or budget line.

Standing. The Ministry of Communications and Digitalisation adopted the Digital Economy Policy in October 2024, and the World Bank records the strategy and policy as approved in April 2024. A successor, the National Digital Transformation and Emerging Technology Strategy, was begun by the ministry in April 2025 and is in preparation.

Text. The policy and strategy text is public, published in 2024.

Period. The text sets a target timeline of 2028 for its objectives and a review every four years.

Delivery plan. The implementation framework lists strategic actions with assigned responsibilities, phased as quick wins within 6 months, medium term at 6 to 18 months and long term at 18 to 48 months, with no cost stated.

Reporting. The policy text assigns responsibilities for each strategic action and sets a review every four years.

Last twelve months. The latest dated event held for the policy is its adoption by the ministry in October 2024.

Not held. No progress report against the policy's own actions and no mandated body are held. The successor strategy is only begun, and no budget line is given for the policy.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2023-2027 digital strategy is public and costed, with a lead ministry named, but whether any progress report exists is not known.
GIN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Stratégie nationale de digitalisation de l'État et de développement de l'économie numérique 2023-2027 names the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy as lead ministry, and its financing table puts the State at USD 209,711 thousand, 12 percent of USD 1,747,590 thousand, with development partners at 60 percent.

Standing. The strategy, titled Guinée Digitale 2027 in its own text, is the Transition Government's strategy in version 1.2 of 11 June 2024, validated in national workshops with UNDP and the African Development Bank.

Text. The full text is published as a PDF on the site of the state digitalisation agency, issued by the ministry.

Period. The strategy is titled 2023-2027 and sets 14 result indicators against 2022 references for a 2027 horizon. It follows the 2016-2020 ICT and digital economy strategy, which has ended.

Delivery plan. The roadmap sets 245 initiatives under 41 orientations and six axes, each with a responsible body, a cost in thousand US dollars and a duration.

Reporting. The lead ministry is responsible for drafting, coordinating, implementing and evaluating the strategy, with a national steering committee to be set up.

Last twelve months. The latest dated row is a round table on 4 and 5 December 2024, where the minister said the strategy had been in implementation since 2022.

Not held. No implementation or results report is held, and no adopting act is named for the strategy. The period reads 2027 in the title and 2026 in one article.

GMB.short: The Gambia's Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is published and reported adopted in 2024; its delivery plan and any progress report are not known.
GMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Economy Master Plan 2024-2034 is issued by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy.

Standing. The Digital Cooperation Organization reports that the government adopted the master plan, with data current to September 2024. A separate National Digital ID and Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2028 was validated at a workshop on 16 and 17 May 2024.

Text. The plan's PDF is published on the ministry's website, with 2024 as its published year.

Period. The ministry's own document gives the plan's period as 2024 to 2034.

Delivery plan. The ministry's published plan document sets out the plan for 2024 to 2034.

Reporting. The Digital Cooperation Organization lists the master plan, 2024 to 2034, among the guidelines it consulted.

Last twelve months. An article of 7 October 2026 gives the master plan as running 2024-2034.

Not held. The master plan has no governance, delivery plan or reporting row of its own. Its adoption rests on one third-party report naming the government and September 2024, and some sources date the plan 2023-2033.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau adopted a 2025-2030 digital transformation strategy by decree in March 2025, with a public text, but any report on results is not known.
GNB.summary:
Governance and finance. UNDP's record of the Mais Digit@l programme shows a US$3,360,500 grant for 2025-2030 to implement the strategy, and its 2024 annual report says the strategy was launched with financing from the Government of Japan.

Standing. Decreto 10/2025, published in the Boletim Oficial on 28 March 2025 after Council of Ministers approval on 13 March, approves the ENTD.GW 2025-2030, which the government had launched on 29 January 2025.

Text. The full text is public as the annex to the gazetted decree.

Period. The stated period is 2025-2030.

Delivery plan. The strategy sets 55 interventions under six strategic objectives, each with a stated start, end and duration in months, and no cost is given for them.

Reporting. UNDP's 2024 annual report says the strategy has six pillars and 55 priority interventions with clear implementation milestones.

Last twelve months. UNU-EGOV reported on 23 September 2026 that a Project Document for implementing the strategy, to set priorities, define governance structures and identify partners and resources, was discussed with a ministry delegation on 9 September 2026.

Not held. No published report against the strategy's targets is held, and no cost is given for its actions. No mandated body is stated.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's national digital economy strategy was in drafting with World Bank support in September 2026, and its adoption and published text are not known.
GNQ.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Transport, Telecommunications and Civil Aviation, led by Minister of State Honorato Evita Oma, opened a World Bank-supported working week on 2 September 2026 to finish the strategy.

Standing. The Estrategia Nacional de Economía Digital was in drafting on 2 September 2026, when a four-day working week opened in Malabo with eight World Bank Group specialists to complete and validate it. The earlier ADIGE digital agenda was launched by the ministry in 2019 for 2019 to 2025.

Text. The government press office of 2 September 2026 describes the strategy as still to be completed and validated.

Period. On 2 September 2026 the ministry expected a consensus roadmap at the close of the working week.

Delivery plan. The World Bank-supported working week of 2 September 2026 aims to complete the strategy.

Reporting. The government press office reported the opening of the working week on 2 September 2026.

Last twelve months. The working week to finish the strategy opened on 2 September 2026, with the ministry expecting a consensus roadmap at its close.

Not held. No adopting act, period, plan or reporting is held for the strategy, and no text is published. No body or finance is stated.

KEN.short: Kenya published a costed national digital master plan for 2022-2032, but any published report against its targets is not known.
KEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The plan names the ICT Authority as the main coordinating and implementing agency, under an inter-ministerial committee and an oversight committee chaired by the Cabinet Secretary (2022).

Standing. The Kenya National Digital Master Plan 2022-2032 is issued by the Ministry of ICT, Innovation and Youth Affairs with a Cabinet Secretary foreword, and was unveiled and launched by ICT Cabinet Secretary Joe Mucheru on 12 April 2022.

Text. The full plan is published as a PDF on the ICT Authority site.

Period. The plan states its period as 2022-2032 and is the successor to the 2014-2017 master plan. Its predecessor as national strategy is the Digital Economy Blueprint of 2019.

Delivery plan. Table 6.1 gives a resource requirement per theme for each year 2022-2032 in Ksh millions, and Annex 1 a budget per key project, for example Ksh 118.0B for 52,000 km of government fibre in 2022-2030.

Reporting. The ICT ministry's 2026 Budget Policy Statement, presented to the National Assembly committee on 17 February 2026, was aligned with the plan.

Last twelve months. An ICT Authority tender of 15 September 2026 cites the plan's national target of 100,000 km of fibre network.

Not held. No published report against the plan's targets is held, and no domestic budget line is stated. No dated event in the last twelve months changes the plan's standing.

LBR.short: Liberia has a National Digital Strategy 2025-2029, adopted per a March 2026 policy, with a costed plan, but results against its targets are not known.
LBR.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications developed the strategy and is responsible for implementing it, according to the National Data Governance Policy of March 2026, and the strategy's costs are to be met from government, multilateral donor and other sources.

Standing. The National Data Governance Policy of March 2026 lists the National Digital Strategy (2025-2029) among the instruments Liberia has adopted, after a validation workshop on 11 December 2024.

Text. The strategy's full text is published on the ministry's website.

Period. The strategy covers 2025 to 2029.

Delivery plan. In the text published on 3 February 2026, Chapter 6 estimates US$151.813 million over 2025-2029 from government, multilateral donor and other sources, and a separate US$776.250 million for about 1,500 cell towers through public-private partnership. Chapter 7 sets an implementation roadmap with timelines.

Reporting. The Digital Transformation Working Group, activated in October 2025, is to coordinate Liberia's digital activities.

Last twelve months. The strategy was officially launched at the National Coordination Session of Digital Liberia Week, held during 28-30 October 2025.

Not held. No progress report against the strategy's targets is held. No adopting act or date is named for the strategy, and no budget line for it is named.

LBY.short: Libya's Prime Minister approved a government digital transformation strategy in April 2025, to 2030, but its approved text is not known.
LBY.summary:
Governance and finance. Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dabaiba of the Government of National Unity approved the National Strategy for Government Digital Transformation, prepared by the Supreme Committee for Digital Transformation.

Standing. The Prime Minister approved the strategy on 21 April 2025, following the General Information Authority's December 2022 proposal.

Text. The General Information Authority publishes the December 2022 proposal for the strategy, marked as a proposal on its cover.

Period. The vision is that by the end of 2030 everyone in Libya will enjoy world-class government services, with 2030 targets set against 2022 baselines.

Delivery plan. The proposal sets 2030 targets against 2022 baselines, such as a rise in Libya's e-government development index rank from 162 to 100, and lists eleven action areas with initiatives. It says a national plan of projects and the budgets are still to be set.

Reporting. At the April 2025 launch the General Information Authority chairman said some of the strategy's plans had already been implemented in a number of ministries and bodies.

Last twelve months. On 19 April 2026 the General Information Authority described Level 3 biometric digital identity trials as part of implementing the National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, the name it also uses for the strategy.

Not held. The text of the strategy as approved in April 2025 is not held, only the December 2022 proposal. No budget, mandated body or results report is held for it.

LSO.short: Lesotho's digital transformation strategy to 2030 was approved in February 2025 and is published, but its action plan and results are not known.
LSO.summary:
Governance and finance. The strategy's text makes the Chief Digital Office in the ICT ministry, under the Chief Digital Officer, accountable for developing the strategy and its implementation plans and for its monitoring and evaluation, with ministries reporting progress to it.

Standing. The finance minister told Parliament on 19 February 2025 that the Digital Transformation Strategy had been approved, without naming an approving act or body.

Text. The strategy's text is published on the government's website.

Period. The strategy is catalogued as Lesotho's national digital transformation strategy to 2030, self-dated 2024.

Delivery plan. The text sets initiatives by priority, the highest to start within about 12 months of operationalisation and medium ones within three to five years, and states no cost. The National Digital Policy lists development of a detailed action plan for the strategy as a task for 2024-2025.

Reporting. A government news item of 29 September 2026 says Lesotho is advancing the strategy, with priorities including connectivity, digital skills, innovation and technology for public services.

Last twelve months. On 29 July 2025 the minister said the memorandum of understanding with India was signed in the wake of the strategy's launch.

Not held. No adopting act or date is named for the strategy, and no finance or results report is held for it. Its initiatives carry start windows and no calendar dates or costs, and no detailed action plan is held.

MAR.short: Morocco has Maroc Digital 2030, listed as adopted in 2025, with MAD 11 billion for 2024 to 2026, but a public text is not known.
MAR.summary:
Governance and finance. The ITU repository names the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform as lead of Maroc Digital 2030, and Morocco World News says MAD 11 billion was allocated for 2024-2026.

Standing. The ITU repository lists Digital Morocco 2030 among the strategies it says countries have adopted, and the Government Council heard a presentation of its general orientations on 25 January 2024. It follows Maroc Numeric 2013 and Maroc Digital 2020.

Text. We Are Tech Africa says Maroc Digital 2030 was launched in September 2024.

Period. The ITU repository gives its time frame as 2024-2030.

Delivery plan. Morocco World News pairs the MAD 11 billion for 2024-2026 with targets of 3,000 start-ups, 100,000 people trained a year and 240,000 jobs by 2030.

Reporting. In its declaration to the African Telecommunications Union conference in Abuja, Morocco highlighted progress under Maroc Digital 2030, without figures.

Last twelve months. On 17 July 2026 the ministry signed a memorandum with Capgemini Maroc on AI skills, and on 4 June 2026 one with Orange Morocco, both presented as implementing it.

Not held. No public text of Maroc Digital 2030 is held, and its adopting act and date are not stated. Results against it are not given beyond a general account of progress.

MDG.short: Madagascar has the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028, presented in 2024 with a USD 800 million estimate, but its adoption and public text are not known.
MDG.summary:
Governance and finance. UNDP says the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028 is coordinated by the digital ministry, supported by the Unité de Gouvernance Digitale attached to the Presidency, and the ministry estimates its budget at USD 800.169 million, of which USD 152.334 million is available.

Standing. Newsmada reports the digital minister presented the plan on 19 January 2024, and UNDP calls it formalised and in implementation in December 2025. A national digital roadmap is in preparation after the Digital Readiness Assessment report was handed over on 17 December 2025.

Text. 2424.mg reports the ministry delivered a national Plan stratégique du numérique 2023-2028 on 26 October 2023.

Period. UNDP names the plan as the national digital strategy for 2023-2028.

Delivery plan. The ministry costs implementation at USD 800.169 million, with USD 647.835 million still to find, across four axes: legal framework, telecommunications, human capital, and digital and financial inclusion.

Reporting. UNDP says the plan is in implementation, in a consolidation phase.

Last twelve months. Tia Tanindrazana wrote on 8 September 2026 that the plan aims to raise the digital sector to 6% of GDP by 2028.

Not held. No source states that the Plan Stratégique Numérique 2023-2028 was adopted or approved, and no public text is held. No reporting against it is held.

MLI.short: Mali has a digital economy policy validated in 2024 with an action plan to 2029, but its adoption is not known.
MLI.summary:
Governance and finance. Le Matin reports that the Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy and Administrative Modernisation, with the Direction nationale de l'économie numérique, held the workshop that validated the policy.

Standing. The Politique nationale de développement de l'économie numérique (PNDEN) was validated at a workshop on 24 October 2024. It follows Mali Numérique 2020.

Text. The ministry reports that the launch ceremony of the study to prepare the policy document was held on 29 December 2023.

Period. Malijet describes the policy as covering 2021-2034, and its action plan covers 2025-2029.

Delivery plan. The validated policy comes with an action plan for 2025-2029.

Reporting. The minister is quoted giving an execution rate of 27.30% for the previous version, 2015-2020.

Last twelve months. On 2 October 2025 Malijet reported the African Girls Can Code Initiative phase III as anchored in the policy.

Not held. The policy's adoption is not stated, and no public text is held. Its periods differ between sources.

MOZ.short: In 2019 Mozambique approved a national information society plan running to 2028, but its delivery plan and published results are not known.
MOZ.summary:
Governance and finance. Decreto n.º 4/2026, approved on 10 March 2026, creates the Agência de Transformação Digital e Inovação, whose Technical Council is to ensure execution and permanent monitoring of the plan's projects. Paradigm Initiative says execution depends heavily on donor cycles, with World Bank projects financing broadband and governance work.

Standing. The Council of Ministers approved the Plano Estratégico para a Sociedade de Informação 2019-2028 and its Plano Operacional by Resolução n.º 52/2019, on 26 February 2019. A National Digital Transformation Strategy entered drafting when the process was launched on 12 February 2026.

Text. The text is printed in the Boletim da República I Série n.º 199 of 16 October 2019, hosted on the INTIC site.

Period. The plan sets its priorities for the horizon 2019-2028.

Delivery plan. The resolution approved the plan together with its Plano Operacional.

Reporting. INTIC's 2022 activity report has a section on evaluating the degree of implementation of the plan.

Last twelve months. Decreto n.º 4/2026 of 10 March 2026 tasks the new agency with mobilising resources for the Information Society Policy and its Strategic and Operational Plans.

Not held. No delivery plan is stated for this plan in the evidence, and no published report against its targets is held. The National Digital Transformation Strategy is still in drafting and would replace it.

MRT.short: Mauritania approved a costed national digital agenda for 2022 to 2025 that has now ended, and results against its targets are not known.
MRT.summary:
Governance and finance. The agenda states that the State has set up a Haut Conseil du Numérique to follow its execution. The digital ministry says the World Bank-supported WARDIP is to attract private investment and co-financing for the agenda's activities.

Standing. The government drew up and approved the Agenda national de transformation numérique 2022-2025 in 2022. On 4 December 2025 the digital ministry announced the start of preparation of an Agenda National de la Transformation Numérique 2030.

Text. The ministry hosts the agenda's text on its official site, dated June 2022.

Period. The agenda is a four-year strategy for 2022-2025 with a calendar of projects. Agence Ecofin refers to it in the past tense on 30 June 2026.

Delivery plan. The agenda is broken into 25 initiatives and 77 projects for a global investment of 400 million dollars, with cost, funding mode and owner given for each project.

Reporting. At a workshop on 4 December 2025 evaluating the agenda, the ministry's secretary general said it brought considerable advances in digital infrastructure, electronic platforms and access to public services.

Last twelve months. On 4 December 2025 the digital ministry opened preparation of the 2030 agenda, with the World Bank taking part by video link.

Not held. No domestic budget line is held for the agenda, and no report against its own targets is held, only accounts of activity. The Agenda National de la Transformation Numérique 2030 has no adopted text.

MUS.short: Mauritius launched a national digital transformation blueprint for 2025 to 2029 in 2025, and its cost and results against targets are not known.
MUS.summary:
Governance and finance. The Blueprint says a National Digital Transformation Bureau is to execute ICT projects and a Steering Committee will oversee implementation. At its first meeting on 26 August 2025 the Inter-Ministerial Committee was reported as mandated to monitor, coordinate and guide the projects, with monthly reports to Cabinet.

Standing. L'Express reports that the ministry officially launched the Digital Transformation Blueprint 2025-2029 on 26 May 2025, at a launch presided over by the President of the Republic.

Text. The full text is published on the MITCI site.

Period. The Blueprint is titled 2025-2029. It follows the Digital Mauritius 2030 Strategic Plan, published in 2018 with a horizon of 2030.

Delivery plan. The Blueprint lists actions per pillar and enabler and contains a phased roadmap with milestones and indicators.

Reporting. On 26 August 2025 the minister said an online motor vehicle licence renewal project under the Blueprint was already deployed, among around 84 projects.

Last twelve months. A government notice of 1 September 2026 names the Digital Transformation Blueprint (2025-2029) as the instrument the Digital Service Framework will help implement.

Not held. The Blueprint states no cost, and no report against its own targets is held, only accounts of activity. No adopting act is named for it.

MWI.short: Malawi has a National Digitalization Policy for 2023 to 2028, approved by Cabinet, but whether its text is public is not known.
MWI.summary:
Governance and finance. The NRB Strategic Plan 2025-2030 describes the National Digitalization Policy (2023) as setting the national direction for digital transformation across all sectors.

Standing. The National Digitalization Policy 2023-2028 was approved by Cabinet, per a MACRA presentation of October 2023, and the Open Government Partnership action plan of June 2025 lists its adoption and operationalisation. Its successor, a draft National Digital Transformation Strategy, went to a validation workshop on 18 and 19 February 2026.

Text. The National Local Government Finance Committee describes the 2023 policy as addressing country-wide ICT challenges and priorities.

Period. GSMA gives the policy as running 2023 to 2028.

Delivery plan. The Times said in January 2026 that principal secretaries' appraisals should be tied to the Malawi Digitalisation Policy 2023-28, measured by services online.

Reporting. The Open Government Partnership action plan of June 2025 lists the policy's adoption and operationalisation among the digital governance achievements of 2023 to 2025.

Last twelve months. In May 2026 the Local Government Finance Committee was reported saying Malawi has one ICT policy for the nation, the National Digitalization Policy.

Not held. No source says the text of the National Digitalization Policy is public or describes its scope. No delivery plan or reporting on it is held, and a National Digital Transformation Strategy is still being validated.

NAM.short: Namibia launched its National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 in August 2025 with a public text; any delivery plan or progress report is not known.
NAM.summary:
Governance and finance. The Paradigm Initiative report lists the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology as lead institution for the National Digital Strategy.

Standing. The Namibian reports that the ICT minister officially launched the National Digital Strategy 2025-2029 on 5 August 2025.

Text. The International Science Council paper of February 2026 cites the strategy's text on the ministry's website.

Period. Ecofin Agency gives the strategy as covering 2025 to 2029.

Delivery plan. In the 2025/26 budget speech of 7 May 2025 the minister said the strategy will be implemented in partnership with stakeholders.

Reporting. ITWeb reported in June 2026 that a national datacentre is a core pillar of the strategy, with no dates set for it.

Last twelve months. The national public key infrastructure DigiNam was launched on 31 August 2026 and described as aligned with the strategy.

Not held. No source names the body or act that adopted the strategy, and no cost or financing is held. No progress report on it is held.

NER.short: Niger's digital development policy for 2026 to 2035 was validated in March 2026 and awaits an approving decree; its text is not known.
NER.summary:
Governance and finance. The drafting committee handed the Politique nationale de développement du numérique 2026-2035 to the Minister of Communication on 13 October 2025.

Standing. A national validation workshop opened on 11 March 2026, and in June 2026 the minister listed the decree approving the policy among coming prospects. It follows the Politique nationale du numérique 2021-2030, which the ministry said in May 2026 a survey would help update.

Text. ANP reports the text was submitted to the workshop participants for validation on 11 March 2026.

Period. The minister gives the policy as running 2026 to 2035, and the earlier policy covered 2021 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The policy comes with a Plan d'Action Sectoriel 2026-2030 whose planned actions the workshop was to enrich.

Reporting. The minister said in March 2025 that the action plan was already drawn up and would be rolled out once the policy is adopted.

Last twelve months. The validation workshop opened on 11 March 2026, five months after the document was handed over.

Not held. No adoption of the policy is on record and its text is not held. No cost, reporting, governing body or financing is held.

NGA.short: Nigeria has a ten-year digital economy strategy unveiled in 2019, but results against its targets and its funding are not known.
NGA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy was assigned its development and implementation, and the March 2020 broadband plan says a National Digital Economy Council was established to oversee it, but the text ties no budget line to it.

Standing. President Buhari unveiled the National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy on 28 November 2019, and a 2025 ITU repository lists it as the country's strategy.

Text. The full text is held on the NITDA site.

Period. The strategy is titled and dated for 2020 to 2030.

Delivery plan. It sets eight pillars with listed government actions and dated targets, among them 70% broadband penetration in four years and 95% digital literacy in ten, with no cost stated.

Reporting. At the 20 December 2022 commissioning of the National Shared Services Centre, implementation was said to have produced "giant strides", with no figure against a target.

Last twelve months. NITDA's National Cloud Investment Strategy of August 2026 says the strategy continues to provide the overarching national policy framework.

Not held. Results against the strategy's targets are not known: reporting is statements of progress only. The plan states no cost, and no funding source is known.

RWA.short: Rwanda's Smart Rwanda plan, issued in 2015, ended in 2020, and a successor was in preparation in 2023, but its current status is not known.
RWA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of ICT and Innovation, supported by the Rwanda Digital Acceleration project under the World Bank, is working on its successor, Smart Rwanda Master Plan II.

Standing. The Government of Rwanda issued the Smart Rwanda Master Plan in October 2015, which INCLUDE in September 2022 says was adopted in 2015, and the October 2023 sector review lists Smart Rwanda Master Plan II among policies under development.

Text. The nearest held row is the October 2015 issue of the plan by the Government of Rwanda.

Period. The sector review names the Smart Rwanda Master Plan I as covering 2016 to 2020, and a Digital Transformation Strategy for Rwanda (ICT Master Plan 2021-2025) is listed with that period.

Delivery plan. INCLUDE gives the plan's aims as broadband for all and digital literacy for all by 2020.

Reporting. The nearest held row is the World Bank's March 2023 brief, which calls the 2020 Smart Rwanda Masterplan dated.

Last twelve months. The latest held row is the 26 October 2023 sector review listing Smart Rwanda Master Plan II, a five-year ICT strategy, among policies under development.

Not held. Whether the plan's text is public, and any delivery plan or reporting against it, are not known. Whether Smart Rwanda Master Plan II succeeds the 2021-2025 ICT Master Plan, and its status since October 2023, are not known.

SDN.short: Sudan's digital transformation ministry announced a strategy in 2025, but whether it was adopted or its text published is not known.
SDN.summary:
Governance and finance. The Central Bank of Sudan's request for proposals of 7 April 2026 refers to the digital transformation strategy announced by the digital transformation ministry in 2025.

Standing. The same request for proposals says the strategy was announced by the digital transformation ministry since 2025.

Text. The nearest held statement is the central bank's April 2026 reference to the strategy the ministry announced in 2025.

Period. The nearest held statement is the April 2026 request for proposals, which refers to the strategy announced in 2025.

Delivery plan. The nearest held statement is the central bank's reference of April 2026 to the strategy the ministry announced in 2025.

Reporting. The nearest held statement is the request for proposals of 7 April 2026, which mentions the strategy announced in 2025.

Last twelve months. The nearest held statement is the April 2026 request for proposals, which refers to the ministry's 2025 announcement of the strategy.

Not held. Whether the strategy was adopted by any act, and whether its text is public, are not known. No period, plan, reporting or governance fact is held.

SEN.short: Senegal launched its New Deal Technologique for 2025 to 2034 and published the text, but whether results are measured against its targets is not known.
SEN.summary:
Governance and finance. The government created the digital governance committee GouvNum among the first decisions under the New Deal Technologique, and the digital ministry's 2026 budget rose 38.7 percent to CFA 81.06 billion.

Standing. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye launched the New Deal Technologique on 24 February 2025, replacing the Stratégie Sénégal Numérique 2025.

Text. The New Deal Technologique text, titled Horizon 2034, is published on the Presidency site.

Period. The strategy runs to 2034, after a predecessor whose period was 2016 to 2025.

Delivery plan. The Digital Master Plan sets 12 priority programmes and 50 priority projects costed at FCFA 1,105 billion, of which 950 billion is identified.

Reporting. At the first anniversary in March 2026, authorities said significant progress had been made after one year of implementation.

Last twelve months. On 24 March 2026 Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko launched the New Deal's structuring projects, including e-Consulat and the sovereign cloud.

Not held. No source names an act adopting the strategy or creating the governance committee. Reporting covers first-year activity and is measured against no targets.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone approved its National Digital Development Policy in 2021 and publishes the text, but who approved it is not known.
SLE.summary:
Governance and finance. The policy proposes a National Digital Development Council under the President and a National Digital Development Agency, and lists an objective to allocate a proportion of the national budget to e-government systems.

Standing. The National Digital Development Policy 2021 was approved in 2021, and a draft National Digital Transformation Roadmap is in preparation.

Text. The policy text is hosted on the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation site.

Period. The policy states no end date, a vision of middle-income status by 2039, and says it shall be reviewed every five years.

Delivery plan. The policy contains no action plan and no costs, and instructs the Ministry to develop the implementation plan.

Reporting. The policy reports no progress against itself and instructs the Ministry to develop a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework.

Last twelve months. The Ministry of Health's 2024-2026 roadmap says the Universal Access Development Fund was established through the policy.

Not held. No act or body is named for the 2021 approval, and the policy text only recommends approval. Nothing dated in the last twelve months is held on the policy.

SOM.short: Somalia launched a Digital Transformation Strategy for 2025 to 2030 after a consultation in October 2025, but whether it was adopted is not known.
SOM.summary:
Governance and finance. The Ministry of Communications and Technology, with the ITU, hosted the October 2025 national consultation to validate the Digital Transformation Strategy.

Standing. The government launched the Digital Strategy 2025-2030, after a two-day consultation on 12-13 October 2025 to validate it.

Text. The ITU's 2025 review says the Digital Transformation Strategy for Somalia was developed in 2025.

Period. The strategy runs 2025-2030, as the Communications Minister named it in July 2025.

Delivery plan. The October 2025 consultation was to review and refine the proposed roadmap.

Reporting. The Hiiraan report on the launch of the Digital Strategy 2025-2030 quotes the Communications Minister.

Last twelve months. On 12 October 2025 the National Communications Authority reported the consultation kicked off to validate the strategy.

Not held. No source reports adoption of the strategy, and no act or body is named for the launch. No text, governance, delivery plan or reporting is held.

SSD.short: South Sudan was still developing its digital road map and master plan in June 2024; whether it has been adopted is not known.
SSD.summary:
Governance and finance. A consulting firm was developing the Digital Development Road Map and Master Plan for the Government, according to the World Bank aide-memoire of 3-7 June 2024.

Standing. The same aide-memoire records the Road Map and Master Plan as in development in June 2024, after consultations on draft recommendations.

Text. The June 2024 aide-memoire describes the Road Map and Master Plan as being developed, with private-sector and public-sector consultations held on drafts.

Period. The aide-memoire dated 7 June 2024 places the Road Map and Master Plan as support to the Government in preparing its future digital development strategy.

Delivery plan. The June 2024 aide-memoire records the firm's draft recommendations as the stage the work had reached.

Reporting. The World Bank mission record of June 2024 states that the firm "has been developing" the Road Map and Master Plan.

Last twelve months. The last dated row, the aide-memoire of June 2024, says the Road Map and Master Plan was still being developed.

Not held. No adopting act, body, text, period, plan or reporting is held for the Road Map and Master Plan, and the last dated record is from June 2024. A South Sudan Digital Transformation Strategy and a Digital Government Strategy are named without further description.

STP.short: The government of São Tomé and Príncipe had launched a national digital transformation strategy by March 2026; its adoption, text and period are not known.
STP.summary:
Governance and finance. The World Bank program document of 11 March 2026 attributes the national digital transformation strategy to the government.

Standing. The same document says the government "has launched" it, and it follows the 2020 Estratégia Nacional para a Governação Digital, approved by the Council of Ministers.

Text. The March 2026 World Bank document describes the strategy as expanding broadband connectivity, modernising the legal and regulatory framework and investing in digital public infrastructure.

Period. The World Bank document of 11 March 2026 is dated the day the launch is recorded, while the predecessor strategy covered 2020/2024.

Delivery plan. The March 2026 document names digital IDs and data exchange platforms as the digital public infrastructure to be invested in.

Reporting. The World Bank program document of 11 March 2026 is the one record of the strategy, stating that it has been launched.

Last twelve months. The government had launched the strategy by 11 March 2026, according to the World Bank.

Not held. The strategy's title, adopting act, date, body, text, period, plan and reporting are not held, and a launch alone does not show adoption. The 2020 digital governance strategy is a separate, earlier instrument.

SWZ.short: Eswatini has a 2024-2028 digital strategy named in sources, but its standing, text and plan are not known, so no stage is set.
SWZ.summary: Not held. No instrument could be staged for Eswatini. An Eswatini Digitalisation Strategy (2024-2028, 'Government in Your Hand') and a Digital Transformation Roadmap in procurement are named, with nothing that sets their standing, text, period, plan or reporting.

SYC.short: In 2026 Seychelles gave two bodies the lead on its digital strategy, but its standing is not known, so no stage is set.
SYC.summary: Not held. The only row on the national AI and digital strategy names the bodies mandated to lead it, in the World Bank's report of 17 September 2026. Its standing, text, period, delivery plan, reporting and finance are not held.

TCD.short: Chad has a 2020 to 2030 digital transformation strategy, but its adoption and public text are not known, so no stage is set.
TCD.summary: Not held. Whether the Stratégie nationale de transformation numérique 2020-2030 was approved, adopted or launched is not known, nor is whether its text is public. The World Bank in 2023 both cites it and says Chad has no comprehensive national digital strategy, and no reporting is held.

TGO.short: Togo's president said in 2022 the Togo Digital 2025 strategy was adopted, but its text and its 2025 to 2030 successor's progress are not known.
TGO.summary:
Governance and finance. In an April 2021 presentation the Ministry of Digital Economy and Digital Transformation is shown leading 6 projects and 1 reform of the Togo Digital 2025 portfolio. A World Bank paper of 29 April 2021 says the World Bank's WARCIP project financed its preparation, at US$1.36 million against a US$0.6 million budget.

Standing. In his independence address of 27 April 2022 the President said Togo had adopted the Stratégie Togo Digital 2025. A successor, Togo Digital 2025-2030, was in preparation from 22 May 2025, when the ministry began recruiting a consultant.

Text. The Minister of the Digital Economy referred to the 2020-2025 roadmap at the opening of the Lomé data centre on 8 June 2021.

Period. Togo Officiel said on 27 May 2025 that the current strategy ends at the end of 2025, and that the new one is to cover 2025 to 2030.

Delivery plan. The April 2021 presentation says the strategic roadmap for Togo Digital 2025 had been launched, with three parts and nine programmes.

Reporting. A WeAreTech.Africa article of 28 May 2025 says the 2020 framework had enabled advances, naming the e-Gouv platform, digital service centres and cybersecurity and data protection laws.

Last twelve months. The government portal reported on 4 May 2026 that under the Stratégie nationale Togo Digital 2025, 181 classrooms were connected, reaching 8,500 pupils.

Not held. No public text of Togo Digital 2025 and no delivery plan are held, and reporting is activity counts only. The successor, Togo Digital 2025-2030, is held only at consultant recruitment in May 2025.

TUN.short: Tunisia's National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025 and no named successor is held, so no stage is set.
TUN.summary: Not held. The National Digital Strategy 2021-2025 ended in 2025, and no named successor is held, only a broader national vision for 2026-2030. No text, delivery plan or governance rows are held for the strategy.

TZA.short: Tanzania's Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 was launched in 2024 and is public; its cost and any report on its targets are not known.
TZA.summary:
Governance and finance. The government, through the Tanzania Business Council, created a Digital Transformation Committee of public and private members to drive the Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034.

Standing. The President, Dr Samia Suluhu Hassan, launched the framework on 29 July 2024, and the ministry's catalogue page gives the same date.

Text. The Ministry publishes the framework on ictc.go.tz, with a statement from the President.

Period. It runs for ten years, 2024 to 2034, and a ministerial statement of 13 May 2026 cites it as in force.

Delivery plan. The Citizen lists its dated targets: ICT at 3% of GDP, 80% broadband and internet penetration and 90% digital literacy, all by 2029.

Reporting. The Ministry presented 758 towers built by December 2025 as supporting the strategy.

Last twelve months. At the 9th Tanzania Annual ICT Conference on 19 January 2026, Minister Angellah Kairuki said delivery must meet the framework's targets on time.

Not held. No finance line tied to the framework is held, and no published report against its targets. Its plan states dated targets without a cost.

UGA.short: Uganda published its Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 in 2022 with a costed plan; any report on progress is not known.
UGA.summary:
Governance and finance. The Vision for a Digital Uganda 2040 names a Digital Transformation Program Working Group of heads of ministries, departments and agencies to coordinate delivery, with the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance leading, and lists budget appropriations, concessional loans and grants as financing measures.

Standing. The Ministry published the Vision in September 2022 with a foreword by President Museveni; a newer Digital Transformation Roadmap was launched by the Government on 17 August 2023.

Text. The Vision is published on the Ministry's site.

Period. The Vision sets a 2040 horizon with targets for 2025, 2030 and 2040, and the Roadmap covers 2023/24 to 2027/28.

Delivery plan. The Vision carries a cost implementation matrix putting first-phase financing to 2030 at UGX 6.08 trillion, with a results framework of 2030 targets.

Reporting. The Vision has the working group prepare quarterly, semi-annual and annual implementation reports and run annual performance reviews.

Last twelve months. The Vision sets a mid-term evaluation in FY2028/29 and a final evaluation in FY2039/40.

Not held. No report against the Vision is held, and its governance rows date from September 2022. The Digital Transformation Roadmap has no adopting act or public text on record.

ZAF.short: South Africa has a final draft digital masterplan dated 2021, not public, with its 2020-2025 period ended; its adoption is not known.
ZAF.summary:
Governance and finance. The final draft of the ICT and Digital Economy Masterplan for South Africa is dated 22 February 2021 and credits Genesis Analytics and Knowledge Executive as authors.

Standing. Economist Impact says South Africa has published numerous draft versions of the masterplan. The department's 2023/24 plan, approved 31 March 2023, lists a Digital Economy Framework and Strategy still to go to Cabinet.

Text. The Economist Impact profile says in a footnote that the plan is not publicly available. The text held is the final draft of February 2021.

Period. Economist Impact titles the masterplan 2020-2025.

Delivery plan. The final draft has a Priority Action Plan in section 6, with an appendix of actions, some with named executors and time limits of three or five years.

Reporting. The Portfolio Committee's report on the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies for 2024/25 states that implementation of the Digital Economy Masterplan was not achieved against the department's target for the year.

Last twelve months. The latest row held on the masterplan is the Portfolio Committee's report for 2024/25, dated 2025.

Not held. No row says the masterplan was approved or adopted, and Economist Impact says the final version is not public. Its 2020-2025 period has ended, and no governance facts are held.

ZMB.short: Zambia adopted a public national digital transformation strategy in 2023, running to 2027, with no cost stated; progress against its targets is not known.
ZMB.summary:
Governance and finance. The National Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2027 makes the technology and science ministry the coordinating agency, responsible for quarterly monitoring and reporting. It is to be financed by the Government with cooperating partners, with no amount given.

Standing. A 2023 journal study says the strategy was adopted in 2023. The Ministry of Technology and Science published it on 12 October 2023.

Text. The strategy's full text is hosted on the Ministry of Technology and Science's site, from October 2023.

Period. The strategy states its period as 2023-2027, a five-year implementation framework.

Delivery plan. It sets out interventions with numeric targets, indicators and lead institutions, for example 998 communication towers and 200 district digital transformation centres.

Reporting. The strategy's results framework carries targets for 2026.

Last twelve months. Freight News described the strategy's five pillars on 3 September 2026.

Not held. No report on progress against the strategy's targets is held, and the delivery plan states no cost. No change in the last twelve months is on record.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe began defining a national digital roadmap for 2026 to 2030 in November 2025; whether it was adopted or published is not known.
ZWE.summary:
Governance and finance. The ICT Minister opened the regulator's POTRAZ Strategic Formulation Workshop in Mutare on 4 November 2025.

Standing. The workshop marks the start of a national process to define the digital roadmap, and no adopting body is named.

Text. The November 2025 report describes the roadmap as still to be defined.

Period. The National Digital Roadmap is meant for 2026 to 2030. The Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan, published in 2019, is a separate national instrument running to 2030.

Delivery plan. The only row on the roadmap is the 4 November 2025 workshop, which begins its formulation.

Reporting. The roadmap's latest row is the workshop of 4 November 2025.

Last twelve months. The Strategic Formulation Workshop of 4 November 2025 started the process.

Not held. No later row says the roadmap was validated or adopted, and no text, delivery plan or reporting is held. The Smart Zimbabwe 2030 Master Plan has one governance row from 2019 and nothing on its standing, text, plan or reporting.

AGO.short: Angola cut its 2026 communications programme budget by 30.5% on 2025; no spending figure is held and no fund is known.
AGO.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget sets 159.2 billion kwanza for the communications expansion and modernisation programme, down 30.5% from 229.3 billion in the 2025 budget. The digital lines held for both years total 9,912,523,594 kwanza for 2026 against 9,854,246,545 for 2025. The 4G expansion line falls from 107.8 to 62.7 billion kwanza, and the cybersecurity programme is cut 54%, from 70.5 to 32.3 billion kwanza in the proposed 2026 budget.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 budget gives 375,466,178,608 kwanza to 52 digital lines. A supplementary credit of 275 million US dollars was opened in the 2026 budget for the Ministry of Territorial Administration's citizens' database plan.

Not held. The money for digital transformation was lower in the latest budget than in the one before.

BDI.short: Burundi's 2026/27 budget raised its digital lines 7.3% and a universal service fund paid for connectivity projects; actual spending is not known.
BDI.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital lines held for both years total 3,236,082,542 Burundi francs for 2026/27 against 3,015,773,158 for 2025/26, a rise of 7.3%. The budget for 2026/27 gives 80,666,493,781 francs to 74 digital lines.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Fonds de Service Universel des TIC is funded by a 1% levy on operators' turnover under decree 100/054 of 29 March 2024 and its 2025/26 plan pays 4,811,751,000 francs for three pilot Villages Numériques. Its 2026/27 plan pays 11.4 billion francs for internet connectivity to public health facilities, secondary schools and community telecentres, reaching 75 health facilities and 75 secondary schools after a first 25 of each.

Not held. No budget execution report, settlement law, audited accounts or fund account from the last three years gives what was actually spent.

BEN.short: Benin cut its 2026 digital budget 6.3% from 2025 and published 2025 spending on digital lines; any fund or levy is not known.
BEN.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 digital budget of 27.2 billion CFA francs is 6.32% lower than the 29.034 billion approved for 2025, mainly through a 12.22% fall in external financing. The state's published tables put spending on digital lines for 2025 at 10,487,000,000 francs. The 2026 figure is 9.7 billion francs of operating costs and 17.4 billion of capital across three programmes. By 30 April 2026 77,247,968 francs of the Numérique programme's 12,372,151,413 had been ordered for payment.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 budget execution table gives the Numérique programme 12.4 billion francs in credits, part-paid by a loan tranche, and the ministry's piloting and support programme 2,184,235,167 francs.

Not held. The money for digital transformation was lower in the latest budget than in the one before.

BFA.short: Burkina Faso's digital lines held in both years fell 11.1% in the 2026 budget; any fund or levy for digital programmes is not known.
BFA.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital ministry's 2026 annual work plan is budgeted at 61 billion CFA francs, but the digital lines held for both years total 6,174,786,000 francs for 2026 against 6,947,413,000 for 2025, a fall of 11.1%. The execution report to 31 December 2025 shows the ministry's domestic investment ordered for payment at 2,094,406,682 francs. For 2024 the infrastructure programme shows 272,081,258 francs spent, 19.6% of the 1,387,136,000 voted. On 16 April 2026 the Council of Ministers authorised 9,113,100,000 francs of procurement for the ministry's specific projects, financed by the 2026 state budget.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 finance law appropriates 1,187,169,000 francs in domestic payment credits to the electronic communications infrastructure programme and 1,916,611,000 francs to the digital transformation and ecosystem programme.

Not held. The money for digital transformation was lower in the latest budget than in the one before.

BWA.short: Botswana's 2026/27 budget cut the communications ministry's development money; an access fund paid for centres in 2025. Full-year 2025/26 spending is not known.
BWA.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The Ministry of Communications and Innovation's development budget for 2026/27 is 473,200,000 pula, down 11.5% on the revised 2025/26 figure and 44.6% on the 2025/26 appropriation. The digital lines held for both years total 1,040,522,175 pula for 2026/27 against 1,055,985,797 for 2025/26. The budget documents publish 1,057,424,684 pula as spent on digital lines for 2024/25.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Universal Access and Service Fund Trust was established in April 2014 and is financed by a levy of up to 1% of licensed operators' annual gross turnover. Two primary-school Digital Centres, each costing 1.59 million pula, were launched on 28 November 2025 through the fund.

Not held. Nothing held shows the state's money for digital programmes higher in the latest budget than in the one before.

CAF.short: Central African Republic's 2026 budget raises digital lines 15 per cent; no fund is shown paying and spending is not known.
CAF.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital lines held for both years total 4,384,800,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 3,804,800,000 for 2025, up 15.2 per cent. The 2026 budget holds 51 digital lines worth 5,881,925,000 CFA francs. The 2026 draft proposes 300,000,000 CFA francs from domestic financing for urban optical fibre loops, and the 2025 finance bill carried 1,400,000,000 CFA francs of domestic money in support of the regulator ARCEP. It also proposes 118 million CFA francs, financed domestically, for six months of 2024 salary arrears at the state's digital development agency.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2026 budget's 51 digital lines, 5,881,925,000 CFA francs in all.

Not held. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying, and no pledge to pay for digital programmes at home is shown with an act following it.

CIV.short: Côte d'Ivoire's 2026 digital ministry budget rose 37 per cent and a telecom levy paid in 2024; the levy's law is not known.
CIV.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2024 settlement law records 23,434,278,284 CFA francs spent in 2024 on programme 22126, Economie numérique et poste. The digital ministry's 2026 budget of 83.275 billion CFA francs is described as a 37% increase, and programme 22126 rises from 19,033,679,859 CFA francs in 2025 to 45,991,319,076 in 2026. The digital lines held for both years total 148,105,376,640 CFA francs for 2026 against 157,659,408,117 for 2025, down 6.1 per cent.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. Programme 23237 is an earmarked account funded by a levy on telecom operators; the 2026 finance law appropriates 33 billion CFA francs to it. In 2024 the levy funded the ANSUT rural-technology account, and collection fell short, so the 32.3 billion voted was cut to 27,676,208,542 CFA francs.

Not held. The law that creates the levy is not named in the documents held.

CMR.short: Cameroon's tabled 2026 budget raises the digital lines held in both years 1.9 per cent; whether any fund pays is not known.
CMR.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. In the tabled 2026 finance bill the digital lines held for both years total 26,500,000,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 26,000,000,000 for 2025, up 1.9 per cent, and 14 digital lines worth 195,060,083,000 CFA francs are held for 2026. The national digital cadastre programme is named at 874,046,000 CFA francs in that bill, against 1,567,500,000 in the 2025 finance law and 1,203,574,000 in the 2024 finance law, both from domestic revenue. The budget documents publish 17,673,504,702 CFA francs as spent on digital lines for 2024.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2025 finance law's 1,567,500,000 CFA francs of domestic revenue for the digital cadastre programme.

Not held. No fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes is shown created, collecting or paying.

COD.short: The 2026 budget gives the digital section 81.7 billion Congolese francs, up from 60.6 billion; no working fund is known.
COD.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget law appropriates 81,698,223,741 Congolese francs of domestic money to section 71, Digital Economy, up from 60,627,481,411 in 2025, which the document says is largely a transfer of the digital mandate from section 52. The digital lines held for both years total 314,991,531,596 francs for 2026 against 432,043,491,504 for 2025. Section 52, posts and telecommunications, gets 53,840,917,417 francs of domestic money for 2026. For 2025 the provisional execution statement shows 31,358,784,468 francs paid against a voted 60,627,481,411, after the section had fallen about 30% from 87,134,433,991 in 2024.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. In February 2025 the secretary general of Internet Society RDC said the universal service fund was still not available.

Not held. No source from the last three years shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying.

COG.short: The 2026 budget raises the digital programme 30.5% to 30.1 billion CFA francs, and a SIM-terminal tax funds digital; its yield is unknown.
COG.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 finance law appropriates 30,139,589,283 CFA francs for programme 118, Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy, up 30.5% from 23,093,583,163 for 2025. The 2025 budget execution report gives 3,158,525,582 francs spent on the programme in 2025, excluding personnel, against a revised 23,348,037,007.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 finance law appropriates 1,000,000,000 francs to the special account for the universal access and service fund, fed by operator contributions, the same sum as in 2025 and in 2024. A tax on new SIM-card terminals, in force since 1 June 2026, was reported operating on 16 July 2026, with proceeds meant for connectivity, digital services and digital transformation.

Not held. The amount the SIM-terminal tax has collected is not stated.

COM.short: Digital lines in the 2026 budget total 541.6 million Comorian francs against 444.3 million in 2025; no fund or levy is known.
COM.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 finance law appropriates 277,128,000 Comorian francs to the state information and communication directorate, up from nothing in 2025. The digital lines held for both years total 541,558,972 francs for 2026 against 444,285,104 for 2025. The ministry's general secretariat rose from 17,546,005 francs in 2025 to 114,001,360 in 2026, including a state-paid investment line of 50,000,000. For 2024 the law appropriated 194,457,800 francs to the ministry, down from 337,232,800 in 2023. The 2024 execution report shows the posts and digital ministry spent 183,586,075 francs in 2024.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 finance law gives 50,000,000 francs as a transfer to the chambre du Numérique.

Not held. No source from the last three years shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying.

CPV.short: The 2026 budget cuts the digital ministry to 174 million Cape Verdean escudos from 370 million; the universal service fund stays flat; payouts unknown.
CPV.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital economy ministry's appropriation fell from 369,781,930 Cape Verdean escudos in 2025 to 174,200,533 in 2026. Its Digital Platform and Innovation programme is appropriated 513,994,724 escudos for 2026. It executed 558,272,390 escudos in 2025, a provisional figure, after 489,920,474 in 2024. The digital lines held for both years total 2,149,551,552 escudos for 2026 against 6,680,534,274 for 2025, and the 2026 law opens a cybersecurity budget unit with 20,000,000.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The 2026 budget law earmarks the operators' communications contribution and the radio-spectrum fee to the universal service and information society fund, with 122,073,633 escudos appropriated for 2026, the same as in 2025.

Not held. The money for digital transformation was not higher in the latest budget than in the one before. The amount the fund collected or paid out is not stated.

DJI.short: The state digital agency's 2026 budget fell about 29% from 2025, while the digital line held for both years rose; no fund is known.
DJI.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget of ANSIE, the state digital agency, is 396.1 million Djibouti francs, down from 556.7 million in 2025, a fall of about 29% that the record ties to a separate cybersecurity authority. The budget gives 485,686,344 Djibouti francs to the one digital line held for 2026, and the digital lines held for both years total 485,686,344 for 2026 against 456,943,040 for 2025. For 2024, ANSIE's approved accounts show 479.2 million francs of charges against 457.1 million of income, and 479,221,862 francs is published as spent on digital lines.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is that ANSIE's 2026 revenue is mainly the state subvention.

Not held. Nothing held shows the state's digital money rising in the latest budget over the one before.

DZA.short: Algeria's 2026 budget gives money to 10 digital lines and the state pays for universal service mobile coverage; the prior year is not known.
DZA.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget gives 20,589,518,000 Algerian dinars to 10 digital lines.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The state pays for the 201-site Mobilis 4G universal service programme, more than 27.3 billion dinars, about 204 million dollars, through the fonds d'appui du service universel, under a specification approved on 4 August 2026, with the fund set up by decree 18-247 of 2018; the document says it is not Mobilis's own investment. On 7 September 2026 the regulator launched a tender for mobile coverage of 3000 small localities, financed wholly by the state through the universal service mechanism. A similar 1,400-locality 4G programme is being completed.

Not held. The money for digital transformation is not held for two budget years running, so whether it rose is not known.

EGY.short: Egypt's digital budget lines rose 24.4% in 2026/27 over 2025/26; no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes is known.
EGY.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026/27 budget gives 30,512,114,000 Egyptian pounds to 44 digital lines. The 39 digital lines held for both years total 30,224,315,000 pounds for 2026/27 against 24,302,193,000 for 2025/26, a rise of 24.4%. For 2025/26 the Minister of Planning told the House of Representatives that 13 billion pounds of public investment is allocated to the ICT sector, of which 9 billion comes from the general budget. No figure for what was spent is held.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is a ministry document, seen by Bloomberg, saying Egypt intends to allocate up to 860 million dollars a year from the general budget from 2026/27 to 2030 for data centres, computing and AI.

Not held. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying for digital programmes.

ERI.short: Nothing held says whether the state budget funds digital programmes or whether a fund or levy pays for them, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not held. Nothing held says whether the state budget gives money to digital programmes, or that a fund or levy pays for them.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's digital budget lines rose 48.2% in 2026/27 over 2025/26; no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes is known.
ETH.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026/27 federal budget gives 35,959,539,563 birr to 125 digital lines. The 73 digital lines held for both years total 21,697,879,134 birr for 2026/27 against 14,643,622,841 for 2025/26, a rise of 48.2%. In 2024/25 the Ministry of Innovation and Technology was voted 2,754,552,330 birr and spent 989,820,128, or 35.9%. The same budget appropriates 1,484,839,300 birr to the Ministry of Innovation and Technology and 6,293,131,040 birr to the Artificial Intelligence Institution, 5,600,000,000 of it capital and 693,131,040 recurrent.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is that the 2026/27 federal budget gives the Artificial Intelligence Institution its money, all from the treasury.

Not held. No fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying for digital programmes.

GAB.short: Gabon's digital lines rose 10 per cent in the 2026 budget, and the ministry's budget rose from 32 to 82 billion CFA francs; spending unknown.
GAB.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. In the 2026 budget, the digital lines held for both years total 25,152,318,272 CFA francs for 2026 against 22,855,429,916 for 2025, a rise of 10.0 per cent, from a budget document dated 17 July 2026. The Ministry of Digital Economy, Digitalization and Innovation's own budget, as the minister presented it to the National Transition Assembly in October 2025, rises from 32 billion CFA francs in 2025 to 82 billion in 2026, an increase of 156.2 per cent. The 10 lines held for both years sit within a wider set: in all, the 2026 budget gives 30,511,992,244 CFA francs to 14 digital lines.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the budget itself, which names no fund, levy or assigned tax for digital programmes: it lists 14 digital lines for 2026, 30,511,992,244 CFA francs in all, and the ministry's 82 billion CFA francs is the figure the minister presented for 2026.

Not held. Nothing held shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it: no fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying. Nothing held gives what was spent.

GHA.short: Ghana's digital lines held for both years rose from 42 million to 258 million cedis in the 2026 budget; spending is not known.
GHA.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. In the 2026 budget, the digital lines held for both years total 258,438,014 cedis for 2026 against 42,313,121 for 2025, a rise of 510.8 per cent, and 35 digital lines in all receive 1,668,447,220 cedis in 2026. The Appropriation (No. 2) Act, 2025 appropriates 100,000,000 cedis for the ICT Capacity Development programme of the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations for 2026, wholly from domestic revenue (60 million for goods and services, 40 million for capital). The ministry's budget estimates give 536,745,448 cedis of domestic money to the National Information Technology Agency sub-programme for 2026, made up of 42,486,769 cedis from the Government of Ghana and 494,258,679 of internally generated funds. A further 138,000,000 of donor money is left out of that figure. The Cyber Security Authority sub-programme receives 25,346,198 cedis for 2026.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2026 appropriation for ICT Capacity Development, paid wholly from domestic revenue.

Not held. Nothing held shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it: no fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying. Nothing held gives what was spent.

GIN.short: Guinea's digital lines nearly doubled in the 2025 budget, and a May 2026 decree created a fund financed by a levy; spending is unknown.
GIN.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. In the 2025 budget, the digital lines held for both years total 13,441,441,299 Guinean francs for 2025 against 6,758,097,055 for 2024, a rise of 98.9 per cent. In all, the 2025 budget gives 347,913,391,946 Guinean francs to 113 digital lines. The 2025 budget law is dated 31 December 2024, and the four lines held for both years are a small part of those 113.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. A decree signed by President Doumbouya on 21 May 2026 created the Digital Sovereignty Fund, to be financed mainly by revenue from a new 3 per cent Digital Compliance Fee on foreign digital services. It is to fund technology infrastructure, cybersecurity, training and innovation. Enforcement of the fee follows a six-month transition, and no money is yet reported collected or paid.

Not held. No budget execution report, settlement law, audited accounts or fund account from the last three years gives what was actually spent.

GMB.short: The Gambia's digital lines rose 5 per cent in the 2026 budget, and 75 million dalasi is published as spent for 2025; any fund unknown.
GMB.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. In the 2026 budget, the digital lines held for both years total 537,355,897 dalasi for 2026 against 511,618,456 for 2025, a rise of 5.0 per cent, and 24 digital lines in all receive 661,855,897 dalasi in 2026. The 20 lines held for both years are part of the 24 lines held for 2026. The 2025 budget document publishes 75,000,000 dalasi as actually spent on digital lines for 2025.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 24 digital lines in the 2026 budget, 661,855,897 dalasi in all, a budget document dated 5 January 2026 that names no fund, levy or assigned tax for them.

Not held. Nothing held shows the government saying digital transformation must be paid for from the country's own resources and acting on it: no fund, levy or assigned tax is shown created, collecting or paying.

GNB.short: The 2026 budget gives 129 million CFA francs to six digital lines, lower than 2025 on shared lines; spending and any fund are not known.
GNB.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget gives 129,000,000 CFA francs to six digital lines. The digital lines held for both years total 70,000,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 130,000,000 for 2025, a fall of 46.2 per cent. Three of the six lines are held in both years, and the budget document is dated 1 December 2025. No spending figure is held.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. Nothing held states a fund, levy or assigned tax paying for digital programmes. The nearest held fact is the 2026 budget's six digital lines. That budget is the only held source on the state's own digital money, and the figure it gives for all six lines is 129,000,000 CFA francs for 2026.

Not held. The digital lines were lower in the 2026 budget than in the one before. No spending figure is held.

GNQ.short: The 2026 budget gives 23.5 billion Central African francs to 113 digital lines, slightly down on 2025 for shared lines; no fund is known.
GNQ.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026 budget gives 23,476,749,000 Central African CFA francs to 113 digital lines. The ten lines held for both years total 8,528,000,000 for 2026 against 8,668,000,000 for 2025, a fall of 1.6 per cent. The budget law is dated 9 December 2025. The 2024 budget document publishes 5,132,000,000 as spent on digital lines for 2024.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. Nothing held states a fund, levy or assigned tax paying for digital programmes. The nearest held fact is the 113 digital lines in the 2026 budget, and the 2026 budget law is the only held source on the state's own digital money for that year.

Not held. The digital lines were lower in the 2026 budget than in the one before, or the same. No fund or levy is held.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2026/27 budget cut the digital package to 8.6 billion shillings, and the Universal Service Fund paid for projects; its legal basis is not known.
KEN.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 2026/27 budget appropriates KES 12,763,784,217 to the State Department for ICT and Digital Economy, and the digital superhighway and creative economy package fell to 8.6 billion shillings, the second cut running after 16.3 billion and 12.7 billion. The digital lines held for both years total 43,931,556,738 shillings for the latest budget year, 2026/27, against 37,618,002,025 for 2025/26. 29,085,287,000 shillings is published as spent on digital lines for 2024/25.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Communications Authority's Universal Service Fund funded the Digital Superhighway backbone and metro fibre procurement, a fund the Communications Authority administers, and, in August 2026, a skilling project for 120,000 people across 19 counties.

Not held. The state's digital money was lower in the latest budget than in the one before on the main figures.

LBR.short: Liberia's FY2026 budget gives 12.5 million US dollars to 14 digital lines and its Universal Access Fund installs links; the 2025 comparison is not known.
LBR.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The FY2026 budget gives 12,464,422 US dollars to 14 digital lines, taken from the national budget document. 731,376 US dollars is published as spent on digital lines for FY2025.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Liberia Telecommunications Authority created the Universal Access Fund by regulation on 10 September 2015, with licensee contributions of 0.5 per cent of annual gross revenues for its first year. The regulation states no collections or payments. The fund is run by the Liberia Telecommunications Authority. On 20 October 2025 the fund reported installing Starlink in Vahun District, Lofa County, a project overseen on site by Commissioner Patrick R. Honnah, with no cost given.

Not held. Nothing held gives the digital money in two budget years running, so whether it rose is not known.

LBY.short: Libya's 2025 budget held its digital lines level against 2024; whether any fund pays for digital programmes is not known.
LBY.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The budget for 2025 gives 1,127,365,400 Libyan dinars to 36 digital lines, and the digital lines held for both years total 1,064,321,200 dinars for 2025 against 1,064,321,200 for 2024. The Central Bank of Libya's statements show the General Authority for Communications and affiliates spent 41,157,054.743 dinars in 2025, of which 28,983,614.952 was Chapter 1, 7,073,439.791 Chapter 2 and 5,100,000 development, and 31,673,827.99 dinars from 1 January to 30 September 2026.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2025 budget's 1,127,365,400 dinars across 36 digital lines. The Central Bank's statement for 2025 gives the authority's line only, with no fund collections.

Not held. The money for digital programmes was no higher in the 2025 budget than in 2024. No fund, levy or assigned tax is held.

LSO.short: Lesotho's digital budget lines rose 38.4 percent for 2026/27, after 539.7 million maloti spent in 2024/25; whether any fund pays is not known.
LSO.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital lines held for both years total 1,003,814,035 maloti for 2026/27 against 725,488,825 for 2025/26, a rise of 38.4 per cent between the two years, and the budget gives 1,046,745,257 maloti to 13 digital lines for 2026/27. The same budget book, dated 30 April 2026, publishes 539,710,000 maloti as spent on digital lines for 2024/25.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the finance minister's 2025/26 budget speech, which allocates 381.1 million maloti to the ICT sector for digital innovation, inclusion and transformation, with no funding source given. The 2026/27 budget book gives 1,046,745,257 maloti to 13 digital lines in all.

Not held. No fund, levy or assigned tax is held as created, collecting or paying in the last three years.

MAR.short: Morocco's digital budget lines fell 8.1 percent in 2026 and 1.63 billion dirhams was spent in 2024; whether any fund pays now is not known.
MAR.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The digital lines held for both years total 2,263,927,000 dirhams for 2026 against 2,463,927,000 for 2025, a fall of 8.1 per cent in the finance law published on 16 December 2025. The Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform's own budget page shows a rise from 1,508.4 million dirhams in 2023 to 2,032.4 million in 2024. The 2024 finance law document publishes 1,626,668,886 dirhams as spent on digital lines for 2024.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The nearest held fact is the 2026 budget's 2,263,927,000 dirhams across 4 digital lines. The ministry budget for 2024 was 2,032.4 million dirhams, of which 1,758.725 million investment and 187.840 million materials and miscellaneous.

Not held. The money for digital programmes was lower in the 2026 budget than in 2025. No source from the last three years shows a fund, levy or assigned tax collecting or paying for a digital programme.

MDG.short: Madagascar's digital budget lines fell 2.0 percent in 2026, while a telecoms fund paid for projects in 2022-2025; what it collects is not known.
MDG.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The 50 digital lines held for both years total 9,703,842,000 ariary for 2026 against 9,904,335,000 for 2025, a fall of 2.0 per cent, and the amended finance law for 2026 gives 53,583,872,000 ariary to 95 digital lines. A financial report published in September 2026 gives 100,864,138,247 ariary as spent on digital lines for 2025.

A commitment to pay at home, and the act that follows it. The Court of Accounts audit says the Fonds de Développement des Télécommunications et des TIC was created and is managed by the telecoms minister, and made large expenditures in 2022-2025, including part-financing of e-Fokontany, which spent 21,541,224,988.66 ariary over 2022-2025 across five funding sources.

Not held. The money for digital programmes was lower in the 2026 budget than in 2025. The law creating the fund and the amount it collected are not held.

MLI.short: The state's digital lines rose 4.1 per cent for 2026, and the universal access fund published its collections and spending for early 2026.
MLI.summary:
Money in the state budget, its direction and what was spent. The universal access fund agency AGEFAU spent 3,188,967,162 CFA francs in the first half of 2026, 8% of its annual budget. The digital lines held for both years total 10,339,800,000 CFA francs for 2026 against 9,935,715,000 for 2025, up 4.1 per cent; the same document gives 24,314,962,000 CFA francs to 103 digital lines for 2026.
