NER.short: Broadband was reported extended to 266 communes in 2026; the total of communes and what their offices do over it are not known.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Projet Villages Intelligents is run by a project management unit under a steering committee chaired by the national agency ANSI, and is financed by the State of Niger and the World Bank at USD 100 million, closing on 23 October 2026. The communications minister said in March 2025 that a programme to connect all communes awaited the adoption of a national digital policy.

What the office does over it. The Council of Ministers stated on 22 April 2026 that the computerised national civil status register is operational in 102 communes.

How the office is connected. The project extended broadband to communes as public service provision, alongside health centres and schools, and Le Sahel reports the broadband connectivity of the mairies delivered to the town halls by the project.

Last twelve months. The mairies' connectivity was officially received at a ceremony on 6 May 2026, in the presence of the communications minister and the World Bank's resident representative.

Local governments connected. The project told the news agency ANP, in a report published on 15 April 2026, that broadband internet had been extended to 266 communes, 339 health centres and 298 schools.

Not held. No total of communes is given beside the 266, and nothing says that the commune offices themselves are on the connection or what they do over it. The civil status register is not said to be reached online.

NGA.short: 510 local government administration offices were counted on broadband in December 2025; how many offices there are, and what they do online, is not known.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's BRIDGE project, approved on 6 October 2025, sets a target of 3,428 local government administration offices on broadband by September 2030. The Bank names the Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy as implementing agency; a company in which private investors are to hold the majority, not yet incorporated on 4 August 2026, is to build the fibre. Of the Bank's US$500 million credit, nothing was disbursed at 24 July 2026.

What the office does over it. The Bank's results framework records the offices as connected to broadband internet at 17 December 2025. Local government area offices enter health facilities' monthly paper returns into the national DHIS2, on the Federal Ministry of Health's report for 2021.

How the office is connected. The Bank counts the local government administration offices themselves as facilities connected to broadband.

Last twelve months. The credit was signed on 30 December 2025 and the project declared effective on 27 April 2026. On 22 September 2026 the communications minister cut the delivery timeline from five years to three, with cable laying to begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Local governments connected. The World Bank counts 510 local government administration offices connected to broadband at 17 December 2025, the same number as in July 2025.

Not held. How many local government administration offices there are, and so what share the 510 is; where the connected offices are, who provides or pays for their connections and what is done over them. No domestic budget line is stated, and no office is yet connected by the project.

RWA.short: District offices worked in the national civil registration system in 2024 and 2025; how many of the districts are connected is not known.
RWA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Governance and Decentralisation Sector Strategic Plan 2024-2029, dated 14 November 2024, costs an intervention giving local government entities ICT equipment and internet connectivity, with the Ministry of Local Government among those responsible. The World Bank-funded Digital Acceleration Project, running 2022 to 2026, plans a government network linking institutions at central, district, sector and cell levels, lawmakers were told on 7 July 2025.

What the office does over it. The civil registration system the National Institute of Statistics calls NCI-CRVS was fully operational at district, sector and cell offices for 2025, as it was in 2024. Engineers at City and District One Stop Centers process building permits in Kubaka, launched in April 2025, and sector offices make all their financial transactions in the national financial management system, on the sector plan of November 2024.

How the office is connected. Ministerial instructions of 12 March 2012 prescribe state-procured bandwidth delivered to central and local government institutions over the national fibre backbone, each institution paying the access fee. Cells, the sub-offices below the sector, have no internet connectivity, on the Ministry of Local Government's assessment published in September 2025.

Last twelve months. Births and deaths in communities are registered at the cell, where before they were registered at the sector, the Ministry of Local Government stated in June 2026.

Local governments connected. Connectivity remains a problem especially at sector and cell level in peri-urban and rural areas, a study published in September 2022 found.

Not held. The share or number of district offices connected, and who provides or pays for a district office's connection. Whether the government network planned to link the districts has been built, and any event at a district office in the last twelve months.

SDN.short: A 2022 meeting recommended fibre for localities that ask; whether any locality office is connected is not known, so no stage is set.
SDN.summary: Not held. No source puts a locality office on a connection, names what an office does over one or counts the localities connected. The one statement held is a meeting's recommendation of 22 November 2022 that Sudatel connect by fibre the localities that ask, at their own cost, with no locality reported connected.

SEN.short: By June 2026, 400 civil-status centres run by communes were linked to the national register; the share of communes connected is not known.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The national civil-status agency ANEC, under the ministry for local authorities, runs the interconnection of the civil-status centres, with the state company SENUM SA installing the network equipment, as stated in August 2025. The NEKKAL programme that interconnected them was financed by the European Union and executed by Civipol and Enabel.

What the office does over it. Agents at the civil-status centres, which the communes run, register and issue acts in the national civil-status register, hosted at three national sites: 108,233 declarations from 1 January to 3 July 2025, on ANEC's figures.

How the office is connected. SENUM SA put network equipment in on site at 383 centres, 235 of them in service and connected to the network, in ANEC's presentation of August 2025. The communal land offices were not yet connected to the internet in November 2025, on a World Bank mission's account.

Last twelve months. NEKKAL's final steering committee reported 400 civil registration centres interconnected on 29 June 2026. SENUM launched the pilot phase of its PRODAP project in six communes on 24 April 2026.

Local governments connected. The application ANEC calls NEKKAL was deployed in 400 civil-status centres, with access to the central database, at 5 November 2025, on its director-general's word. In the 138 communes of the World Bank's land project, no municipal land bureau was equipped and operational with access to the land information system at 21 November 2025.

Not held. No share of communes connected is held: no source sets the 400 civil-status centres against a count of communes, and ANEC's director general said on 27 April 2026 that in some centres the circuit was never completed and elsewhere it is very slow. Who pays for the centres' links after the donor programme closed is not stated.

SLE.short: All 21 councils had internet and a national accounting system live in early 2026, the finance ministry says; who pays afterwards is not known.
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Finance reports the roll-out to the councils as its own work and procured the councils' internet service itself, on a contract signed on 12 August 2025 and charged to a World Bank grant. The National Digital Development Strategy of December 2022 sets 2027 for extending broadband to all government institutions, local councils among them.

What the office does over it. PFM Smart, the ministry's name for a web-based, real-time accounting system, went live in all 21 local councils in the first quarter of 2026. At Freetown City Council in 2025 transactions were processed live and payment instructions printed from the system.

How the office is connected. The roll-out included the provision of an internet facility for 21 local councils and a local area network at 21, by the ministry's report. The ministry hired a provider of internet services for the local councils, to support the accounting system. In 2023 seven councils outside Freetown reached the internet through individually provided modems.

Last twelve months. In the first quarter of 2026 the system went live in all 21 councils, with solar panels and batteries installed at 18. The internet contract is shown as completed on 18 November 2025, ahead of a planned 26 February 2026.

Local governments connected. 21 of 21 local councils, by the Ministry of Finance's count for the first quarter of 2026. In 2025 one council, Freetown City Council, was live.

Not held. The ministry's report gives no rural share, states live transactions only for Freetown City Council, and counts 21 councils in one place and 22 in another. The internet contract names no number of councils served, and no source says who pays for the service afterwards or names a domestic budget line.

SOM.short: A 2022 report says finance systems are implemented in all municipalities; how their offices are connected is not known.
SOM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National ICT Policy and Strategy 2019-2024 set the goal that all local authorities of the federal government and the member states have internet access by its third year, with costs left to each agency. It made the ICT Department of the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Technology responsible for connectivity in government.

What the office does over it. The World Bank's Digital Economy Diagnostic of 2022 says the web-based financial management systems of the federal government, Puntland and Somaliland, which it names SFMIS, PLFMIS and SLFMIS, have each been implemented in all ministries, departments and agencies, state-owned enterprises and municipalities.

How the office is connected. The 2019 policy lists local authorities among the rural public services whose connectivity is to be built in a co-ordinated way.

Last twelve months. The policy that set the target for local authorities ran from 2019 to 2024.

Local governments connected. The 2022 diagnostic says the finance systems are implemented in "all" municipalities of the federal government, Puntland and Somaliland.

Not held. No source says how any municipal office is connected, or that municipal staff work in the finance systems at their own offices, and no count or total of municipalities is given. Nothing on record is dated within the last three years.

SSD.short: One county office of eleven assessed had its own satellite link in 2021; how many of the country's counties are connected is not known.
SSD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Maban County has two satellite terminals, one for the Office of the Commissioner and one for the Health Department, on an assessment of eleven local governments that the International Organization for Migration (IOM) carried out from September to December 2021.

What the office does over it. The Commissioner's office in Maban has a satellite terminal, IOM found in late 2021.

How the office is connected. The Maban office is connected by a satellite terminal of its own, as of 2021. In Renk and Rubkona the only terminal is the Health Department's, and the Commissioner's office and every other department have none. Baliet, Fashoda, Leer, Pariang, Pibor, Raja, Wau County and Wau Municipality have no terminal and report a need for one across all departments.

Last twelve months. IOM's assessment of the eleven locations dates from September to December 2021.

Local governments connected. One of the eleven local governments IOM assessed in late 2021, ten counties and Wau Municipality, has a satellite terminal at the Commissioner's office, and ten have none.

Not held. No count of connected offices across all the country's counties, no use named for the Maban terminal, who pays for it, and nothing on governance or on any event since 2021. The one assessment held omits Maban from its own recommendations section.

STP.short: Whether any district council office is connected is not known as at 2026, so no stage is set.
STP.summary: Not held. Which institutions are on the government network, and whether any district council is. The digital governance strategy is held cut off before its network chapter.

SWZ.short: One town council, Ezulwini, reported its own office internet line in the year to March 2024; how many councils are connected is not known.
SWZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Digital Eswatini Project is implemented by the Ministry of Information, Communications and Technology and financed by USD 65.0 million of World Bank loans and credit approved on 15 June 2026. Town councils meet their ICT costs from their own budgets, in Ezulwini's accounts for the year to March 2024 and Mbabane's for the year to March 2023.

What the office does over it. Ezulwini Town Council moved to Microsoft Office 365 for business email, installed virtual conferencing equipment and ran its telephone lines over the internet line in the year to March 2024. In Mbabane the council's IT Section has automated municipal activities, mail tracking among them (year to March 2023).

How the office is connected. Ezulwini Town Council carries its five office telephone lines over the office's internet line (year to March 2024). The Municipal Council of Mbabane pays for internet among its utility services (year to March 2023).

Last twelve months. The House of Assembly gave a second reading on 21 September 2026 to the three Bills enabling the project's loans. COMESA reports that from January to June 2026 the project was in preparation, with its infrastructure assessment begun.

Local governments connected. One urban local authority, Ezulwini Town Council, reports on its own office's internet line (year to March 2024), and the capital's council reports paying for internet at its offices (year to March 2023). Thirty-eight Tinkhundla centres are set to benefit from broadband, with rollout expected in 2027.

Not held. No share or total of local governments with a connected office is published, and no Tinkhundla centre is reported connected. No national or shared system is named as worked in over the councils' connections.

SYC.short: All 27 listed district administrations had a government email address in 2025; how their offices are connected is not known.
SYC.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Office of the President's government directory places the district administration offices under the Ministry of Local Government and Community Affairs, as from 1 March 2025.

What the office does over it. Each of the 27 district administration offices has its own office mailbox on the government's gov.sc domain, from anseauxpinsda@gov.sc to takamakada@gov.sc, as from 1 March 2025.

How the office is connected. The directory gives each district administration office a gov.sc mailbox beside an office telephone number (1 March 2025).

Last twelve months. The directory lists the district administrations and their mailboxes as from 1 March 2025.

Local governments connected. The directory's table of district administrations lists 27 districts, Praslin's two and La Digue among them, and gives every one of the 27 an office mailbox on gov.sc (1 March 2025).

Not held. How the district administration offices are connected is not stated, and none is said to be on the government network. No total of districts, no system the offices work in, and nothing on governance or on the last twelve months is held.

TCD.short: Internet kits and subscriptions were handed to 23 communes in 2026; whether the links are in service and the total of communes are not known.
TCD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The World Bank's appraisal of the Chad Digital Transformation Project, dated 4 September 2024, names the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy as implementing agency, puts its financing at an IDA grant of US$92.2 million equivalent within a US$120 million total, and provides for last-mile connectivity to selected public institutions, local government offices among them. The 2027 budget orientations, reported on 4 August 2026, provide for generalising the public finance system SIGFiP to the collectivités territoriales.

What the office does over it. The national agency ANATS said, in a report published on 3 June 2025, that its civil registration system links municipalities, among other points, which send their data by SMS to the agency for validation.

How the office is connected. The finance ministry stated on 19 May 2026 that the equipment handed to communes under the project it calls PATN included Starlink Business kits with antenna, router and Wi-Fi, monthly internet subscriptions and Wi-Fi access points.

Last twelve months. The finance ministry reported on 19 May 2026 the official handover of the kits and subscriptions, with computers, printers and copiers, made with the World Bank's support at a ceremony chaired by the Secretary of State for Finance and Budget.

Local governments connected. The 23 communes that are provincial capitals received the equipment, the finance ministry stated on 19 May 2026.

Not held. Nothing says that a commune's link is in service, and no national total of communes is given beside the 23. The municipalities sending civil registration data are not counted or placed, and nothing says a connection is provided to their offices.

TGO.short: A birth-records platform was at pilot in four communes in 2026 and town hall fibre had not begun; how town halls connect is not known.
TGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The digital ministry's resettlement plan of July 2026 names the ministry's project unit as promoter of the fibre extension that is to reach town halls, under the Projet d'Accélération Numérique du Togo, a 100 million dollar project with a target of 136 town hall buildings, implemented with the World Bank. KfW's records show a EUR 20 million grant committed in 2024 and a EUR 15 million grant committed in 2025 to connect town halls, hospitals and schools to the fibre network.

What the office does over it. Under a pilot in Vo prefecture, Togo First reported in May 2026, the mairie reaches in the platform Naissance Keva the newborn's data entered at the maternity, to draw up the birth record. In Lacs 1, UNDP reported in May 2021, the Kadodo application shares data in real time between health centres and the town hall's civil registry.

How the office is connected. The government's site said on 7 February 2026 that the town hall digitalisation project it calls PDiMa is to connect the 136 municipal buildings themselves.

Last twelve months. The Vo pilot has been deployed since February 2026, and the final resettlement plan for the Maritime region's fibre works was issued in July 2026, with the operator still to be recruited.

Local governments connected. The platform is a pilot in the four communes of Vo prefecture. The July 2026 plan states that the fibre works to the 136 town hall buildings had not begun.

Not held. Nothing says how any town hall is connected, and no figure is given for town halls connected by means other than the planned fibre. Outside the pilots, the one commune on record as working online is Lacs 1, in 2021, with no total.

TUN.short: Sixteen municipalities worked in a national permit system in 2026; how many municipalities have a connected office is not known.
TUN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Communication Technologies' performance plan for 2025 makes the connection of public bodies' sites to the integrated administrative network an indicator of its digital development programme, targeting 98 per cent in 2025 and 100 per cent from 2026. It lists the network for the municipalities among the projects financed through the communications development fund.

What the office does over it. Since 24 June 2026 municipalities issue building permits in the national platform Tunisia calls Taamir, from the application to the final signature. The Centre National de l'Informatique states that municipalities and municipal arrondissements work on the centralised national civil status database it calls Madania.

How the office is connected. The Centre National de l'Informatique states that workstations installed in municipalities are connected to the servers of the state's data centre. The 2025 plan names RNIA3 as the administrative network for local collectivities and municipalities.

Last twelve months. On 24 June 2026 the Municipality of Tunis issued the first building permit handled entirely online and Taamir's extension to 16 municipalities began. On 31 August 2026 the Ministry of the Interior launched a remote service for translated birth extracts whose requests go directly to the municipality of registration.

Local governments connected. Taamir was extended to 16 named municipalities on 24 June 2026. The 2025 plan estimates that 71 per cent of the public bodies' sites programmed for the administrative network were connected in 2024, counting ministries, local collectivities, municipalities and sectoral networks together.

Not held. The number of municipalities whose offices are connected, and the total of municipalities to set the 16 against. How the municipal offices working in Taamir are connected, and how many municipal offices are on the administrative network.

TZA.short: In 2025, 174 district councils worked in a national loans system and councils are on the government network; the share connected is not known.
TZA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The e-Government Authority's roadmap of February 2024 sets out a strategy to expand GovNet to all facilities of local government authorities, ministries, departments and agencies. The Digital Economy Strategic Framework 2024-2034 targets 184 local government authorities on a structured office network and GovNet by June 2026. African Business reported in August 2026 that the World Bank-financed Digital Tanzania Project supports the extension of broadband to local government offices.

What the office does over it. The deputy minister for regional administration and local government said district councils process, disburse and collect repayment of the ten per cent special-group loans in the state-run system Tanzania calls WEZESHA. The Controller and Auditor General reports that local government authorities issued bills through the revenue system TAUSI in the year to 30 June 2025.

How the office is connected. The e-Government Authority states that local government authorities, with ministries, departments and agencies, are connected on GovNet, the government communication network.

Last twelve months. On 1 May 2026 the Geita Regional Commissioner directed District Executive Directors and other employers to pay for employees' internet from internal revenues, after the trade union congress said many public employees in the region buy internet bundles with their own money.

Local governments connected. 174 district councils were authorised to issue loans through WEZESHA between July 2024 and December 2025, after a pilot in 10. The e-Government Authority's roadmap of February 2024 gives 265 ministries, departments, agencies and local government authorities on GovNet, as one figure.

Not held. The share of councils whose own offices are connected: the 174 district councils come with no total, and the 265 bodies on GovNet are not divided between central bodies and local government authorities. How the offices of the councils working in the national systems are connected.

UGA.short: In 2022, 60.6 per cent of districts, municipalities and town councils answering a survey had office internet; the share of all is not known.
UGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. NITA-U, the state's IT authority, was the internet provider of 70.1 per cent of connected local governments in its 2022 survey. The Uganda Communications Commission reports that the fourth National Development Plan, for 2025/26 to 2029/30, sets a target of extending high-speed internet to local government offices. On 6 December 2023 Parliament authorised borrowing of up to RMB 1,050 million from the Export-Import Bank of China for Phase V of the national backbone.

What the office does over it. A gender ministry study states that as of July 2022 all local governments had been migrated to the Integrated Financial Management System. NITA-U's 2022 survey found that local governments used the internet mostly for email, 90.9 per cent, and for services to the public, 74 per cent.

How the office is connected. In NITA-U's 2022 survey local governments gave staff internet over institution wireless networks and institution-owned USB modems.

Last twelve months. On 22 September 2026 the Ministry of Local Government launched its web-based accounting tool, which it calls SCART, in Hoima city's two divisions and supplied a laptop and a router for it. On 1 December 2025 the President launched the backbone's extension in Kanungu District, to connect the district headquarters and sub-counties.

Local governments connected. NITA-U's National IT Survey, of January to April 2022, found that 60.6 per cent of the local government administrations that answered it had institutional internet access; 95 of 128 sampled districts gave full data, with 17 municipalities and 10 town councils.

Not held. The share of all local governments connected, any share later than 2022, and the rural share: the survey's figure counts those that answered. A domestic budget line for connecting local governments, and how the lower local governments using SCART outside Hoima are connected.

ZAF.short: Municipalities across the Eastern Cape have worked in a shared disaster system since 2025; how many municipalities' offices are connected is not known.
ZAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality told the National Council of Provinces in November 2025 that its network upgrade is its own project, run under a council-approved ICT governance framework, and that it has adopted a three-year ICT strategic plan naming broadband as an outcome. It said that it faces limited resources and an inadequate budget for ICT.

What the office does over it. The State Information Technology Agency said in July 2026 that municipalities across the Eastern Cape are operational on its Provincial Disaster Management Application System. The Road Traffic Infringement Agency names the integration of municipalities with the national traffic information system among the upgrades behind the AARTO rollout. Mangaung has moved its email to a cloud platform, migrating 900 user accounts beside 600 already there.

How the office is connected. By November 2025 Mangaung had appointed a service provider to upgrade its network infrastructure across its seven towns, with the first phase under way, and was still appointing an internet service provider for last-mile connectivity.

Last twelve months. The Eastern Cape disaster system went live on 21 November 2025, with training for provincial and municipal users. AARTO entered its second phase in July 2026, expanding to 62 municipalities.

Local governments connected. One metropolitan municipality, Mangaung, reports an upgrade of its own network. Interviews with nine managers of rural local municipalities in Limpopo, published in 2025, found that only communication had been digitally transformed, through social media and Microsoft Teams.

Not held. A share or a count of municipalities connected against the national total, and how the offices working in the Eastern Cape system and the rural Limpopo offices are connected. Whether Mangaung's last-mile provider has been appointed, who pays for its upgrade, and the years its plan covers.

ZMB.short: Government counted 93 of 116 councils on its network in 2025 and all 116 in March 2026; the rural share is not known.
ZMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The National Electronic Government Plan 2023-2026 commits to extending the Government Wide Area Network to the 116 district administrative centres and local authorities. It names the Electronic Government Division as the network's deployer and says implementation will depend largely on domestic financing through annual budget allocations.

What the office does over it. Smart Zambia's national coordinator said on 24 March 2026 that data entry into the Constituency Development Fund system was under way across councils. A survey of 2023 found every local authority it covered undertaking e-procurement on the national e-GP platform, and 70% reporting constraints including unstable internet.

How the office is connected. The budget address of 26 September 2025 says Government connected local authorities to the Government Wide Area Network. SMART Zambia said on 7 July 2026 that all local authorities in North-Western Province were on it over fibre.

Last twelve months. Smart Zambia called the connection of all 116 councils complete on 24 March 2026, and announced North-Western Province's local authorities connected on 7 July 2026.

Local governments connected. Each government count puts at least 93 of the 116 councils on the network, the finance minister's figure of 26 September 2025. Smart Zambia's chief technical officer said on 24 March 2026 that all 116 were connected, as did its national coordinator in a briefing published the next day. An article of 26 August 2026 reports one council, Sinazongwe, given high-speed internet under an initiative that seeks to connect all 116.

Not held. The rural share of the councils connected, and whether the 116 stated in March 2026 included Sinazongwe and the North-Western Province councils reported connected later that year. Whether council staff enter Constituency Development Fund data at their own offices, and a budget line for council connections.

ZWE.short: Government handed over 250 satellite kits for local authorities in 2025; whether any council office is connected is not known.
ZWE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The government, through the Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services, donated 250 Starlink satellite kits to the Ministry of Local Government for local authorities, reported on 24 July 2025, with deployment, management and maintenance left to the councils. Manyame Rural District Council's chief executive said in April 2026 that its US$491,039 digitalisation programme, connectivity included, is funded from the approved council budget.

What the office does over it. Masvingo's Minister of State for Provincial Affairs said the Starlink kits given to schools, clinics and local authorities in the province in the first half of 2026 improved internet connectivity and access to digital services.

How the office is connected. Local authorities in Masvingo Province received Starlink kits in the first and second quarters of 2026. For the 250 kits handed over nationally in July 2025, installation and use were still to come.

Last twelve months. Manyame Rural District Council began in December 2025 a programme of phased investment in software, hardware, connectivity and training, due to be complete by December 2026. In the first half of 2026 104 Starlink kits were distributed in Masvingo Province.

Local governments connected. The provincial minister gives Masvingo's 104 kits as one total for schools, clinics and local authorities. In October 2021 a network link from councils to the National Data Centre had been piloted in four councils.

Not held. Whether any local authority's office is connected and working over its connection, and how many are: no installed or activated kit is reported, and Manyame's connection is not said to be live. A plan naming the connection of local authorities, and who pays the kits' subscriptions.

AGO.short: A finance ministry system recording municipal payers and fees was put in all 164 municipalities by 2021; how many record in it is not known.
AGO.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Finance launched and runs the Portal do Munícipe under Presidential Decree 47/18. In November 2021 its Secretary of State presented it as a ministry tool, run with the ministry's SETIC-FP IT service, that the municipalities use.

What is recorded. In November 2021 the Portal held the records of residents and their households and tracked the whole cycle of fees, licences and fines billed by local administrations, with payment by the state's single payment reference.

Where the record is held. The ministry describes the Portal as a centralised system reached over the web, with revenue deposited in a Treasury sub-account. In August 2019 it let central bodies see the amounts local administrations collect.

Last twelve months. The ministry officially launched the Portal on 10 November 2021 across the 164 municipalities.

Local governments recording. The Secretary of State for Finance said on 10 November 2021 that the Portal was implemented in all 164 municipalities, with telecommunications problems in some. In August 2019 the ministry said it had created the technical conditions for it in 152 of 164.

Not held. No share or count of the municipalities whose staff record in the Portal. Nothing dated after November 2021, so the system's current plan, finance and progress are not shown.

BDI.short: Thirty communes collect local revenue electronically by 2026, recording payments only; where the record is held and the share of communes are not known.
BDI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Interior ministry's revised budget for 2025/26 carries a line of 2,000,000,000 BIF from the domestic state budget for extending the digitalisation of revenue collection in the communes. The digitalisation master plan adopted on 10 May 2023 includes an initiative to digitalise communal tax collection. One platform in use, IBB M+, is run by Interbank Burundi, a bank.

What is recorded. In Kayanza in June 2025, 48 of the commune's 54 collectors used point-of-sale machines, with the revenue transferred digitally to the commune's account. In May 2026 IBB M+ took payments from traders by phone or through agents, notified a commune officer of each transaction and kept the data to follow revenue.

Where the record is held. In 2021 the Direction of Communal Finances was considering an IT solution to replace the manual collection of communal taxes.

Last twelve months. Butihinda commune trained its planning and accounting staff on IBB M+ on 5 May 2026, for use from the 2026–2027 budget year.

Local governments recording. The Interior ministry's third-quarter execution report for 2025/26 lists 30 communes digitalised in communal revenue. A UNDP mission of June 2025 reported the E-Taxe system operational in communes such as Kayanza.

Not held. No register of payers is described in any system, and where the electronic record is held is not stated. The 30 communes carry no total, so no share of communes is given.

BEN.short: Twelve of 77 communes were selected in 2019 for cash-desk software that records payments; whether they were equipped and use it is not known.
BEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The PAACOL project, which equips communes with cash-desk software, is coordinated by the AIMF and implemented with the ANCB, the communes' association. In September 2019 its 743 million CFA francs came from the European Union, the AIMF and the ANCB.

What is recorded. The project's single cash window for non-tax revenue has software that records each payment, as described in September 2019.

Where the record is held. The software is networked within the commune, so that information is shared among the communal actors concerned.

Last twelve months. The project, begun in 2017 for three years, was to equip its selected communes during 2019/2020.

Local governments recording. In September 2019 the project had selected 12 of Benin's 77 communes to be equipped with the cash windows.

Not held. Whether the 12 selected communes were equipped and their cash desks went into use. Nothing dated after September 2019.

BFA.short: State tax services run tax billing and collection (2021); whether any collectivité territoriale keeps a digital record is not known, so no stage is set.
BFA.summary: Not held. Whether any collectivité territoriale keeps its own digital revenue record. No source on local government revenue records is held.

BWA.short: One city council has an online rates payment channel (2024); whether any council keeps a digital record is not known, so no stage is set.
BWA.summary: Not held. Whether any council keeps a digital revenue register or receipt record. Nothing held says the national tax system collects any council revenue.

CAF.short: Bangui agreed with a private firm in December 2025 to digitise its municipal revenue; whether the system is in use is not known.
CAF.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Under an agreement signed with the Mairie de Bangui in December 2025, BMI-WFS, a firm under Ivorian law, is to run the city's digital collection system.

What is recorded. In late 2020 municipal agents began a door-to-door census of traders in central Bangui, to build a taxpayer database with an individual sheet showing what each owes.

Where the record is held. In December 2020 a city-centre trader told RFI that Bangui town hall had no computerised file of taxpayers and that its collectors issued paper receipts.

Last twelve months. The agreement to digitise Bangui's municipal revenue was signed on 12 December 2025 in the presence of the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralisation.

Local governments recording. The agreement of 12 December 2025 covers the municipal revenue of Bangui, the capital, and names no other commune.

Not held. What the system agreed for Bangui will record, where it will be held and whether it is in use. No commune outside the capital is named, and no plan or finance is stated.

CIV.short: A ministry-built register system was in a 22-commune pilot of 201 in December 2025; whether any commune records in it is not known.
CIV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Directorate General of Decentralisation and Local Development (DGDDL) developed the SYGIDAN Recettes software in its own services and directs the PAMREC project. In April 2024 the project was financed by the African Development Bank and the Ivorian State, together 3,003,901,293 FCFA.

What is recorded. In April 2024 the DGDDL's director described SYGIDAN Recettes, then at pre-validation, as digitalising all of a commune's revenues, with traceability each time a tax is collected. The project's design of July 2021 registers taxpayers and records payments, balances, arrears and penalties.

Where the record is held. The tool is to centralise the data from all the actors collecting local revenue. The 2021 design was to connect it to the systems of the tax directorate, the Treasury, the DGDDL or the Court of Auditors.

Last twelve months. On 9 December 2025 the DGDDL handed the commune of Assinie-Mafia its taxpayer database, within the PAMREC pilot.

Local governments recording. The African Development Bank's appraisal of July 2021 places the pilot in 22 of 201 municipalities. In April 2024 the tool was to be deployed to the 22 communes and then distributed to all from January 2025.

Not held. No fact says the system is in use in any commune, and no count of communes recording is given. Whether the distribution to all communes announced for January 2025 took place.

CMR.short: A platform for traders to register and pay local tax was presented in 2023 for two councils; whether any council uses it is not known.
CMR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The AIMF, the association of French-speaking mayors, reports that FEICOM presented Inform'All City, a platform for collecting local tax from informal traders, on 21 March 2023.

What is recorded. On the platform, as presented in March 2023, informal traders register and pay their local tax, against a site the commune assigns them.

Where the record is held. The platform is built so that, with traders registered and paying on it, councils collect remotely.

Last twelve months. The platform, to be deployed first in two councils, was presented on 21 March 2023.

Local governments recording. In March 2023 the platform was to be deployed first in the councils of Yaoundé II and Douala III, in the political and economic capitals, with no wider count given.

Not held. Whether the platform was deployed in the two councils or in any other, and where its record is held. Nothing dated after March 2023 shows a commune keeping a digital revenue record.

COD.short: Tools to track revenue and register taxpayers were being assessed with 20 decentralised territorial entities in 2024; whether any uses one is not known.
COD.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The digital tools for the decentralised territorial entities are supported by USAID's Good Governance Activity, launched in July 2023, whose July 2024 workshop was co-hosted with COREF, the national public finance reform committee.

What is recorded. A workshop of 23–24 July 2024 was to standardise and assess tools for tracking revenue, registering taxpayers and budgeting.

Where the record is held. The tools under assessment in July 2024 were for the public financial management of the decentralised territorial entities themselves.

Last twelve months. The Good Governance Activity held its workshop on the tools on 23–24 July 2024.

Local governments recording. In July 2024 the activity worked with 20 decentralised territorial entities in four provinces: Haut Katanga, Lualaba, Tshopo and Haut Uele.

Not held. What the tools record, where the record is held and whether any entity uses one. The tier of the 20 entities, the tools' owner and any plan are not stated.

COG.short: A state platform for local governments' revenue was validated in February 2026; whether any local government yet records on it is not known.
COG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Plateforme de dématérialisation des recettes des collectivités locales (PDRCL) was given to the state's Agence congolaise des systèmes d'information (ACSI) by the 2025 finance law. ACSI's procurement notice of 4 September 2025 lists equipment for it from the agency's 2025 investment budget, with the Ministry of the Interior as client.

What is recorded. The finance ministry said in February 2026 that the platform has a back-office module for local government agents and a market-collector module, Zando collecte, that enrols taxpayers, records revenue by payment mode and tracks each taxpayer's operations.

Where the record is held. The ministry said on 14 February 2026 that the platform brings the revenues of local governments into one information system.

Last twelve months. The platform passed final validation at Kintélé on 14 February 2026 and ACSI presented it to the Mayor of Brazzaville on 30 April 2026.

Local governments recording. The platform was validated after workshops with the communes of Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire. On 24 February 2026 ACSI was preparing its deployment, and in 2026 a pilot was to follow at the Ndjindji central market in Pointe-Noire once municipal staff had been trained.

Not held. No local government is stated as recording on the platform, in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire or elsewhere. No plan naming the platform is held.

COM.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
COM.summary: Not held. No source on local government revenue records is held, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

CPV.short: Terms of reference for a municipal property tax module were issued in 2025; what municipalities record today is not known.
CPV.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The finance ministry's special projects unit issued terms of reference in 2025 for the Territory Management modules of SIMple, a planned successor to the municipal information system. The work is funded from a US$15 million World Bank credit for the Harmonization and Improvement of Statistics in West Africa Project.

What is recorded. The planned modules cover the cadastre, property assessment and property tax collection.

Where the record is held. The system the modules are to succeed, SIM 2.0, handles accounting, financial management and budget execution, the allocation of revenues and expenses.

Last twelve months. The terms of reference for the property tax modules were issued in 2025.

Local governments recording. The modules are planned for the municipalities, all of which run SIM 2.0.

Not held. What municipalities record of their revenue, where they hold it and how many of them record are not held. No source says the property tax modules are piloted or live.

DJI.short: In 2020 local authorities could not levy taxes and none collected its own; how records are kept is not known, so no stage is set.
DJI.summary: Not held. The one source held, on 2020 fiscal data, says local authorities are not empowered to levy taxes and that none of the nine collects its own; no source says how a local authority keeps any revenue record, and none names a system in preparation. Nothing held is dated since 2020.

DZA.short: A 2018 audit found most communes reviewed had no current tax-base census; how communes record revenue is not known, so no stage is set.
DZA.summary: Not held. No source says how communes keep their revenue records, and none names a revenue system in preparation or on pilot. The one fact held is an audit of 22 communes over 2014 to 2018, which found most had no updated census of their taxable base and does not speak for the country.

EGY.short: A central authority collects the real estate tax, a quarter for local government (2020); local records are not known, so no stage is set.
EGY.summary: Not held. Whether any governorate or local unit keeps its own digital revenue record. No source on local government revenue records is held.

ERI.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
ERI.summary: Not held. No source on local government revenue records is held, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

ETH.short: A property tax platform was built for three pilot cities in 2016 and never fully implemented; whether any city still uses it is not known.
ETH.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. An assessment of the Computerized Property Tax Administration (CPTA) platform is run with the Ministry of Urban and Infrastructure's Urban Revenue Reform Project Office and the Ministry of Finance's Tax Policy Department, with UNECA support, according to LoGRI's project page.

What is recorded. CPTA is a platform for administering property tax, developed in 2016.

Where the record is held. The platform was never fully implemented, LoGRI says.

Last twelve months. The Addis Ababa City Government Revenues Bureau began a property-tax reform pilot in July 2026, covering property identification and valuation, in a move from the land-rent and building-tax arrangement to a value-based property tax.

Local governments recording. CPTA was developed for three pilot cities in 2016, and a national scale-up is planned.

Not held. What the platform records and where the record is held are not held, nor whether any of the three pilot cities still uses it. No plan or finance for it is held, and nothing on it is dated within the last twelve months.

GAB.short: Libreville's mayor said in July 2026 the city runs its own digital revenue system; whether any other local government records is not known.
GAB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Libreville's pilot platform is developed by the company GTI Gabon for the city hall, and the mayor said on 3 July 2026 that the city's system was developed with the public Treasury. Digitax is the platform of the Direction générale des Impôts.

What is recorded. At its launch on 29 July 2025 the Libreville pilot platform was described as resting on a geolocated taxpayer file, online declaration and payment, automatic tax and penalty amounts and a dashboard showing who is up to date on which taxes.

Where the record is held. Under the Owendo agreement of 29 April 2026 the tax directorate will align the municipal agents' taxpayer directory with its own.

Last twelve months. The commune of Owendo signed an agreement with the tax directorate on 29 April 2026 to implement Digitax for municipal taxes. A consultancy presented the Colloc-Pay platform to the Ntoum commune and the Komo-Mondah departmental council on 19 June 2026.

Local governments recording. The mayor of Libreville said on 3 July 2026 that the city has its own operational system digitalising municipal revenue and securing collection. The city hall had launched a pilot of digitised revenue collection on 29 July 2025.

Not held. No local government outside Libreville is stated as recording, and where the record is held is not stated. Whether the system the mayor calls operational is the 2025 pilot is not held, and no plan or finance is stated.

GHA.short: Some assemblies record payers and bills in a shared national system, nine of 260 using it in 2019; how many do now is not known.
GHA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Office of the Head of the Local Government Service, a state body, runs the training on the revenue software it calls dLRev, under a programme the World Bank supports. GIZ funded the application in 2019. Korle Klottey Municipal Assembly's own system is a company's software as a service, as audited at 31 December 2024.

What is recorded. dLRev holds a register of businesses and properties with their owners, and manages the billing and collection of property rates and business operating permits, as described in 2019. Korle Klottey's system held a property database, payer accounts and bills at 31 December 2024.

Where the record is held. Since 2017 dLRev has been hosted on the national platform of the National IT Agency, with no standalone operation in a district.

Last twelve months. A training of 350 staff of 35 Municipal Assemblies on the software began in February 2026, and about 150 officers in six regions were trained in July 2026. Ga West Municipal Assembly introduced a digital revenue system in one zonal council, with data capture set for April 2026.

Local governments recording. Nine of Ghana's 260 assemblies, 3.5 per cent, used dLRev throughout 2019, by a paper GIZ commissioned. In February 2020 47 of GIZ's 90 partner districts had properties registered in it. The Ministry of Local Government reports that in 2021 it rolled the software out in 114 of the 260.

Not held. No figure for assemblies recording in dLRev is dated after February 2020: the 2021 figure is a roll-out and the 2026 figures are staff trained. No current plan for the software is held, and nothing on its hosting is dated after 2017.

GIN.short: A revenue tool was presented in March 2025 for a pilot in communes of Conakry, Coyah and Kindia; whether the pilot began is not known.
GIN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The president of Kindia's special delegation said on 25 March 2025 that financing for the tool remained to be found.

What is recorded. The tool presented on 25 March 2025 is one for digitalising the management of communes' revenue.

Where the record is held. The tool comes from Benin, where it was in use before its presentation in Guinea in March 2025.

Last twelve months. On 25 March 2025 the tool was presented at the Conakry governorate to the communes that are to receive it and to officials of the ministry of territorial administration and decentralisation, ahead of a pilot.

Local governments recording. The pilot presented in March 2025 is for Conakry's 13 urban communes, with Coyah and Kindia, which are to experiment with the tool.

Not held. Whether the pilot began, what the tool records and where its record is held. No owner or plan is named, and nothing is dated after March 2025.

GMB.short: One council outside the capital keeps a digital tax register, reported in 2024 and 2025; the share of councils recording is not known.
GMB.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The evaluation of the 2021–2025 public finance strategy says most of the funding for revenue reform comes from the councils, with support from donors. Kuntaur Area Council had a budget line for a pilot of digital collection in September 2025. A UN agency tendered in June 2026 for a property tax digital management system for Kanifing Municipal Council; the award is not held.

What is recorded. Basse Area Council implemented a digital tax register in 2024. Kanifing Municipal Council holds a property rates database, by its Rates Manager in June 2026. In Banjul market stalls were registered by QR code in three of five pilot zones by August 2022.

Where the record is held. Basse's system runs beside the government accounting system, with the link between the two pending in September 2025. Kanifing's database is the council's own.

Last twelve months. The evaluation, dated April 2026 and covering the period to 2025, reports the Digital Tax Collection System largely unimplemented in Banjul City Council, and its link to the accounting system incomplete in Kanifing and Janjanbureh.

Local governments recording. The ministry of finance's report of September 2025 names one council, Basse, as operating the system, and says Janjanbureh has none and Brikama no digital platform for collections.

Not held. The total of councils is not stated beside any count, so no share of councils recording is established. No plan for the system is held from the last three years.

GNB.short: Only national tax declaration and online payment systems are named (2022); local governments' revenue records are not known, so no stage is set.
GNB.summary: Not held. Whether any local government keeps a digital revenue record. Neither system held is stated as serving a local government.

GNQ.short: Only the finance ministry's national tax systems are named (2023 to 2026); municipalities' revenue records are not known, so no stage is set.
GNQ.summary: Not held. Whether any municipality keeps a digital revenue record. No municipal system is named.

KEN.short: Thirty-three of 47 counties had automated revenue collection by 2020, issuing electronic receipts; whether they hold a register of payers is not known.
KEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. On 7 February 2019 the President directed a task force to deliver one revenue management system for all 47 counties, and none had been delivered by September 2020. A 2018 policy brief says most counties that had automated did not own their system. Standards for county revenue automation, gazetted on 27 July 2026, say counties are to own their systems and revenue data. An October 2026 commentary puts about 70 per cent of counties on contracts that pay a vendor up to 15 per cent of collections, on the writer's own figures.

What is recorded. A 2020 paper describes automation as the move from paper receipts to an electronic system, with point-of-sale machines. In 2018, 97 per cent of the 34 counties with a system used only its collection module.

Where the record is held. A 2020 survey of 24 counties found that most could not host their revenue data, which the vendor hosted. In 2018, 14 of the 34 counties used one vendor's cloud service.

Last twelve months. The Vision 2030 Delivery Secretariat's review of all 47 counties, dated 23 February 2026, names five with well-established systems and cashless collection: Murang'a, Nairobi City, Machakos, Laikipia and Nyeri.

Local governments recording. Thirty-three of the 47 counties, 70 per cent, had automated their revenues, some of them in part, by a paper in the European Scientific Journal of September 2020. In February 2026 six of the 47 relied heavily on manual and cash-based systems, by the Secretariat's review.

Not held. No source says counties hold a register of payers, and no count of counties recording is dated after 2020. No source says any county has complied with the July 2026 standards.

LBR.short: A pilot revenue database was planned in June 2023 for two city corporations; whether it was built is not known.
LBR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. Terms of reference of June 2023 put a revenue advisor under the project unit of the Ministry of Public Works, and the work is financed by the World Bank under the Liberia Urban Resilience Project.

What is recorded. The June 2023 terms of reference plan a revenue collection database built on a map, and a digital payment system.

Where the record is held. The data collected is to be owned by the municipalities and the Republic of Liberia, by the terms of reference of June 2023.

Last twelve months. The terms of reference, of June 2023, set the pilot within an advisor's contract of 36 months.

Local governments recording. The pilot planned in June 2023 is for two city corporations, Monrovia and Paynesville.

Not held. Whether the pilot database was built, and whether any local government records on it. Nothing is dated after June 2023.

LBY.short: A 2024 ministry programme signed by 27 municipalities includes electronic collection; how many municipalities use its local revenue system is not known.
LBY.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Local Government of the Government of National Unity runs the National Programme for Activating Local Revenues. Its action plan for municipalities covers economic-activity revenue, electronic collection, revenue regulations and a forum.

What is recorded. The programme's projects include an electronic collection system and a database of municipal economic activities, as reported in June 2024.

Where the record is held. The local revenue system and the electronic collection project both sit under the ministry's national programme.

Last twelve months. On 10 June 2024, 27 municipalities signed a sponsorship document committing them to implement the programme.

Local governments recording. The programme director said in June 2024 that it targets both municipalities where the local revenue system is already activated and those where it still needs activating, and gave no count of either.

Not held. What the local revenue system records, where its record is held, and how many municipalities use it or which they are. The 27 signatories are not said to use it; 21 municipalities were given access and training in October 2025.

LSO.short: Nothing is held on local governments' revenue records, digital or paper, and no system is named, so no stage is set.
LSO.summary: Not held. No source on local government revenue records is held, and no system of any class is named. Nothing is shown either way, including absence.

MAR.short: Communes issue local tax bills in a national system, in more than 100 large municipalities in August 2025; the share recording is not known.
MAR.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. GIR-CT, the integrated revenue management system for local authorities, is run by the Interior Ministry's directorate for local authorities with the national treasury, as reported on 29 May 2025. The minister's circular of 19 May 2020 told authorising officers to equip their revenue offices and work with the treasury on extending it.

What is recorded. Communal tax officials issue the annual bills for local taxes in GIR-CT, and the treasury's accountants take the payments, as reported on 29 May 2025.

Where the record is held. The World Bank's status report on its mission of August 2025 has GIR-CT operating at national level, interfaced with local systems. In May 2025 the ministry told local authorities to upload their revenue orders in GIR-CT alone and to drop software they had bought or built. The treasury collects all municipal revenues except the professional tax, the World Bank said in November 2021.

Last twelve months. On 29 May 2025 taxpayers were being urged to declare and pay local taxes through the online platform set up with the treasury.

Local governments recording. The World Bank's status report of August 2025 puts GIR-CT in place in more than 100 large municipalities and gives no total of municipalities. The Interior Ministry's circular had it deployed in 969 of 1,590 local authorities on 19 May 2020.

Not held. How many local authorities record in GIR-CT, as a share: the newest count has no total and the only figure with one is a deployment figure of 2020. No plan or finance for the system, and nothing dated in the twelve months to September 2026.

MDG.short: One commune outside the capital was handed property-tax software in 2021; whether it or any other commune records payers digitally since is not known.
MDG.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. In September 2021 UNDP, through its GBCI project with the Ministry of Economy and Finance, supported and developed the G-IFPB property-tax software and installed it.

What is recorded. UNDP states that G-IFPB, fed by a 2019 taxpayer census, was handed over on 13 September 2021 to manage collection of the built-property tax in Toamasina.

Where the record is held. The software was installed at the Commune Urbaine de Toamasina and at the Direction Régionale des Impôts Atsinanana, the regional tax office.

Last twelve months. UNDP reported the software's operational launch and official handover in Toamasina on 13 September 2021.

Local governments recording. In September 2021 only Toamasina commune used the software, and staff were trained to replicate the process in the city's other arrondissements.

Not held. Whether Toamasina went on to bill from the software after the handover, and whether any other commune was equipped. Nothing dated between September 2021 and 30 September 2026 shows a commune recording its payers or their payments in a system.

MLI.short: Communes tested tax registers in 2023 and Koutiala began a pilot in March 2026; whether any uses one as routine is not known.
MLI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. ReCoDe, the communes' software, was chosen by the national local finance committee and rolled out by the DGCT and the treasury, a Pro-ARIDES note of July 2024 says. The Koutiala project launched on 6 March 2026 is financed by the Embassy of the Netherlands and carried with the NGO ID Sahel Afrique.

What is recorded. ReCoDe's local tax module follows a census of taxable matter, with an electronic ticket coded for each taxpayer and a payment terminal that feeds the town hall's server; Bamako's Commune VI collected 250 million CFA francs with it in 2023. In a test at Koulikoro reported in June 2023, about 100 vendors were registered and each ticket was entered at once in the town hall's database.

Where the record is held. In July 2024 the data of the 13 Pro-ARIDES communes using ReCoDe were centralised on a server at the DGCT. Market fees were collected by hand, the agent writing each ticket, UNDP Mali said in June 2023.

Last twelve months. A project launched on 6 March 2026 is to give pilot communes a digital solution and equipment for financial management and the collection of communal taxes, starting with Koutiala.

Local governments recording. ReCoDe was deployed in 680 communes for testing, the July 2024 note says. After training in 27 of the programme's communes, only Kava was willing to carry tax digitalisation through.

Not held. Whether any commune outside Bamako uses the local tax module as routine, and how many of the 680 communes use it at all. No plan for the system is stated.

MOZ.short: Only Maputo's municipality is shown keeping a taxpayer register, on a 2020 assessment; whether any other municipality records its revenue digitally is not known.
MOZ.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. CEDSIF, the state's information systems centre, specifies e-SGA, a single integrated municipal management system of 22 modules, with ANAMM named as client, on a page published on 8 August 2026.

What is recorded. A September 2020 assessment for the Ministry of Economy and Finance describes SISPGIA, the Maputo municipality's property tax system, built in 2009, with modules for a taxpayer register, taxpayer queries and the payment of taxes and fees.

Where the record is held. The e-SGA specification includes modules for municipal revenue management, markets and street trading, and commercial rents.

Last twelve months. CEDSIF's page setting out the e-SGA modules was published on 8 August 2026.

Local governments recording. The September 2020 assessment describes a property tax system in one municipality, Maputo.

Not held. Where the record is held, how many municipalities record, and whether e-SGA is in use anywhere. No plan or finance is stated, and no dated event falls in the twelve months to September 2026.

MRT.short: One commune, Sebkha, kept a digital register of taxpayers in 2020 and eight were installing it; how many communes record now is not known.
MRT.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. El Mouhassil was tested and provided to communes by the Interior Ministry's directorate for local authorities, with support from Germany, France and the World Bank, the directorate's report of November 2022 says.

What is recorded. In Sebkha a seven-week census found 10,564 taxpayers against the 2,000 officially recognised, as reported in April 2020. The software, launched there in April 2019, issues numbered, barcoded fiscal stamps and tracks each from stock to sale to payment into the commune's Treasury account; agents with tablets scan a trader's stamp to see whether it is paid or overdue.

Where the record is held. Sebkha's mayor describes the system as completely independent and run by the commune with its own stamps, as reported in April 2020.

Last twelve months. On 11 July 2023 the commune of Rosso held a training session on integrating civil-status records into its El Mouhassil programme.

Local governments recording. In April 2020 El Mouhassil was live in one commune, Sebkha in Nouakchott, and being installed in eight others. On 23 May 2023 the commune of Zouerate launched its own digitised tax collection programme, built on a census of the town's commercial activities.

Not held. Whether any commune other than Sebkha records in El Mouhassil, and how many communes use it. Nothing is dated after July 2023.

MUS.short: Permit and document systems run in local authorities (2024); whether any council keeps a digital revenue record is not known, so no stage is set.
MUS.summary: Not held. Whether any council keeps a digital revenue register or receipt record. Nothing held says the national tax portal collects any council revenue.

MWI.short: Five of 35 local governments recorded revenue digitally by 2025, three with registers of payers; the cities' position since 2022 is not known.
MWI.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. In 2022 the four city councils' systems were supplied by vendors under revenue-share contracts, Blantyre's and Mzuzu's by Technobrain and Lilongwe's and Zomba's by Nitel. Mwanza District Council adopted its system with the support of the United Nations Development Programme, as stated in February 2025. In August 2024 Lilongwe City Council said the United States had agreed US$24 million in grant funding for property records and billing in four cities.

What is recorded. In 2022 the systems in Blantyre, Lilongwe and Mzuzu held property and business owners with their payments and liabilities in one database per city, used to produce demand notices and business licences. Zomba's covered market rates, bus depots and parking only in March 2022. In February 2025 Mwanza issued electronic tickets for market fees, vehicle parking and border entry fees.

Where the record is held. In 2022 each of the four city councils ran its own cloud-hosted system from a different vendor, none of them integrated with the treasury's system, banks or mobile money. Mwanza's is built and run by the council's own systems analyst, as stated in February 2025.

Last twelve months. In February 2025 Mwanza District Council was using every component of the system it calls LORMIS.

Local governments recording. Revenue management systems had been introduced in all four city councils since 2017, of 35 local governments, the International Growth Centre's study found in 2022. The United Nations Development Programme named one district council, Mwanza, in February 2025.

Not held. No figure for the four cities after 2022, and no system named in the other 30 local governments. No current plan naming the systems, and no event in the last twelve months.

NAM.short: The capital city billed water accounts to named customers in its own system in 2024; whether any other local authority records revenue is not known.
NAM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The City of Windhoek's billing system is its own, with the vendor BCX supplying the financial management software, The Namibian reported for February 2024.

What is recorded. The City of Windhoek bills water accounts for named customers in the system it calls Solar, with payments and arrears recorded against each account. A city memo of February 2024 found accounts imported from the financial system with wrong customer information, and a payment history missing from one account.

Where the record is held. In February 2024 the billing system ran on the city's own servers.

Last twelve months. On 2 July 2024 the City of Windhoek confirmed irregularities in its water billing system, with forensic investigators appointed and nine accounts found with wrong figures. The system keeps its logs for 30 days.

Local governments recording. The Namibian's report of July 2024 covers the City of Windhoek's billing system, the capital's, and names no other local authority.

Not held. Any local authority outside Windhoek, a total of those recording, and any of the city's accounts other than water. Nothing on who plans or pays for the systems, and no event in the last twelve months.

NER.short: The capital registers its taxpayers digitally and one commune outside it began in December 2025; how many communes record is not known.
NER.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The City of Niamey launched the platform it calls Naneye Yarda under its 2025-2027 strategic plan, with the national information society agency building the architecture, Le Sahel reported in January 2025. The city's delegated administrator called it the main pillar of that plan at the launch on 3 October 2024.

What is recorded. In Diffa the system covers a digital census of taxable establishments by agents with tablets, automatic tax calculation, tax notices with QR codes and payment by electronic terminals, from 11 December 2025. In Niamey 50 field agents with mobile devices had geolocated over 2,000 taxpayers by January 2025.

Where the record is held. In Niamey municipal tax payments through Al Izza and Nita were integrated with real-time revenue tracking and an automated audit of each transaction, the city's administrator said in January 2025.

Last twelve months. The commune urbaine of Diffa put the system into service on 11 December 2025, replacing manual collection with incomplete taxpayer files.

Local governments recording. The platform launched in the City of Niamey in January 2025. The United Nations Development Programme named Diffa in December 2025 as the first outside the capital to deploy it in full. On 21 August 2025 Niamey received 100 electronic payment terminals.

Not held. Where the record is held, in Niamey or in Diffa, and who pays for the system. No count of communes recording, no report of use in Diffa since it was put into service, and no statement that Niamey's 100 terminals are in use.

NGA.short: Two local government areas in one state registered payers digitally from 2017; how many record across the country is not known.
NGA.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. In March 2017 the Edo State government, with the local councils, introduced an automated revenue collection system under the Edo Jobs Initiative.

What is recorded. A journal article of November 2018 describes an app in which local government revenue agents register payers, businesses and vehicles and collect and print receipts. Before it, the authors say, revenue from drivers, traders and others was collected on manual receipts, with no data of collection.

Where the record is held. The agents' entries go onto a taxpayers' database.

Last twelve months. The system in the two local government areas of Edo State was introduced in March 2017.

Local governments recording. The authors say two of Edo State's local government areas, Oredo and Egor, use the system, as at November 2018.

Not held. Whether the two local government areas still use the system, and how many local government areas across the country keep a digital revenue record. Nothing on a local government area's own record is dated after 2018.

RWA.short: The national revenue authority collects for the districts and keeps their tax register (2024); districts' own records are not known, so no stage is set.
RWA.summary: Not held. Whether any district keeps a revenue record of its own. What is held is the national revenue authority's record, kept on the districts' behalf.

SDN.short: One locality began electronic collection as a model site in May 2026; whether it keeps a register of payers is not known.
SDN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. In Sennar State, Isali electronic collection is run by the state finance ministry's unified collection department, as reported in May 2026.

What is recorded. The Sennar state finance ministry launched Isali electronic collection on 12 May 2026 at the transport and petroleum department and Sinja locality, with collectors, auditors and accountants equipped and trained.

Where the record is held. The state's governor described Isali as a national programme covering all Sudanese states.

Last twelve months. The launch of 12 May 2026 followed preparation from January 2026, in stages of networking, account opening and training.

Local governments recording. Sinja locality was one of two model sites in Sennar State at the launch. The state's finance director general said all state institutions would be covered at the start of the second half of 2026.

Not held. Whether collection in Sinja ran past its model stage, whether a register of payers is kept and where the record is held. No other locality is named as collecting electronically.

SEN.short: More than 20 communes were equipped with a vendor's municipal software by November 2025; whether any records its revenue in it is not known.
SEN.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The municipal software named in Senegal's communes is a product of the vendor Linking Development, supplied to communes, on the vendor's own account in November 2025.

What is recorded. The vendor says the software, which it calls Terlink, includes accounting and taxation modules covering the recovery and management of communal taxes. Its other modules are for civil status and for planning and land.

Where the record is held. Linking Development describes Terlink as all-in-one municipal management software, supplied together with a website for the commune.

Last twelve months. In November 2025 the vendor published its account of the software and of the communes it had equipped with it.

Local governments recording. Linking Development, the vendor, states that more than 20 communes in Senegal are equipped with Terlink, as at November 2025.

Not held. Whether any commune uses the software it was equipped with, what the software records of payers, and where the record is held. No total of communes beside the count, no plan or finance, and no event in the last twelve months.

SLE.short: Three of 22 local councils had a property tax system by December 2025, with billing shown only in the capital; use elsewhere is not known.
SLE.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. The Ministry of Finance runs the rollout through its Fiscal Decentralization Division, with the Ministry of Local Government, as at May 2026, under a 2025-2029 strategy for property tax roll-out pilots and scaling-up plans. The rollout is financed by a US$50 million IDA grant and US$6.73 million of GEF co-financing under the Resilient Urban Sierra Leone Project.

What is recorded. The Municipal Property Tax System covers a georeferenced property roll, valuation, billing, demand notices and payment reconciliation, the ministry said on 20 May 2026. Freetown City Council's database held more than 160,000 properties and billed each a Rate Demand Notice in 2020.

Where the record is held. The ministry's notice of 20 May 2026 says the system, which it calls MOPTAX 2.0, is integrated with the Central Government Monitoring and Reporting System.

Last twelve months. Freetown City Council was upgraded to MOPTAX 2.0 in December 2025. On 20 May 2026 the ministry invited firms to roll the system out in Bo and Koidu New Sembehun City Councils over fifteen months.

Local governments recording. In December 2025 Freetown became the third local council, after Kenema and Makeni, to have the upgraded system, of 22, the Ministry of Finance says: 14 per cent of local councils given the system. Makeni's was deployed in April 2025, and the ministry called Kenema's a pilot in May 2026.

Not held. Whether Kenema or Makeni bills from the system each was given, and any council recording outside Freetown past a pilot. The ministry's 2025 progress report still expected in 2026 the integration that its May 2026 notice describes as made.

SOM.short: Four Puntland local governments kept a digital register of payers and payments in 2022; the share of all local governments is not known.
SOM.summary:
Governance, planning, finance. As of September 2023 the property tax work was run by the UN Joint Programme on Local Governance with state ministries of interior. In Puntland the system was implemented through the Ministry of Interior with the telecom firm Golis, on programme support, in August 2021.

What is recorded. In Garowe, Qardho and Galkacyo properties were mapped and registered in the local government financial system, which generates the tax invoices and receipts payments made through mobile money, on fieldwork of October 2022. The system, which the local governments call FMIS, replaced printed receipts and books, from 2019 in Garowe and from 2021 in three others.

Where the record is held. In June 2021 the programme described the Puntland districts' system as moving to a coherent financial system from district to state level, deployed through the state Ministries of Interior and Finance.

Last twelve months. The latest dated event is in the period to September 2023, when three of five targeted Puntland districts had completed the demonstration phase of a mobile-payment tax collection system.
