Not held. No source held says a statistics law is in force. No source held says the proclamation was issued, or withdrawn, after 2007.

ETH.short: Ethiopia's 2005 statistics proclamation is in force; parliament approved its successor in June 2026, and whether that is published is not known.
ETH.summary:
Law in force. Ethiopia's statistics law is the Central Statistics Authority Establishment Proclamation No. 442/2005, published in the Federal Negarit Gazeta on 20 April 2005. Its successor has passed parliament: the Council of Ministers took up a draft statistics proclamation on 26 May 2026, and the House of People's Representatives approved the Ethiopian Statistical Service Proclamation unanimously on 30 June 2026.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the vote of June 2026. The House approved the new proclamation at its 29th regular session on 30 June 2026; the draft the Council of Ministers considered covers the Statistical Service's independence, its oversight and the confidentiality of data. The report of the vote does not say the proclamation has been published in the gazette, so the 2005 proclamation is the law in force.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. No source held says the 2026 proclamation has been published in the gazette.

GAB.short: Gabon's statistics law, amended in 2022, is in force; an August 2024 decree under it approved the statistics institute's statutes.
GAB.summary:
Law in force. Gabon's statistics law is law 15/2014 instituting and organising the national statistical system, amended by law 16/2022 of 6 September 2022. The state news agency reported in May 2026 that it is the legislation in force, and the economy ministry says the Head of State promulgated it. An amendment is in progress: on 22 May 2026 the planning minister presented to the Council of Ministers a bill amending ten articles of the law to bring it into line with the Constitution of December 2024.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. A rule was made under the law in 2024. Decree 0314/PR/MPP of 1 August 2024 approves the statutes of the National Institute of Statistics and cites the statistics law, as amended in 2022, as the basis it is taken under. It was published in the Journal Officiel of 15 August 2024.

Not held. No source held shows the statistics council meeting under the law.

GHA.short: Ghana's 2019 Statistical Service Act is in force; a replacement bill went to consultation in July 2026, and rules under the Act are not known.
GHA.summary:
Law in force. Ghana's statistics law is the Statistical Service Act, 2019 (Act 1003), assented to on 24 September 2019 and commenced on 27 September 2019. The Ghana Statistical Service publishes the Act's operative text as its governing law. A replacement is being prepared: in July 2026 the Service held a stakeholder engagement on a proposed Statistics Ghana Bill, 2026 with ministries, development partners, civil society and academia.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the engagement on the bill. The Service announced the consultation on the Statistics Ghana Bill in July 2026, which would replace the 2019 Act seven years after it commenced. The bill is at the stage of consultation by the Service, and the 2019 Act is the law in force.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GIN.short: Guinea's 2014 statistics law is in force with decrees and a council appointed under it in 2015; nothing done under it since is known.
GIN.summary:
Law in force. Guinea's statistics law is Law L/2014/019/AN of 8 July 2014 on the organisation and regulation of statistical activities, which repealed the law of 1995. The statistics institute publishes it in a compendium with the texts that apply it.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. Rules were made under the law in 2015 and its council was appointed. The compendium reproduces the decree of 5 August 2015 on the attributions, organisation and operation of the national statistics council. It also carries a 2015 decree on managing the financial resources of the national statistical programme, and ministerial orders on the specialised commissions and on the duty of administrations to send data to the statistical system. After the decree, an order of the Prime Minister named the council's members, with the Prime Minister as its president. All of it dates from 2015.

Not held. No source held dates an act done under the law in the last three years.

GMB.short: The Gambia's 2005 Statistics Act is in force and a 2019 replacement bill has not passed; rules under the Act are not known.
GMB.summary:
Law in force. The Gambia's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2005. The statistics bureau's strategy published in September 2023 says the Act governs statistical activities, provides for the national statistical system and establishes the bureau as its supervisory authority. A revision has been pending for years: the same strategy says the Act is under revision, and plans a review of the 2019 Statistics Bill and a new statistics law by 2026.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the strategy's plan for the bill. The strategy of September 2023 commits the bureau to review the Statistics Bill of 2019 and to press for its enactment. The bill was four years old when the strategy was written. No other document held on the country's statistics reports the bill tabled or passed.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

GNB.short: Guinea-Bissau's 2007 statistics law is in force and was given a regulation in March 2023; nothing done under it since is known.
GNB.summary:
Law in force. Guinea-Bissau's statistics law is Lei n.º 6/2007 of 10 September 2007, the framework law of the National Statistical System, made by the National People's Assembly. It sets up the national statistical system with its higher statistics council and the national statistics institute.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. A rule has been made under the law. The statistics institute's compilation of the law also carries Decreto n.º 4/2023 of 31 March 2023, the regulation of the 2007 statistics law. The regulation came sixteen years after the law. It is known by its title in the compilation: the text held breaks off before it, so what it regulates is not held. It is dated six months before the three years that end on 30 September 2026, and nothing later is held.

Not held. No source held dates an act done under the law in the last three years. The text of the 2023 regulation is not held.

GNQ.short: Equatorial Guinea's 2020 statistics law is in force, replacing one of 2001; rules made under it are not known.
GNQ.summary:
Law in force. Equatorial Guinea's statistics law is Law 3/2020 of 16 October 2020 regulating statistical activity. The national statistics strategy for 2022 to 2026 says statistical activity in the country is governed by that law, which replaced Law 3/2001 of 17 May 2001 and was aligned with the African Charter on Statistics.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the strategy's account. The strategy says the government amended the 2001 law to meet the new needs of the statistical system, and names the national statistics council, the statistical programmes committee and the statistics institute as the system's parts under the 2020 law. No other document held on the country's statistics ties a meeting or a decree to the statistics law.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. The law's own text is not held.

KEN.short: Kenya's 2006 Statistics Act is in force; a bill to replace the bureau with an authority was published in April 2026; rules are not known.
KEN.summary:
Law in force. Kenya's statistics law is the Statistics Act (Cap. 112), assented to on 23 August 2006 and commenced on 1 February 2007, which establishes the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics. A replacement has been published: in April 2026 the Bureau and the National Treasury published the Statistics Bill, 2026, which would establish a Kenya Statistics Authority in place of the Bureau and repeal the Act.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the bill. The Statistics Bill, 2026 runs to 38 pages and is a bill, not an enacted law. The Act it would repeal is held in the consolidated revision to 31 December 2022, which lists two orders for a population census as the subsidiary legislation made under it, the later in 2018. Orders for one census are noted here and not counted as rules that put the law to work.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LBR.short: Liberia's 2004 statistics act is in force and is cited in 2024 surveys; rules made under it are not known.
LBR.summary:
Law in force. Liberia's statistics law is the National Statistics and Geo-Information Act, approved on 22 July 2004, which adds a chapter to the Executive Law and establishes the statistics institute as an autonomous agency. The institute relies on it for confidentiality: its catalogue entries for the 2024 agricultural survey and the 2024 women's empowerment and nutrition survey say respondents' confidentiality is guaranteed by the Act.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held facts are those two survey entries. The institute's entry for the 2024 Annual Agricultural Survey says the Act of 2004 guarantees the confidentiality of respondents, and the entry for the nutrition survey of the same year says the same. They show the Act cited to respondents twenty years after it was approved. A survey carried out is not counted as the law applied, and the entries name no regulation.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LBY.short: Libya's 1963 statistics and census law is listed as in force; rules made under it are not known.
LBY.summary:
Law in force. Libya's statistics law is Law No. 16 of 1963 on statistics and censuses, issued by King Idris I on 19 September 1963. The Law Society's database of legislation lists it as in force.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is that listing. The database carries the text of the 1963 law and marks it as in force. It is the one source held for Libya on the subject. The law predates every later constitution and government of the country and is sixty-three years old, the second oldest statistics law in force among the countries assessed. The law therefore stands as the database gives it. Its title covers both the regular statistics of the state and the taking of censuses.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

LSO.short: Lesotho's 2001 statistics act is in force; a fourth replacement bill is expected to pass in 2026, and rules under the Act are not known.
LSO.summary:
Law in force. Lesotho's statistics law is the Bureau of Statistics Act, No. 8 of 2001. The African Union's peer review says the Act established the Bureau, the national statistical system and the National Statistical Council, and needs modernising, and in September 2026 a newspaper reported that the Bureau is mandated under it to conduct censuses and compile official statistics. A replacement is being drafted: the reviewers were told in August 2025 that the Office of Parliamentary Counsel was drafting a fourth Statistics Bill.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the bill's progress. In June 2026 the Bureau's director told a media workshop that the Statistics Bill is expected to be enacted before the end of 2026. The Bureau lists the 2001 Act first among its current documents.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MAR.short: Morocco's 1968 decree-law on statistics is in force; parliament adopted its replacement in July 2026, and whether that is promulgated is not known.
MAR.summary:
Law in force. Morocco's statistics law in force is Royal Decree-Law no. 370-67 of 5 August 1968 on statistical studies, in force from 15 August 1968. Its replacement has passed parliament: the Council of Government approved draft law 046.26 on the national statistical system on 2 July 2026, and the Chamber of Councillors adopted it unanimously on 13 July 2026.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the vote. The bill, presented by the Interior Minister, was adopted by the Chamber of Councillors on Monday 13 July 2026. It sets a new legal frame for the statistical system in place of the 1968 text. The reports of the vote do not say the law has been promulgated, so the decree-law of 1968 is counted as the law in force at the end of September 2026.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. No source held says law 046.26 has been promulgated.

MDG.short: Madagascar's 2018 statistics law is in force; rules made under it are not known.
MDG.summary:
Law in force. Madagascar's statistics law is Loi n° 2018-004 of 18 April 2018 on the organisation and regulation of statistical activities, adopted by the Senate on 2 March 2018 and by the National Assembly on 12 March 2018. The statistics institute names the law as an institutional result achieved, on its page for the statistics development strategy for 2023 to 2030.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the institute's account of the law. Its strategy page lists the law of 18 April 2018 among the results already secured and plans the period to 2030 on that footing. The strategy is a plan and is not a rule made under the law. No other document held on the country's statistics names a decree applying the law.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MLI.short: Mali's 2016 statistics law is in force with decrees of 2016 and a council appointed in 2018; nothing done under it since is known.
MLI.summary:
Law in force. Mali's statistics law is Loi n°2016-005 of 24 February 2016 governing public statistics, published in the Official Gazette of 18 March 2016. The statistics master plan says the law gave the national statistical system a legal frame in line with the African Charter on Statistics. A methods manual of December 2025 cites its first article as the ground of statistical quality.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. Rules were made under the law and its council was appointed. The master plan says the implementing decrees of the statistics law were taken in 2016. It adds that the order appointing the members of the National Statistics Council, the coordinating body the law sets up, was taken only in 2018, which delayed putting the body in place. Nothing made or done under the law in the last three years is held.

Not held. No source held dates an act done under the law in the last three years.

MOZ.short: Mozambique's 1996 law creating the national statistical system is in force; rules made under it are not known.
MOZ.summary:
Law in force. Mozambique's statistics law is Lei n.º 7/96 of 5 July 1996, by which the Assembly of the Republic created the National Statistical System.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the law's own text. The text held is an excerpt of the opening chapters of the 1996 law, which set up the system and its bodies. It is the one source held for Mozambique that states a fact on the statistics law. The law is thirty years old. No other document held on the country's statistics states a fact on the statistics law. No decree, regulation or order made under the 1996 law is named in what is held, and no bill to amend or replace it.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MRT.short: Mauritania's 2005 statistics law is in force with a council decree of 2006 and members named in 2008; nothing done under it since is known.
MRT.summary:
Law in force. Mauritania's statistics law is law no. 2005-017 of 27 January 2005 on public statistics. The national statistics strategy for 2021 to 2030 lists it as the main text governing public statistical activity, and says it had not been revised.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. Rules were made under the law and its council was appointed. The strategy records that decree no. 2006-024 of 17 April 2006 sets the organisation and operating rules of the National Statistical Council, created in application of the statistics law, and that order no. 1012/MEF/08 of 30 March 2008 appointed the council's members. Both acts date from the three years after the law was made. No other document held on the country's statistics names anything made or done under the law since 2008.

Not held. No source held dates an act done under the law in the last three years. The law's own text is not held.

MUS.short: Mauritius's Statistics Act of 2000 is in force and was amended in 2025 and August 2026; rules made under it are not known.
MUS.summary:
Law in force. Mauritius's statistics law is the Statistics Act (Act 38 of 2000), which commenced on 2 April 2001 and makes Statistics Mauritius the central statistical authority. It has been amended twice lately: the IMF's data review of September 2025 says most recommended amendments were made through the Finance Act 2025, and Act No. 14 of 2026, assented to on 12 August 2026, amends it again, adding public sector debt to the statistics it covers.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the 2026 budget. The Budget Annex for 2026-2027 refers to the governance, quality and confidentiality safeguards provided under the Statistics Act and says the Act will be amended; the amendment followed in August. An amendment changes the law and is not a rule made under it.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

MWI.short: Malawi's National Statistics Act has been in force since 2013; rules made under it are not known.
MWI.summary:
Law in force. Malawi's statistics law is the National Statistics Act (Chapter 27:01), which commenced on 19 July 2013. It establishes the National Statistical Office and the National Statistical System.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the Act's own text. The text held gives the commencement date of 19 July 2013 and the two bodies the Act sets up; the capture stops partway through, so no later section is held. It is the one source held for Malawi that states a fact on the statistics law. No other document held on the country's statistics states a fact on the Statistics Act. No decree, regulation or order made under the Statistics Act is named in what is held.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

NAM.short: Namibia's 2011 Statistics Act is in force and a policy was made under it in 2015; nothing done under it since 2023 is known.
NAM.summary:
Law in force. Namibia's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2011 (Act No. 9 of 2011), signed by the President on 2 August 2011 and promulgated on 18 August 2011. The statistics agency says the Act provides for the national statistics system and establishes the agency and its Board, and its census release of October 2024 says results are reported under the Act, which restricts publishing confidential information.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is from 2015. Under the Act the agency and the lands ministry were charged to develop the national spatial data policy, signed on 24 February 2015; the policy describes the Act as the law that establishes the spatial data infrastructure. That falls outside the last three years. The agency's data collection policy of March 2014 was written to comply with the Act.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

NER.short: Niger's 2004 statistics law is in force; cabinet adopted a replacement draft ordonnance in January 2026, and whether it is signed is not known.
NER.summary:
Law in force. Niger's statistics law is Loi n° 2004-011 of 30 March 2004 on the organisation of statistical activity, which creates the National Institute of Statistics and the national statistical system. A replacement is close: in October 2025 a statisticians' union said a committee of the institute had drafted an ordonnance on the principles of statistical activity and sent it to the government's secretariat.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the cabinet's decision. The Council of Ministers of 23 January 2026 adopted a draft ordonnance on the fundamental principles of statistical activities, instituting a National Statistical System and a national fund for statistical activity. The communiqué does not say the ordonnance was signed and published, so the law of 2004 is counted as the one in force.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. No source held says the 2026 ordonnance has been signed.

NGA.short: Nigeria's 2007 Statistics Act is in force; a replacement bill passed the House in December 2025, and rules under the Act are not known.
NGA.summary:
Law in force. Nigeria's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2007 (Act No. 9), published in the Official Gazette of 11 June 2007, which establishes the National Statistical System and the National Bureau of Statistics. A bill to repeal it is before parliament: the House of Representatives passed the Statistics Bill, 2025 at third reading on 10 December 2025.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the hearing of June 2026. A House committee held a public hearing on the Statistics Bill, 2025 on 8 June 2026, and the report describes the 2007 Act as the current law, eighteen years old, in place until the bill repeals it. The legislative reform office likewise refers to the existing Act of 2007 as the one the bill would repeal.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

RWA.short: Rwanda's 2013 law on statistical activities is in force; rules made under it are not known.
RWA.summary:
Law in force. Rwanda's statistics law is Law N° 45/2013 of 16 June 2013 on the organisation of statistical activities in Rwanda.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the law's own text. The text held is the law as made on 16 June 2013, published by the national statistics institute. It is the one source held for Rwanda on the subject. The law is thirteen years old and governs how statistical activities are organised in the country. No other document held on the country's statistics states a fact on the statistics law. No decree, regulation or order made under the statistics law is named in what is held, and no bill to amend or replace it. The law therefore stands as the institute publishes it.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SDN.short: Sudan's 2003 Statistics Act was in force and judged outdated in 2021; rules made under it are not known.
SDN.summary:
Law in force. Sudan's statistics law is the Statistics Act of 2003. An assessment by UN Women and the Central Bureau of Statistics, published in December 2021, treats the Act as the current statistics law, calls it outdated and notes it is silent on gender statistics. The statistics strategy of 2012 had already listed an inadequate Statistics Act, and some of its provisions not being implemented, among the system's weaknesses.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the 2021 assessment. The assessment rests on fieldwork from March to July 2021 and finds the 2003 Act still the governing text. It is the latest source held for Sudan on the subject and is nearly five years old. Neither source names a regulation made under the Act, and the 2012 strategy says parts of the Act were not being carried out.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. The Act's own text is not held, and nothing on it after 2021.

SEN.short: Senegal's 2004 statistics law, amended in 2012, is in force with rules on survey visas made in 2020; nothing done under it since is known.
SEN.summary:
Law in force. Senegal's statistics law is law no. 2004-21 of 21 July 2004 on the organisation of statistical activities, modified and completed by law no. 2012-03 of 3 January 2012. In September 2026 a report on the IMF's data review said Senegal has a statistical law, which the authorities will revise to strengthen the statistics agency's coordinating role.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. Rules have been made under the law. A regional inventory of statistics laws lists decree n° 2248 of 23 May 2005, setting the organisation and operating rules of the national statistics council and the technical committee on statistical programmes. It also lists two orders of 4 March 2020 on the statistical visa for censuses and surveys, the first taken under the law as amended in 2012. The 2020 orders fall outside the last three years, and nothing later is held.

Not held. No source held dates an act done under the law in the last three years.

SLE.short: Sierra Leone's 2002 Statistics Act is in force and is cited in 2023 and 2024 surveys; rules made under it are not known.
SLE.summary:
Law in force. Sierra Leone's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2002, passed in Parliament on 12 September 2002 and published in the Gazette on 7 November 2002. It establishes Statistics Sierra Leone as a body corporate. The office relies on it for confidentiality: its catalogue entries for the annual agricultural surveys of 2024 and 2023 say respondents' confidentiality is guaranteed by the Act.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held facts are those survey entries. The entry for the 2024 Annual Agricultural Survey says the Statistics Act of 2002 guarantees the confidentiality of respondents, and the 2023 entry says the same. They show the Act cited to respondents more than twenty years after it passed. A survey carried out is not counted as the law applied, and the entries name no regulation made under the Act.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SOM.short: Somalia's 2020 National Statistics Law is in force, replacing one of 1970; rules made under it are not known.
SOM.summary:
Law in force. Somalia's statistics law is Law No. 24, the National Statistics Law of the Federal Republic of Somalia. The National Bureau of Statistics says the law's enactment mandated the Bureau's establishment and repealed Statistical Law No. 35 of 1970. The Bureau's page gives no date for the law; the record held dates it 24 February 2020.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the Bureau's own account. The Bureau presents Law No. 24 as the act that created it in place of the 1970 law. It is the one source held for Somalia that states a fact on the statistics law, and it comes from the body the law set up. No other document held on the country's statistics says anything of the law. No decree, regulation or order made under the law is named in what is held, and the text of the law is not among the documents held.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. The law's own text is not held.

SSD.short: South Sudan's National Bureau of Statistics Act of 2024 is in force; rules made under it are not known.
SSD.summary:
Law in force. South Sudan's statistics law is the National Bureau of Statistics Act, 2024. The Bureau's page of laws and policies lists the Act as the principal legislation establishing the Bureau and defining its mandate, functions and authority. In September 2025 a radio report said the Bureau's Director General raised the Act as one of two key documents in a briefing to the Vice President's office.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is that briefing. The report of 16 September 2025 names the National Bureau of Statistics Act 2024 among the documents the Bureau put before the Vice President's office, in a briefing on population data ahead of elections. Neither source gives the date the Act was made or signed, and neither names a regulation made under it. The Bureau's page is the fuller of the two.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law. The Act's own text and its date of signature are not held.

STP.short: São Tomé and Príncipe's 1998 statistics law is in force; rules made under it are not known.
STP.summary:
Law in force. São Tomé and Príncipe's statistics law is Lei n.º 5/98, the framework law of the National Statistical System, passed by the National Assembly on 12 August 1998 and promulgated on 31 August 1998. Its article 18 brings it into force at once.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the law's own text. The text held is published by the national statistics institute and gives the dates of passage and promulgation. It is the one source held for São Tomé and Príncipe on the subject. The law is twenty-eight years old and sets the bases of the national statistical system, which the institute leads. No decree, regulation or order made under the law is named in what is held, and no bill to amend or replace it.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SWZ.short: Eswatini's 1967 Statistics Act is in force; rules made under it are not known.
SWZ.summary:
Law in force. Eswatini's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 1967 (Act 14 of 1967), which commenced on 27 October 1967. The text held is consolidated at 1 December 1998 and is stated to be the latest version.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is that consolidated text. The legal database gives the 1967 Act as in force and unamended since the 1998 consolidation. It is the one source held for Eswatini that states a fact on the statistics law. The Act predates the country's independence in 1968 and is fifty-nine years old. No other document held on the country's statistics names a regulation made under the Act or a bill to replace it. The Act gives a power to make regulations; no regulation made with that power is held.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

SYC.short: Seychelles' 2010 statistics act is in force; a 2025 peer review urged adoption of a new bill, and rules under the Act are not known.
SYC.summary:
Law in force. Seychelles' statistics law is the National Bureau of Statistics Act, 2010 (Act No. 14 of 2010), assented to on 9 July 2010, which establishes the Bureau as the principal statistics agency. The Bureau says its legal framework was recast in July 2010, when the Act repealed and replaced the National Statistics Bureau Act 2005.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is a call for a new law. The African Union's peer review of Seychelles' statistical system, published on 17 October 2025, recommends accelerating adoption of the new Statistics Bill to modernise the legal framework. The review was held from 12 to 16 May 2025 and gives no date or stage for the bill. No other document held on the country's statistics names a regulation made under the 2010 Act.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

TCD.short: Chad's 2019 statistics law is in force with three decrees of July 2019 under it; nothing done under it since 2023 is known.
TCD.summary:
Law in force. Chad's statistics law is Loi N°026/PR/2019 on the organisation and regulation of statistical activities, dated June 2019, which makes the statistics institute the central body of the national statistical system. The institute's data archive requires users to comply with articles 4 to 10 of the law of 11 June 2019, and a government adviser listed the law among reforms strengthening statistics at a regional forum in 2024.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. Rules were made under the law in 2019. The institute's page of regulatory texts lists three decrees dated July 2019 on the attributions, organisation and operation of the National Statistics Council, of the institute and of the National Statistics Development Fund. They followed the law by a month. Nothing made or done under the law in the last three years is held.

Not held. No source held dates an act done under the law in the last three years.

TGO.short: Togo's 2011 statistics law is in force with decrees of 2012 and 2015, and its statistics council met in June 2026.
TGO.summary:
Law in force. Togo's statistics law is law no. 2011-014 of 3 June 2011 on the organisation of statistical activity. The statistics institute says the law sets the principles and institutional frame of the national statistical system and was promulgated on 3 June 2011; the statistics strategy says it creates the National Statistics Council and the institute.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. Rules have been made under the law and its council meets. The institute says the council was made operational by a decree of 7 November 2012 on its composition and functioning, and the strategy cites a decree of 24 February 2015 setting the institute's functions and organisation as an implementing text. The council held its 13th ordinary session on 30 June 2026 and adopted the national statistical activity reports for 2023 and 2024.

Not held. No source held shows a penalty under the law. The law's own text is not held.

TUN.short: Tunisia's 1999 statistics law is in force and the ministry is preparing a new bill; rules made under the law are not known.
TUN.summary:
Law in force. Tunisia's statistics law is Law no. 99-32 of 13 April 1999 on the national statistical system, adopted by the Chamber of Deputies and promulgated by the President of the Republic. A revision is planned: in June 2026 the acting president of the National Statistics Council said the ministry is preparing a new statistics bill as a full revision of the 1999 law.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is that statement. The council's acting president, speaking on 5 June 2026, described the bill as in preparation at the ministry. A law in preparation with no draft published is not counted as a draft, so the standing is that of the 1999 law alone. No other document held on the country's statistics names a decree or order made under the law.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

TZA.short: Tanzania's 2015 Statistics Act is in force and is cited in a 2025 survey; rules made under it are not known.
TZA.summary:
Law in force. Tanzania's statistics law is the Statistics Act, Chapter 351, originally Act No. 9 of 2015, which commenced on 2 November 2015. It continues the National Bureau of Statistics and sets up its Governing Board. It is held in the revised edition of 2023 as well as that of 2019. The Bureau's dissemination policy of September 2024 says the Bureau operates as an autonomous public institution in accordance with the Act.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is a 2025 survey. The Bureau's catalogue page for the 2025 Integrated Labour Force Survey says survey information is collected under the Statistics Act. A survey carried out is not counted as the law applied. The commencement notice of 2015 brought the Act into force and is not a rule under it.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

UGA.short: Uganda's 1998 statistics act is in force and its board chairman invoked it in August 2026; rules made under it are not known.
UGA.summary:
Law in force. Uganda's statistics law is the Uganda Bureau of Statistics Act (Chapter 310), which commenced on 11 June 1998. It establishes the Bureau and the national statistical system.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is a statement of August 2026. The chairman of the Bureau's Board told the Finance Minister that the Bureau was established under the Act of 1998 and continues to coordinate the National Statistical System under it, as the finance ministry reported on 7 August 2026. The statement shows the Act standing twenty-eight years after it commenced and names the Board the Act provides for. It does not date the Board's appointment or a meeting, and it names no regulation. No other document held on the country's statistics names a regulation made under the Act.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

ZAF.short: South Africa's 1999 Statistics Act is in force and its 2024 amendment took effect in October 2025; regulations under it are not known.
ZAF.summary:
Law in force. South Africa's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 1999 (Act 6 of 1999), published in the Government Gazette on 21 April 1999. It was amended by the Statistics Amendment Act, 2024, assented to on 10 December 2024 and gazetted on 20 December 2024. The Deputy Minister in The Presidency told a parliamentary committee that the amendment was proclaimed for implementation on 1 October 2025.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the roll-out of the amendment. A parliamentary committee report of 23 June 2026 records Statistics South Africa briefing it on the Act and lists rolling out the 2024 amendments as work in hand. The office also cites sections 17 and 18 of the 1999 Act as the guarantee of respondents' confidentiality. An amendment changes the law and is not a rule made under it.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.

ZMB.short: Zambia's 2018 Statistics Act is in force and the statistics agency issued the release calendar it requires in December 2025; regulations are not known.
ZMB.summary:
Law in force. Zambia's statistics law is the Statistics Act, 2018 (Act No. 13 of 2018), assented to on 23 December 2018. A ministerial foreword says it repealed the Census and Statistics Act of 1955 and the Agricultural Statistics Act of 1964 and reconstituted the Central Statistics Office as the Zambia Statistics Agency.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The Act has been applied in the last three years. The Agency issued the National Statistical Release Calendar for 2026 on 1 December 2025, which section 27(1) of the Act requires it to prepare, and the calendar names the Act as the law under which the Agency acts. The statistics strategy published in July 2023 says the Act's operation began with the appointment of the Board of Directors and the Statistician General and the setting up of a coordinating committee of fifteen ministries.

Not held. No source held names a regulation made under the Act.

ZWE.short: Zimbabwe's Census and Statistics Act has been in force since 2009; the statistics agency called it outdated in 2025; rules under it are not known.
ZWE.summary:
Law in force. Zimbabwe's statistics law is the Census and Statistics Act (Chapter 10:29), Act 1 of 2007, which commenced on 1 July 2009 and establishes the Zimbabwe National Statistics Agency. The agency says official statistics are carried out on the basis of the Act, which sets up the agency and its Board.

Rules made under the law and the law applied. The nearest held fact is the agency's own criticism of the law. In October 2025 the agency's spokesperson said the Act is regarded as outdated and does not support an effective national statistical system or the sharing of administrative data. No bill to replace it is named. No other document held on the country's statistics names a regulation made under the Act or dates an appointment or meeting of the Board.

Not held. No source held names a decree, regulation or order made under the law.
